author: xavierbach
body:
## Summary

Three things, bundled because they all need to land before App Store + Play Store submission and they all touch the same files:

1. **iOS + Android positioning** — site previously read as iPhone-only. Now reflects that Bucko ships on both stores at the same time.
2. **Bucko Pro pricing** — added the actual subscription model ($1.99/mo or $9.99/yr, 7-day free trial, free plan = 1 kid) in the FAQ and the new legal pages. Replaces the stale "No, pay once when it ships" answer.
3. **Legal pages** — new `/privacy/`, `/terms/`, `/support/` required by both stores.

This supersedes the closed #2 (which was rebased onto an older `main`; the Build 2 copy rewrite landed in between).

## Changes

### `index.html`
- New "iOS · Android" pill banner under the nav
- CTA section: "Bucko is coming to iPhone" → "Bucko is coming to iPhone *and* Android"
- CTA copy: now mentions TestFlight (iOS) + internal track (Google Play)
- FAQ rewrites:
  - **Is there a subscription?** — now reflects Bucko Pro ($1.99/mo, $9.99/yr, 7-day trial, free plan = 1 kid)
  - **Is it on Android?** — yes, both at once
  - **How many kids?** — free 1, Pro unlimited
  - **Lose my phone?** — iCloud (iOS) + Google Drive (Android) sync as a Pro perk (coming)
- Footer gets a `.footer-links` nav with Privacy / Terms / Support

### `styles.css`
- `.platform-strip` and friends — the iOS · Android banner
- `.cta-and` — highlighted "and" in the CTA heading
- `.footer-links` — small light-grey legal nav in the footer
- `.doc-page`, `.doc-head`, `.doc-body`, `.doc-callout`, `.doc-toc` — type system for the new legal pages, designed to match the existing brand (same Inter / Space Grotesk fonts, same green accents, same surface treatment)

### New pages

- **`privacy/index.html`** — full privacy policy with a dedicated **Bucko Pro subscriptions** section that explains the RevenueCat + Apple/Google data flows (anonymous app-user ID, transaction processing, technical metadata). Anchored TOC.
- **`terms/index.html`** — Terms of Use (EULA) including:
  - Apple Licensed Application clauses (third-party beneficiary, etc.)
  - **§3a** — full auto-renewing-subscription disclosure (prices, free trial, auto-renewal, cancellation, refunds, price changes, post-cancellation behaviour)
- **`support/index.html`** — FAQs + contact, with:
  - A `#data-deletion` anchor for the Play Console's data-deletion-URL field
  - A **Subscriptions** section (how to subscribe / cancel / restore / refund)

## Test plan

- [ ] Pull this branch, run `python3 -m http.server 8080` from the repo root, click through the nav and footer links
- [ ] Confirm the iOS · Android pill renders under the nav on desktop and mobile
- [ ] Confirm `/privacy/`, `/terms/`, `/support/` all load and look on-brand
- [ ] Confirm `/support/#data-deletion` deep-links correctly
- [ ] Merge → GitHub Pages auto-deploys → `getbucko.com/privacy` resolves

## Why now

Both Apple and Google require a public privacy policy URL before the app can be submitted. Apple also requires a Terms / EULA URL. Apple additionally requires the auto-renewing-subscription disclosure visible to the user before purchase — covered by both the Terms page and the legal copy inside the app's paywall. The submission runbook in the app repo (`SUBMISSION_GUIDE.md`) points at these URLs.

author: emilyspringerton
body:
### Motivation

- Improve observability of the online join path and early gameplay net flow so failures (missing WELCOME, missing snapshot sync, blocked input, stale/malformed usercmds) can be diagnosed without flooding logs.
- Make client UI wording truthful: indicate `CONNECT_SENT` instead of implying a full connection before `PACKET_WELCOME`.
- Keep logic/semantics unchanged; only add diagnostics and small, safe hardening (minor malformed checks and rate-limited warnings).

### Description

- Added compile-time flags (`NET_VERBOSE_LOG`, `NET_LOG_HANDSHAKE`, `NET_LOG_SNAPSHOT`, `NET_LOG_USERCMD`, `NET_LOG_TIMEOUT`) and tagged logging macros (`[NET_CLIENT]`, `[NET_SERVER]`, `[NET_WARN]`, `[NET_ERR]`, `[NET_SUMMARY]`) to `apps/lobby/src/main.c` and `apps/server/src/main.c` for unified diagnostics.
- Client (`apps/lobby/src/main.c`): instrumented `net_init()`/`net_connect()` with socket/DNS/send diagnostics and `CONNECT_SENT` semantics; added a `NetClientDiag` struct, rate-limited timeout checks (`WELCOME_TIMEOUT`, `SNAPSHOT_SYNC_TIMEOUT`), first-receive logs for `PACKET_WELCOME` and `PACKET_SNAPSHOT`, local snapshot-sync confirmation log (`LOCAL_SNAPSHOT_SYNC`), one-time `CONTROL_UNLOCKED` and `USERCMD_TX_FIRST` logs, once-per-second `USERCMD` and `SNAPSHOT` summaries, short/unknown packet warnings, and replaced the misleading "Connected to..." message.
- Server (`apps/server/src/main.c`): added `NetServerDiag` counters and helpers, startup logs (bind/port/mode/scene), slot lifecycle logs (`SLOT_ASSIGN`, `SLOT_REUSE`, `SLOT_FREE`, `SLOT_FULL`, `SLOT_TIMEOUT`), connect-path logs (`CONNECT_RX`, `CONNECT_ACCEPT`, `WELCOME_TX`), per-client first-snapshot transmit log (`SNAPSHOT_TX_FIRST`), per-client first-usercmd packet log (`USERCMD_RX_FIRST`), malformed usercmd detection and rate-limited stale-usercmd warnings, and once-per-second server net summary (`[NET_SUMMARY] SERVER ...`).
- Safety/fix: removed the earlier immediate `send_welcome()` from the raw slot-allocation path so welcome is sent only from the authoritative `PACKET_CONNECT` accept path to avoid duplicate/misleading welcomes.
- Rate-limiting helpers were added and used to avoid log floods (most repeated warnings are limited to once-per-second per category).

### Testing

- Built server-only binary successfully with: `gcc -O2 -Wall -D_REENTRANT -Ipackages/common -Ipackages/simulation -Ipackages/render -Ipackages/world apps/server/src/main.c packages/world/terrain.c -o /tmp/shank_server_test -lm` which compiled without errors.
- Ran the repository `make -j2`; lobby build failed in this environment due to missing SDL2 headers (expected in CI/dev machines), and server build is otherwise covered by the successful direct `gcc` compile above.
- Ran `git diff --check` and basic static checks; no whitespace/diff errors reported.

author: lawcontinue
body:
## Summary

Proposes a constitutional constraint layer as a community extension for AGT, responding to the discussion in #934.

### Problem

AGT's three-gate architecture has two gaps:
1. **Intent drift** — agents can produce individually compliant actions that collectively diverge from the original goal
2. **Policy-compliant harm** — actions pass all rules but violate operator intent in unanticipated scenarios

Both gaps share a structural cause: the governance layer evaluates point-in-time compliance, not goal alignment over time.

### Proposal

- **Critic-with-veto pattern**: a dedicated agent that can block/pause actions but never execute them
- **Goal re-evaluation at decision boundaries**: checks trajectory alignment at phase transitions, side-effect tool calls, and delegation points
- **Blast-radius tier escalation**: actions classified by downstream fanout (≥3 dependents → auto-escalate one tier)
- **Community extension model**: wired into GovernanceGate as a post-check hook, not baked into core

### Why community extension

1. Constitutional rules are domain-specific
2. Critic pattern has runtime cost (LLM inference at decision boundaries)
3. Separation of concerns — constitutional alignment is a different concern from policy enforcement

### Related

- Discussion: #934
- Reference ADR: #948 (liveness attestation, format template)

This is a design proposal. Feedback welcome on the architectural approach and whether the community-extension boundary is right.

author: superdav42
body:
## Summary

- `ConversationTrimmer::find_turn_boundaries()` was counting `FunctionResponse` `UserMessage` objects as turn boundaries, allowing the trimmer to cut between a `tool_use` and its matching `tool_result` in multi-tool workflows (e.g. 7 parallel image imports).
- This produced API 400: `tool_use ids were found without tool_result blocks immediately after` — also reproduced when continuing or restarting sessions after tool calls (GH#1025).

## Root Cause

`ConversationSerializer::append_tool_response()` splits multi-part tool responses into individual `UserMessage` objects for OpenAI compatibility. Each split message has `role=user` — so `find_turn_boundaries()` counted 7 image import results as 7 turns, hit the trim limit, and severed the `tool_use`/`tool_result` pair.

Separately, any interrupted agent job (timeout, error mid-cycle) could leave the session DB with orphaned `tool_use` blocks — blocks without their matching `tool_result`. On the next request (even a new chat session loading the same history), the Anthropic API returns 400.

## Changes

- **`ConversationTrimmer::find_turn_boundaries()`** — skips `UserMessage` objects containing `FunctionResponse` parts via new `is_tool_response_message()` helper. Only genuine user text messages count as turn boundaries.
- **`ConversationTrimmer::validate_tool_pairs()`** — new safety-net that removes orphaned `tool_use` messages (missing matching `tool_result`) from history post-trim.
- **`AgentLoop::run_loop()`** — calls `validate_tool_pairs()` before every `send_prompt()`, even when trimming is disabled, to catch history corruption from deserialization round-trips.
- **`SessionController::handle_process()`** — calls `validate_tool_pairs()` after loading session history from the DB and after deserializing inline history from the request body. Defense-in-depth at the `/run` entry point.
- **`RestController` (client-tool resume path)** — same defensive strip when reconstructing history from the paused state.
- **5 regression tests** covering parallel tool calls, orphaned cycles, partial responses, and the exact 7-image scenario that triggered the bug.

## Testing

PHPCS and PHPStan pass on all modified files. Regression tests added in `ConversationTrimmerTest`.

Resolves #1025

author: jasonleetucker-code
body:
## Summary

Closes PR #82's follow-up TODO. Before this PR, 3+ team trades fell back to raw linear totals (zero VA). Now each side in a multi-team trade earns an independent consolidation premium computed via V2 against the merged opposition (every other side's assets flattened).

## Design

For an N-team trade (N ≥ 2), each side's VA runs the V2 2-side formula with:
- `small` = that side's received pieces
- `large` = union of every OTHER side's received pieces

Reduces exactly to the existing 2-side behavior when N = 2. For N ≥ 3:
- Each side can earn its own VA for consolidation relative to what it gave up
- V2's `topGap` guard still fires — sides whose top asset is no better than the merged opposition earn 0, so only the stud-holder typically gets a non-trivial premium in balanced trades

**This is a structural extension, NOT a separately calibrated formula.** V2 was fit against 13 two-side KTC observations. Multi-team output is plausible and self-consistent but uncalibrated until we have KTC multi-team data.

## API

New exports in `frontend/lib/trade-logic.js`:

```js
computeMultiSideAdjustments(sides: object[][], valueMode, settings?): number[]
multiAdjustedSideTotals(sides: object[][], valueMode, settings?): {raw, adjustment, adjusted}[]
```

The 2-side math is now factored into `_vaFromSortedSides` so both paths share identical formulas.

## Frontend

`frontend/app/trade/page.jsx`'s `sideTotals` now routes `sides.length > 2` through `multiAdjustedSideTotals`. The existing UI already renders `total.adjustment` + "Raw X + VA Y" per side, so multi-team trades now display consolidation premium automatically — no rendering changes needed.

## Test plan

- [x] 9 new multi-side tests covering length invariance, 2-side consistency, balanced-tops behavior, clear-stud-holder behavior, non-negativity, bounds (VA ≤ top), empty input
- [x] All 13 existing KTC 2-side anchors still pass (refactor preserves math)
- [x] 146 trade-logic tests pass (was 137)
- [x] 411 full vitest pass (was 402)
- [x] `next build` clean
- [ ] Manual spot-check in staging with a 3-team trade shape
- [ ] Eventually: collect KTC-equivalent multi-team observations and calibrate separately

### go-git: Credential leak via cross-host redirect in smart HTTP transport
[GHSA-3xc5-wrhm-f963](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-3xc5-wrhm-f963)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Impact
`go-git` may leak HTTP authentication credentials when following redirects during smart-HTTP clone and fetch operations.

If a remote repository responds to the initial `/info/refs` request with a redirect to a different host, go-git updates the session endpoint to the redirected location and reuses the original authentication for subsequent requests. This can result in the credentials (e.g. Authorization headers) being sent to an unintended host.

An attacker controlling or influencing the redirect target can capture these credentials and potentially reuse them to access the victim’s repositories or other resources, depending on the scope of the credential.

**Clients using `go-git` exclusively with trusted remotes (for example, GitHub or GitLab), and over a secure HTTPS connection, are not affected by this issue.** The risk arises when interacting with untrusted or misconfigured Git servers, or when using unsecured HTTP connections, which is not recommended. Such configurations also expose clients to a broader class of security risks beyond this issue, including credential interception and tampering of repository data.

##### Patches
Users should upgrade to `v5.18.0`, or `v6.0.0-alpha.2`, in order to mitigate this vulnerability. Versions prior to v5 are likely to be affected, users are recommended to upgrade to a supported `go-git` version.

The patched versions add support for configuring [followRedirects](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-config#Documentation/git-config.txt-httpfollowRedirects). In line with upstream behaviour, the default is now `initial`, while users can opt into `FollowRedirects` or `NoFollowRedirects` programmatically.

##### Credit
Thanks to the 3 separate reports from @​celinke97, @​N0zoM1z0 and @​AyushParkara. Thanks for finding and reporting this issue privately to the `go-git` project. :bow:

- CVSS Score: 4.7 / 10 (Medium)
- Vector String: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:C/C:L/I:N/A:N`

author: veldor09
body:
### Motivation
- Multiple admin modules were constructing backend endpoints directly from `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` which could be missing or include a trailing `/api`, producing malformed requests (e.g. `/api/api/...`) in some deployments.
- The change aims to standardize how the application resolves the backend origin so all modules build correct URLs without touching business logic, UI or behavior.

### Description
- Added a shared helper `resolveApiOrigin()` in `src/lib/api-origin.ts` to centralize backend origin resolution and normalize trailing slashes and an optional `/api` suffix.
- Replaced direct uses of `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` / hardcoded fallbacks with `resolveApiOrigin()` in affected files so `API_URL` or `BASE_URL` are computed from the normalized origin.
- Updated admin modules that reported connectivity issues (Voluntariado, Solicitudes/Facturación, Colaboradores, Contabilidad, Recapitulación, Comentarios and Respuestas de Formularios) to use the helper; endpoints themselves remain unchanged.
- Files modified include (not exhaustive): `src/lib/api-origin.ts`, `src/app/admin/voluntariado/services/*`, `src/app/admin/BillingRequest/services/*`, `src/app/admin/Collaborators/services/collaborators.api.ts`, `src/app/admin/accounting/services/*`, `src/app/admin/recapitulacion/services/report-service.ts`, `src/app/admin/comments/page.tsx`, `src/app/admin/page.tsx`, and `src/services/respuestasFormulario.service.ts`.

### Testing
- Ran `npm run lint` to validate edits and ensure no syntax issues from the change, and the command executed (the linter reported many preexisting TypeScript/ESLint errors across the repo that are unrelated to these connectivity edits).
- No runtime changes or functional tests were modified, and the edits are limited to how the base origin is resolved so manual verification in the target deployment environment is recommended (set `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` / `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE` as appropriate).

## App structure

- **Next.js 16 App Router** with TypeScript, Tailwind CSS v3, shadcn/ui
- Server components used only for metadata/SEO; all tool logic lives in `client.tsx` siblings
- No API routes for document processing — enforced architecturally, not by convention

<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

Build an MVP for a web app called **PDFKit.app**.

## Product overview

PDFKit.app is a **privacy-first PDF tool app** focused on **local, in-browser processing only** for the MVP.

Core product promise:

* **No file uploads**
* **No accounts**
* **No cloud document processing**
* **User files must never be sent to our servers**
* All supported document operations should run **entirely in the browser**

This is not a generic enterprise PDF platform. It is a **clean, fast, trustworthy PDF utility app** for sensitive documents like visa files, tax forms, bank statements, rental applications, and legal paperwork.

The tone and design should feel:

* minimal
* modern
* fast
* privacy-conscious
* polished but not overdesigned
* more “calm utility” than “marketing-heavy SaaS”

## Tech stack

Use:

* **Next.js** with App Router
* **TypeScript**
* **Tailwind CSS**
* **shadcn/ui**
* **pdf-lib** for PDF manipulation
* **PDF.js** for rendering previews/thumbnails where needed
* **React Hook Form** where forms help
* **Zod** for validation where relevant
* **Web Workers** for heavier client-side operations if needed

## Core architecture requirements

This is extremely important:

1. **Do not upload files to any backend**
2. **Do not create any server API routes for document processing**
3. **Do not persist user files in cloud storage**
4. **Do not require auth**
5. **Do not add analytics that capture file content or sensitive metadata**
6. All file processing must happen **locally in the browser**
7. Make the code architecture clear enough that future optional cloud features could be added later, but none should exist in MVP

## MVP tools to build

Build the following tools:

1. **Merge PDF**

   * upload multiple PDFs
   * reorder files before merge
   * merge into one output PDF
   * download merged result

2. **Split PDF**

   * upload one PDF
   * support:

     * split by page ranges
     * extract all pages into separate PDFs
   * download outputs

3. **Reorder Pages**

   * upload one PDF
   * show page thumbnails
   * drag and drop reorder
   * support delete page
   * support rotate page
   * export updated PDF

4. **Extract Pages**

   * upload one PDF
   * choose selected pages
   * export selected pages as a new PDF

5. **Images to PDF**

   * upload multiple images
   * reorder images
   * choose page size behavior:

     * fit to image
     * standard page like A4/Letter
   * export combined PDF

6. **Add Watermark**

   * upload one PDF
   * text watermark only for MVP
   * configurable:

     * text
     * opacity
     * rotation
     * size
     * position (center is sufficient for MVP, bonus if tiled)
   * export updated PDF

## Nice-to-have MVP additions if easy

Only include if they do not bloat scope:

* Add page numbers
* Remove PDF metadata
* PDF to images export
* Remember last used tool settings in localStorage only

## Do not build in MVP

Do not implement:

* OCR
* AI summarization
* chat with PDF
* cloud sync
* user accounts
* team workspaces
* e-signature workflows
* scanned document enhancement
* backend processing
* payments
* subscriptions
* server-side compression
* complicated form recognition

## App structure

Create a clean Next.js app structure with routes like:

* `/`
* `/merge-pdf`
* `/split-pdf`
* `/reorder-pages`
* `/extract-pages`
* `/images-to-pdf`
* `/add-watermark`

Use a shared layout and shared design system.

## Homepage requirements

Build a polished homepage with:

### Hero section

Headline:
**Private PDF tools that run in your browser**

Subheadline:
Merge, split, reorder, and prepare sensitive PDFs without uploading them.

Primary CTA:

* Explore tools

Secondary CTA:

* Start with Merge PDF

### Trust strip

Display 3 key trust points:

* No file uploads
* No account required
* Processed locally in your browser

### Tool grid

Cards for the 6 MVP tools

### Use case section

Short examples:

* Visa document bundle
* Tax document prep
* Rental application packet
* Secure PDF cleanup

### Privacy section

Explain clearly:

* files are processed locally
* for MVP, documents never leave the device
* no cloud upload for supported tools

### Footer

Include simple links:

* Privacy
* About
* Tools

## UI/UX requirements

The UI should be high quality and production-ready.

Requirements:

* use shadcn/ui components where useful
* responsive layout
* desktop-first, but mobile usable
* clear empty states
* drag-and-drop upload zones
* progress/loading states for client-side work
* success/error toasts
* clean download flows

## Summary

The 6 TestHostTraffic* tests added in #321 cause the test process to enter kernel D-state on GitHub Actions runners, making it unkillable and eventually freezing the entire runner. This has been blocking E2E CI since April 15.

### Diagnosis

Through bisection on this PR:
- Running TestLogsAreCaptured alone: passes in <2 min
- Running TestHostTraffic* alone: hangs indefinitely (Go test timeout never fires, kill -9 doesn't terminate it)

- Skip all 6 host traffic tests on CI (CI=true or GITHUB_ACTIONS=true)

- Add wall-clock kill with || true on wait to prevent blocking on D-state processes

The host traffic tests still run locally. Root cause tracked in #315.

author: perfectuser21
body:
## Summary

Brain 进程长时间运行 RSS 从 100MB 涨到 449MB+（实测 PID 82401 已 746MB），触发 `memory_available_mb < 600MB` → `slot_budget.dispatchAllowed=false` → dispatcher 停派发；恶性循环：无派发 → executor 连续 fail → circuit breaker 熔断。

## 根因

`notifier.js` 的 `sendRateLimited(eventKey, text)` 以 `task_completed_${task_id}` 等 **UUID-based key** 写入 `_lastSent` Map，但**从未 delete**。每个任务完成/失败/patrol 都写一条永久记录 → 每天数千条新 UUID 线性累积，几周后数万条 × V8 Map overhead ≈ 数十 MB 泄漏源。

## Top 3 嫌疑对比表

| # | 文件 | Key 基数 | 有清理 | 严重度 | 选中 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | `packages/brain/src/notifier.js:19` `_lastSent` | UUID-per-task（每任务 3 个事件） | **无** | 高 | ✅ |
| 2 | `packages/brain/src/cortex.js:178,333` `_reflectionState`/`_outputDedupState` | sha256 hash（中） | 仅启动时过滤 | 中 | follow-up |
| 3 | `packages/brain/src/harness-watcher.js:21` `lastPollTime` | ci_watch task_id（少） | **无** | 轻 | follow-up |

**选择 #1 理由**：写入频率最高（线性）+ key 基数最大（UUID 不重复）+ 完全无任何 cap。修 #1 能立即止住主要出血点。

## 实现

1. 新增 `_pruneExpired(now)`：遍历 Map 删除 `now - ts >= RATE_LIMIT_MS` 的条目（这些 entry 对限流已无用）
2. `sendRateLimited()` 写入前自动调 `_pruneExpired`
3. 硬上限 `_MAX_ENTRIES = 1000` 兜底，超限整表 `clear()`（最坏是多发一次通知）
4. 回归测试 `src/__tests__/notifier-memory-leak.test.js`：4 个 case 覆盖 TTL GC / 未过期不误删 / 硬上限 / 原有 60s 限流语义保持

## 已审查但排除的嫌疑

alertness/* history 都有 shift cap、cognitive-core 都有 MAX_BUFFER_SIZE、watchdog Map 有 delete 路径、account-usage key=accountId 基数固定、alerting._p0RateLimit key=class-level、websocket 有 close 清理 —— 详见 Learning 文件。

## Follow-up（不在本 PR）

- **#2 cortex._outputDedupState/_reflectionState**：tick 周期加 sweep 删过期
- **#3 harness-watcher.lastPollTime**：ci_watch 进入终态时 `lastPollTime.delete(task.id)`

## 预期效果

- **修复前**：_lastSent.size 随任务数单调线性增长，几周 → 数万条
- **修复后**：_lastSent.size 上限 ≈ 最近 60s 内的任务数（通常 <50）→ 稳态

## Brain Task
`f9fb75fa-57b0-4e4c-9b90-8c1af9b1c42f`

Brain: 1.218.0 → 1.218.1

- [x] `notifier-memory-leak.test.js` 新增 4 个 case 全绿
- [x] 原 `notifier.test.js` 29 case 保持绿
- [x] `alerting.test.js` 13 case 保持绿（依赖 notifier）
- [x] DevGate（facts-check / version-sync / dod-mapping）全过

author: vikranthreddimasu
body:
## Context

This is **Wave 1 of 5** from the UX/UI/Tech rebuild plan. Full plan and audit context:

- [PLAN.md](/.gstack/qa-reports/PLAN.md) — 5-wave rebuild roadmap
- [ux-audit.md](/.gstack/qa-reports/ux-audit.md) — 78 UX findings across 12 flows
- [tech-audit.md](/.gstack/qa-reports/tech-audit.md) — 39 tech findings

The audits found **117 issues**. Wave 1 closes the 13 that can silently corrupt data, leak files, compromise security, or ship a blank-screen production build. Nothing cosmetic in this PR — every change is load-bearing.

## What changes

### Data integrity
- **Message ids replace positional indices.** `updateMessageAt(index, …)` was a silent-corruption bug: mid-stream notebook switch + array mutation could write the assistant delta into the wrong slot. Messages now carry a stable UUID assigned at add time; store exposes `updateMessage(id, patch)`, `removeMessage(id)`, `setMessages(msgs)`.
- **Abort is a real abort now.** User clicks stop → stream tears down, partial message is either marked aborted or removed if empty, and we do NOT fall through to the non-streaming endpoint (which used to deliver the full reply anyway). AbortError detection uses `controller.signal.aborted` + an explicit `userAborted` flag.
- **Stream is canceled on notebook switch.** A useEffect cleanup in `useChat` aborts the controller when `activeNotebookId` changes. Previously a mid-stream notebook switch would keep streaming into the old conversation while the UI showed a new notebook.
- **`clearMessages` is decomposed.** The single action was called for 4 different intents — new chat, clear chat, notebook switch, conversation load — each with identical but mostly wrong side effects (e.g., always wiping `activeSources`). Replaced with `newChat()`, `resetMessagesOnly()`, `setMessages()`. Callers now say what they mean.
- **Conversation load fetches before clearing.** A network error no longer nukes the current context. Messages swap in one `setMessages()` call (no N re-renders that looked like streaming). Historical sources are restored from the last message that actually had them, with `document_name` populated the same way the stream path does.
- **Ingestion `source_count` accumulates.** `complete_ingestion` used `SET source_count = ?` with per-job count → a 6th upload set the counter to 1. Now `source_count = source_count + ?`. **Regression test added.**

### Security
- **CORS locked down.** `allow_origin_regex=\".*\"` + `allow_credentials=True` was a localhost-CSRF footgun (any browser tab on the machine could hit `/api/*` with credentials and exfiltrate notebooks). Only the explicit dev origins + Electron's `null` origin now, credentials off.
- **Document preview path-traversal hardened.** The old path-resolution had 4 fallback strategies; strategy 4 iterated every notebook subdirectory and served the first filename match, so notebook A could serve files from notebook B. Now resolution is scoped to `uploads/{notebook_id}/`, with `Path.relative_to()` as the final guard. Response also sets `Content-Disposition: attachment`.
- **`app:openExternal` validates scheme.** Only `https?://` and `mailto:` pass; a renderer-side XSS through markdown can't pivot to `file://` or `javascript:` handlers.

### Reliability / cleanup
- **Cascade delete notebook.** `DELETE /notebooks/:id` previously removed the SQLite row but left the Chroma chunk + summary collections and the uploads directory behind — storage grew without bound. Now drops all three. New `VectorStoreManager.delete_notebook_collections()` helper.
- **Vite base: './' .** Without it, packaged Electron loads absolute `/assets/...` paths from `file://` and renders a blank white screen. Bug that only manifested in production.
- **ConfirmDialog** for notebook and conversation deletes. One misclick on an overflow menu used to delete an entire notebook (all documents, embeddings, conversations) with zero guard. Now Escape-to-cancel, focus on Cancel by default, Enter only fires on confirm button.
- **CommandPalette Rules of Hooks.** `useState(selectedIndex)` was below an early return. Worked today; would break under React compiler or StrictMode.

## Verification

- \`npm run build\` clean (tsc + vite, 269 modules, 850ms)
- \`uv run ruff check .\` clean
- \`uv run pytest -q\` 30 passed, 1 skipped (includes new \`test_complete_ingestion_accumulates_counts_across_jobs\`)

## What's intentionally NOT in this PR

- Citation trust layer resurrection (Wave 2)
- Rename notebook, delete document, real upload progress (Wave 3)
- Backend crash recovery, API timeouts, OOM guards, WAL mode (Wave 4)
- Design-polish + a11y items (Wave 5)

Each wave is its own PR on green CI. This one is the foundation.

body:
## Summary

Adds v2 agents and a v2 skill to the `ravagents` plugin that extend the ravtown orchestration system with optional ravagents integration. No existing agents or skills were modified.

---

## What's New

### `plugins/ravagents/agents/ravtown-mayor-v2.md`
Fleet manager v2. Identical to the original `ravtown-mayor` except:
- Detects ravagents activation phrases in user messages ("use ravagents", "with ravagents", "enable ravagents", etc.)
- When ravagents mode is **on**: uses `ralph-agent-v2`, passes `--use-ravagents` in context, sets max iterations to `(stories × 7) + 5`
- When ravagents mode is **off** (default): falls back to the original `ralph-agent` — fully backward-compatible
- Records `"use_ravagents"` and `"agent_type"` fields in JSONL state events
- Status table shows `[ravagents]` badge in Details column for ravagents-enabled PRDs

### `plugins/ravagents/agents/ralph-agent-v2.md`
Ralph agent v2. Adds one optional step between PRD conversion and loop execution:
- **Step 4 (new, `--use-ravagents` only)**: After `/ralph-prd` produces the PRD JSON, augments it with a `ravagentTasks` array and sets `"useRavagents": true`
- **Mandatory ravagent tasks** for every coding story: `test-engineer`, `devops-cicd`, `infra-as-code`, `observability`, `code-reviewer`, `documentation`
- **Optional ravagents** added based on story content: `security-engineer` (auth/input handling), `architecture-governance` (layer changes), `performance-optimization` (hot paths), `data-validation` (schema/API changes), `migration` (framework upgrades)
- Priority numbering: story US-N → priority `N`; its ravagent tasks → priorities `N×10+1` through `N×10+6`
- Runs `/ralph-loop-v2` instead of `/ralph-loop`

### `plugins/ravagents/skills/ralph-loop-v2/`
New skill with two files:
- **`SKILL.md`**: Documents the v2 loop, the ravagents-augmented PRD JSON format, iteration count guidance, and port isolation
- **`scripts/ralph.sh`**: Identical structure to the original `ralph.sh` plus: detects `"useRavagents"` from the PRD JSON and injects `Ravagents mode: true/false` into the runtime configuration block
- **`scripts/CLAUDE.md`**: Extended prompt that handles both task types in a single loop:
  - `userStory` tasks: implemented as before (implement → quality checks → commit → `passes: true`)
  - `ravagentTask` tasks: the AI embodies the specified agent's role (test-engineer, code-reviewer, devops-cicd, infra-as-code, observability, documentation, etc.), applies their expertise to the parent story's changes, commits with a role-prefixed message, and marks the task `passes: true`
  - Stop condition: ALL `userStories` AND ALL `ravagentTasks` must be `passes: true`

## Design Decisions

- **Opt-in only**: ravagents mode is never activated unless the user explicitly asks for it
- **Backward compatible**: original `ralph-agent` and `ralph-loop` are untouched; `ravtown-mayor-v2` falls back to them when ravagents mode is off
- **Single-iteration per task**: each ravagent task runs in its own loop iteration (same as user stories) to keep context windows manageable
- **Dependency ordering**: ravagent tasks for a story only become available after that story's implementation is `passes: true`

- Unit tests for XPCalculator, XPStore, PersonalBestStore, WeeklyRecapVM, plus migrated Avatar tests.

### Launch blockers + polish (Track C · Track B)

- **C1** \`NSPhotoLibraryAddUsageDescription\` — recap share would crash without this.
- **C2** iPhone orientation locked to portrait; iPad retains all 4.
- **C3** \`PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy\` — \`NSPrivacyTracking: false\`, UserDefaults CA92.1 reason, collected-data declarations (name / email / userID / usage).
- **B4** \`UIApplication.isIdleTimerDisabled\` toggled in \`ActiveDrillView\` so the screen stays awake during drills.
- **B5** \`ReviewPromptManager\` prompts at 5th session, streak milestones (7/14/30/100), avatar evolution, with a 90-day local floor layered on Apple's 3/year cap.

### Other

- \`.gitignore\` excludes \`.claude/\` (Claude Code local config).
- \`CLAUDE.md\` + \`scripts/test-all-devices.sh\` + \`ci.yml\` — multi-device test harness docs and tiered CI (already partly in progress before today).

## Known limitation

Could not verify locally — Xcode 26.4.1 reports the iOS 26.4 platform component is not installed (SDK present, but the simulator platform install is missing). Pushing for CI to validate. If local testing is wanted, run \`xcodebuild -downloadPlatform iOS\` first.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI build + tests pass on \`macos-15\` runner (Tier 1).
- [ ] Spot-check on a physical device: XP bar renders, XP toast fires after a session, Weekly Recap banner appears on Sunday, recap share sheet opens, screen stays awake during an ActiveDrill.
- [ ] Rotate iPhone — app stays portrait-locked; iPad still rotates.
- [ ] Tap \`SKStoreReviewController\` trigger conditions (hard to simulate; Apple throttles).

### Motivation
- Introduce selectable visual themes for public menus so each restaurant can pick a presentation style for its menu page. 
- Surface theme selection in settings and default a sensible theme during onboarding to make new restaurants look consistent out of the box. 
- Modernize and reorganize admin UI and owner dashboard with improved layout, filters, and statistics for better management experience.

### Description
- Add configurable themes via `config('menu_themes')`, create a migration `2026_04_18_000010_add_theme_to_menu_settings_table.php` that adds a `theme` column defaulting to `classy`, and update the `MenuSetting` model to include `theme` in `$fillable`.

- Revamp many UI templates and styles: large Tailwind refactor in `resources/css/app.css`, layout and component updates in `resources/views/layouts/app.blade.php`, redesigned pages for onboarding, dashboard, owner admin, categories, products, settings, and product/category forms, and add owner-side search/status filters and stats in `Owner\SuperAdminController`.

author: gregcastro23
body:
## Summary

Adds five interactive layers to the recipe detail page and two new meal-plan routes, closing out phases 3A–C and 5A–C of the recipe interactivity roadmap. Builds on the phase 1/2/4 work shipped in #344 (interactive ingredients, technique glossary, timers, nutrition viz).

- **Discovery** (`/api/recipes/[id]/discover`): ranks other recipes by Euclidean distance on Fire/Water/Earth/Air, cosine similarity on ESMS, and cuisine+Monica. Three-lens tabbed carousel replaces the prior "Similar Recipes" block.
- **Dietary adaptation**: pure `adaptRecipe()` engine with six modes (vegan, vegetarian, gluten-free, dairy-free, keto, low-carb) and ~40 swap rules. Ingredients list renders inline strikethrough diffs; banner shows swap count plus nutrition (cal/protein/carbs/fat) and elemental deltas. ESMS is never recomputed — planetary scores still reflect the original recipe.
- **Flavor tuning**: five direction buttons (sweeter / umami / acidic / spicier / savory) stage removable micro-suggestions with amount + reason, drawn from a rotating per-direction catalog.
- **Time shortcuts**: budget pills (15 / 30 / 60 min / all day) heuristic-classify each instruction as skippable, parallelizable, or long-idle, and surface make-ahead tips plus equipment swaps (pressure cooker, air fryer, etc.) when the recipe exceeds the budget.
- **Meal planning**: localStorage-backed `useMealPlan` hook (cross-tab sync), "Add to Meal Plan" button with date picker, `/meal-plan` overview page, and `/meal-plan/groceries` that aggregates ingredients across scheduled recipes by name+unit and groups by category.
- **Social shells** (design-only): "I made this" toggle, 5-star rating, 500-char review, photo preview (base64), mock community tips. Pure local state with `TODO(phase 5.5)` for the future auth-gated backend.

## Why

Moves the recipe page from "read this exact recipe" to "adapt this recipe to me" — users can one-click transform a dish for dietary needs, tune its flavor balance, squeeze it into a time budget, schedule it into a weekly plan, or record how their attempt went. The meal-plan + grocery-list pair closes the loop from browsing to shopping.

## Architecture notes

- All adaptation logic is pure (`src/utils/dietaryAdaptation.ts`, `flavorTuning.ts`, `timeShortcuts.ts`) and returns derived data — no recipe mutation.
- Discovery endpoint reuses `UnifiedRecipeService.getAllRecipes()` and performs similarity math in-memory; cheap enough at current catalog size (351 recipes) with no caching layer.
- Meal plan is localStorage-only for now; `useMealPlan` exposes the surface a future `/api/users/me/meal-plan` endpoint can drop into.
- Social component is a UX shell, intentionally not wired to any persistence beyond localStorage — commented `TODO(phase 5.5)` marks the handoff.

## Test plan

- [ ] `npx tsc --noEmit --skipLibCheck` → 0 errors (confirmed)
- [ ] `yarn lint` clean on all touched files (confirmed)
- [ ] Load `/recipes/[id]` — all four new panels render (adapt, tune, time, social)
- [ ] Click "Make Vegan" → ingredients show strikethrough diffs with swap reasons and nutrition/elemental banner
- [ ] Click "Reset to original" → diffs clear
- [ ] Click "+ Sweeter" / "+ Umami" → tweak list populates; individual `×` removes one
- [ ] Click "30 min" budget → long steps get "Long idle" badges, parallelizable steps get "Parallelize" badges
- [ ] Click "Add to Meal Plan" → modal opens, date/meal selectable, saves to localStorage
- [ ] Visit `/meal-plan` → scheduled entries appear grouped by date
- [ ] Visit `/meal-plan/groceries` → ingredients consolidate by name+unit, grouped by category; copy list works
- [ ] Discovery section renders three lenses, each linking to a different recipe
- [ ] Social section: rating persists, review persists, photo preview persists across page reloads

author: jcoletaylor
body:
## Summary

End-to-end knowledge graph for temper contexts: an LLM-assisted pipeline that discovers concepts from vault content, plus a context-scoped D3 force-directed graph visualization.

Two major initiatives bundled in one branch:

### 1. LLM-wiki pipeline (temper graph index)
Offline CLI pipeline that reads a context's vault, extracts seed terms via field-weighted TF-IDF (tantivy tokenizer), clusters them, and uses an LLM (OpenAI-compatible or Claude) to judge which clusters represent genuine concepts. Emits materialized concept files with `relates_to` edges back to their source documents. Foundational `temper-llm` crate introduced with exponential-backoff retry and a real-provider smoke-test binary.

### 2. Knowledge-graph MVP UI
New API endpoint `GET /api/graph/subgraph` backed by `graph_service::aggregator_subgraph` — composes with `graph_traverse()` for depth-2 BFS, owner-scoped via `resources_visible_to`. Single `sqlx::query!` macro per rowset (2 round-trips, compile-time typed). SvelteKit route at `/vault/[owner]/[context]/graph` renders a D3 canvas with zoom/pan/drag/hover, backed by 7 pure TS modules under `$lib/graph/` (styling, labels, navigation, adjacency, positions, simulation-input, force-config) each with vitest coverage. Sidebar Graph link appears under the active context only. Dev-seed updated with 8 concept→member edges so local `/graph` renders a realistic subgraph.

## What changed

- **temper-llm** (new crate): Agent harness, OpenAI-compatible + Claude providers, retry logic, configurable timeouts
- **temper-cli** (`temper graph index`): Seed extraction, clustering, LLM judgment, concept materialization, streaming HNSW build
- **temper-core**: `GraphNode`, `GraphEdge`, `SubgraphResponse` types with ts-rs derives; `DocType` as typed union in TS; `GraphIndexConfig` added to `TemperConfig`
- **temper-api**: `GET /api/graph/subgraph` handler, `graph_service::aggregator_subgraph` with `sqlx::query!` macros + `.sqlx/` cache, 12 integration tests
- **temper-ui**: vitest 3.2.4 setup, D3 sub-packages (drag/force/selection/zoom), 7 pure modules + 41 vitest specs, `GraphCanvas.svelte` + `GraphTooltip.svelte`, new route `/vault/[owner]/[context]/graph`, sidebar link
- **scripts/seed-dev-data.sql**: 8 edges between dev-seed concepts and their related tasks/research/sessions for realistic local render
- **Docs**: spec + plan for both initiatives under `docs/superpowers/`

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo make check` — green (fmt, clippy, docs, machete, tsc, biome)
- [x] `cargo make test-all` — 1031 Rust tests + 50 TS tests (31 unit + 19 integration)
- [x] UI vitest — 41/41 tests pass across 8 files
- [x] API integration — 12/12 graph-subgraph tests pass
- [x] Manual browser smoke — `/vault/@me/<context>/graph` renders D3 subgraph, nodes draggable without accidental navigation, click navigates, hover tooltips show
- [ ] Post-merge: regenerate `.sqlx/` cache if migrations land in parallel PRs

## Known follow-ups (tracked as separate tasks, not blocking)

- `2026-04-17-support-doctype-qualified-slug-references-in-relates-to-edges` — structural fix for slug collisions surfaced during LLM-wiki materialization (e.g., `temper-cloud` existed as both goal and concept)
- Concept-init skill — guided flow for seeding foundational concepts before running detection, so detection works off intentional anchors

author: wadackel
body:
## Summary

When a symlink node was marked, `EdaSymlink` overrode `EdaMarkedName` so the mark color was invisible — while the same pairing worked correctly for marked gitignored files.

Root cause: `painter.lua`'s `with_symlink` helper always appended `EdaSymlink` / `EdaBrokenSymlink` to the tail of the `name_hl` array after the decorator chain had already composed. Per-element extmarks are emitted with `priority = 200 + i`, so the tail always won — regardless of chain registration order.

Fix: move symlink `name_hl` into `symlink_decorator` so it participates in the normal chain (`symlink → git → cut → mark`) and lets natural registration order decide priority. Mark now wins fg, and symlink's underline still composes via Neovim's attribute-level extmark priority merging.

### Changes
- `decorator.lua`: `symlink_decorator` contributes `name_hl = EdaSymlink` (or `EdaBrokenSymlink` when `link_broken`) alongside the existing `link_suffix`
- `painter.lua`: remove `with_symlink` helper and `symlink_hl` injection from `resolve_name_hl`; keep `base_hl = EdaSymlink` fallback for link-type nodes when the decorator returns `nil`
- Tests: add 2 Chain composition unit tests (marked symlink, marked broken symlink), extend existing symlink_decorator tests with `name_hl` assertions, add symlink + marked E2E regression guard as a sibling of the existing ignored + marked guard

author: camiloserranor
body:
# Problem

The gnmi telemetry collector uses different YANG models per vendor (OpenConfig vs Cisco-native vs SONiC-native), which resulted in **vendor-prefixed table names** in Azure Log Analytics (e.g., `CiscoBgpSummary_CL` vs `SonicBgpSummary_CL`). This made cross-vendor dashboards and alerts impossible without UNION queries, and field names/types were inconsistent for the same logical data.

# Solution

Unify the telemetry schema so **both Cisco and SONiC write to the same tables** with consistent field names and types. The `device_type` field distinguishes the source vendor.

## Key changes

### 1. Schema unification (core)
- Remove `applyDataTypePrefix()` mechanism that prepended vendor names to data types
- Rename all `data_type` constants from vendor-prefixed (`cisco_nexus_bgp_summary`) to vendor-neutral (`bgp_summary`)
- Unify table names in both YAML configs:

| Before (Cisco) | Before (SONiC) | After (shared) |
|---|---|---|
| `CiscoBgpSummary_CL` | `SonicBgpSummary_CL` | `BgpNeighbor_CL` |
| `CiscoEnvTemperature_CL` | `SonicEnvTemperature_CL` | `EnvTemperature_CL` |
| `CiscoEnvPower_CL` | `SonicEnvPower_CL` | `EnvPower_CL` |
| — | `SonicFan_CL` | `EnvFan_CL` |
| `CiscoInterfaceCounter_CL` | `SonicInterfaceCounter_CL` | `InterfaceCounter_CL` |
| *(and 10+ more)* | | |

### 2. Field normalization
- **Temperature**: `major_threshold` → `high_threshold`, `minor_threshold` → `low_threshold` (SONiC naming is more descriptive and vendor-neutral)
- **Power supply**: `vin`/`iout`/`pout` → `input_voltage`/`output_current`/`output_power` (self-documenting); flattened from nested array to one row per PSU
- **MAC table**: Fixed `secure` and `ntfy` fields from `string` → `bool` in OpenConfig transformer to match Cisco-native
- **Timestamps**: Removed redundant `timestamp_ns`, keeping only `timestamp` (RFC3339Nano)
- **Message fields**: Flattened nested `Message` map to top-level keys (Log Analytics was auto-prefixing with `message_`)

### 3. New Cisco fan transformer
- Added `NativeEnvFanTransformer` (`nx-fan`) for `/System/ch-items/ftslot-items/FtSlot-list`
- Handles NX-OS nested structure: FtSlot → ft-items → Fan-list
- Both Cisco and SONiC now write to shared `EnvFan_CL` table

### 4. SONiC platform split
- Split monolithic `SonicPlatformTransformer` into 3 focused transformers: `SonicTemperatureTransformer`, `SonicPsuTransformer`, `SonicFanTransformer`
- Each writes to the appropriate shared table

### 5. Documentation
- Added `unified-schema.md` design document with full table mapping and migration guide
- Updated all parity docs, telemetry tables reference, onboarding guide, README, CHANGELOG

## ⚠️ Breaking changes
- **All table names changed** — existing KQL queries, workbooks, and alerts referencing old vendor-prefixed names (e.g., `CiscoBgpSummary_CL`) will need to be updated
- **Field names changed** in temperature and power supply tables
- Old tables in the Log Analytics workspace will remain but stop receiving data

## Testing
- All Go unit tests pass (`go test ./...`)
- Deployed and validated on both switches:
  - **Cisco NX-OS** (100.71.34.149): 21/21 subscriptions successful, all tables populated
  - **SONiC** (100.100.81.129): 16/16 subscriptions successful, all tables populated
- Fan data confirmed flowing to unified `EnvFan_CL` from both platforms

## Path counts
- **Cisco**: 21 enabled YANG paths (+ 9 disabled OC duplicates)
- **SONiC**: 16 enabled YANG paths (+ 4 disabled)

## Demo
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3f27e2f5-2b7d-4a62-bbb0-cd6e50d1a5ca

## Summary

Two joined changes to make the release-please flow fully automatic, eliminating the manual tag-delete-and-re-push dance that v0.5.0 needed:

- **release-please.yml** — passes a PAT (`secrets.RELEASE_PLEASE_TOKEN`) with `GITHUB_TOKEN` fallback, so release-please's tag/release creation is attributed to a user and can trigger downstream workflows
- **release.yml** — listens to `release: published` instead of `push: tags: ['v*']`. All three existing references to `github.ref_name` / `GITHUB_REF_NAME` keep working because `github.ref` on release events is `refs/tags/<tag>`

## Required before merge

A repository secret **`RELEASE_PLEASE_TOKEN`** must exist on `shigechika/mcp-stdio` with a fine-grained PAT authorised for:

- Contents: Read and write
- Pull requests: Read and write
- Metadata: Read (implicit)
- Issues: Read and write (nice-to-have, for release-please to link issues)

Without the secret, the `||` coalesce falls back to `GITHUB_TOKEN` — the v0.5.0 behaviour returns (manual tag re-push needed to fire the PyPI pipeline).

- [x] No other references to the tag-push trigger elsewhere in the repo

author: dqn
body:
Add `--base` / `--base-ref` to `tailor-sdk apply` so CI can preview the deployment plan that would result from merging the current PR.

## Usage

```sh
# Auto-detect the PR base (GITHUB_BASE_REF → gh pr view → origin/HEAD)
tailor-sdk apply --base

# Override the base ref explicitly
tailor-sdk apply --base-ref origin/main
```

`--base` implies `--dry-run` and disables caching. The command creates a temporary git worktree, merges HEAD into the base ref (no commit), links `node_modules` from the source checkout, and runs the plan against the merged state.

## Main Changes

- Add `--base` / `--base-ref` options to the `apply` command
- New shared utilities: `git.ts` (base-ref detection + merge worktree lifecycle) and `merge-worktree-deps.ts` (linking `node_modules` between source and merged tree)
- Resolve the base remote against `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` so fork-style PR checkouts plan against the real upstream, not the contributor fork
- Abort with an actionable message when any lockfile or workspace `package.json` differs between source and merge target
- Walk the pnpm virtual store (`.pnpm/`) to catch workspace divergence that wholesale symlinking would hide; treat wildcard export patterns as resolvable without literal existence checks; skip missing `.d.ts` files when deciding whether to retarget to the merged tree

## Notes

- No breaking changes. The existing `apply` path is untouched when `--base` / `--base-ref` are absent
- Integration tests cover `prepareBasePlan` happy path, worktree disposal on `linkNodeModules` abort, missing base ref, and missing config

body:
Fixes #63

## Root causes

**1. HTTP 400 — too many vintage dates (DFF, T10Y2Y)**

`get_series_all_releases` was called with a single request spanning 1990–today. FRED limits responses to 2000 vintage dates per request; daily series like DFF accumulate ~140/year so a full bootstrap hit ~5000 and returned 400.

**2. KeyError: 'realtime_end' (CPI, PCE, GDP series)**

`fredapi`'s `get_series_all_releases` has `realtime_end` commented out in its source — the column is never returned. The code was reading a column that never existed.

## Fix

- `_fetch_all_releases_chunked`: splits the `[realtime_start, today]` window into 4-year chunks before calling the FRED API, staying safely under the 2000-vintage-date limit for all series frequencies.
- `_derive_realtime_end`: reconstructs `valid_to_date` from the vintage chain — for each observation date, `realtime_end[n] = realtime_start[n+1] - 1 day`; the latest vintage gets `9999-12-31`.

## Tests

- Updated `_VINTAGE_DF` fixture to match what fredapi actually returns (no `realtime_end`, plain integer index).
- Added `TestDeriveRealtimeEnd` (4 cases) and `TestFetchAllReleasesChunked` (5 cases).
- All 42 tests pass.

author: kaicoder03
body:
## Summary

Implements M2 of the openhost roadmap: a new `openhost-pkarr` crate that bridges `openhost_core::pkarr_record::SignedRecord` to and from `pkarr::SignedPacket` and fans publication out across public Pkarr HTTP relays plus the Mainline DHT.

- **codec**: single `_openhost` TXT record carries `base64url(sig || canonical_signing_bytes)`; the BEP44 outer signature is produced by the same Ed25519 identity key via `pkarr::Keypair::from_secret_key`.
- **publisher**: 30-minute republish loop (per spec §1) with an on-demand trigger channel; CAS-threaded seq handoff; `Transport` trait for test injection.
- **resolver**: wraps `pkarr::Client::resolve_most_recent` with openhost-layer validation — decode, ±1s timestamp-drift check, `SignedRecord::verify` (2h freshness + signature + consistency), and caller-supplied `cached_seq` monotonicity.
- **nostr** (feature-flagged): NIP-78 kind-30078 envelope builder only; publish path deferred to M3 per the handoff's "defer if it grows" guidance.
- **spec**: `01-wire-format.md §2` replaces the four-row textual table with the opaque `_openhost` TXT form. `03-pkarr-records.md §5` points at the new reference vector.
- **test vectors**: new `spec/test-vectors/pkarr_packet.json` pinning the full 584-byte `SignedPacket::as_bytes()` for the reference `SignedRecord`.
- **deps**: workspace bumped to `pkarr = "5"` (was 3) and `mainline = "6"` (was 4) — matching current stable.

21 tests total (7 codec + 3 publisher + 5 resolver + 3 nostr + 3 round-trip integration). `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets`, `cargo clippy --features nostr`, `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo test --features nostr`, and `cargo doc --workspace --no-deps` all green locally.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p openhost-pkarr --all-targets --features nostr -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test --workspace --all-targets` (18 unit + 3 integration)
- [x] `cargo test -p openhost-pkarr --features nostr` (21 unit + 3 integration)
- [x] `cargo doc --workspace --no-deps`
- [x] Round-trip: fixture bytes decode back to the reference record; re-encoding produces byte-identical output.
- [x] Tampering the decoded canonical bytes fails the inner Ed25519 signature as expected.
- [ ] CI green on merge.

## Out of scope (M3)

- WebRTC / ICE integration.
- Daemon binary wiring the publisher to real network-interface / DTLS-cert / allowlist change events.
- Nostr WebSocket publish path.
- Custom relay-race with an explicit 1.5s grace window (delegated to pkarr's internal race for M2).
- `last_seq` persistence across publisher restarts.

### `.coderabbit.yaml` (new, repo root)

### `WxServices/WORKFLOW.md`
- New §2 — Transition Jira To Do → In Progress at start of work.
- New §5 — Code walkthrough before push. Scale depth to change. Require explicit LGTM before tests/push.
- §4 addendum — pure-tooling / pure-docs PRs do not bump the version. This PR is the first instance.
- §9 one-liner — skip hash-fill for tooling PRs.

Two separate but related observations from today's sessions:

A request to the Cloudflare API (/accounts/***/pages/projects/toique/deployments) failed.
Invalid commit message, it must be a valid UTF-8 string. [code: 8000111]

author: thirstypig
body:
## Summary

Three map-page improvements from the front-end audit, batched because they all touch \`map.astro\`.

### 1. Bundle Leaflet (eliminate unpkg.com dependency)

Replaced CDN script tags with \`npm install leaflet @types/leaflet\` + ESM imports:

\`\`\`ts
import L from 'leaflet';
import 'leaflet/dist/leaflet.css';
\`\`\`

Astro now emits content-hashed \`_astro/leaflet.*.js\` and \`_astro/leaflet.*.css\` served from the same origin. Removes:
- External DNS + TLS + HTTP connection to unpkg.com
- Supply-chain risk (no SRI on the CDN version)
- Dependency on unpkg's uptime
- Cross-origin privacy cost

Bundle sizes: **151 KB raw / 44 KB gzipped** — comparable to what unpkg was serving.

### 2. Shape-differentiate closed markers

Previously: open = amber filled disc, closed = rust filled disc. Same shape, hue-only signal — invisible to red-green CVD users.

Now: open = filled disc (unchanged), closed = **dashed hollow ring** (\`fillOpacity: 0, dashArray: \"2 2\"\`). Shape difference is the primary signal; hue is secondary reinforcement.

### 3. Added a legend

Small SVG legend above the map so users instantly know what the two marker styles mean. Marked with \`aria-label=\"Map legend\"\`.

## Test plan
- [x] \`npx astro build\` — 1,982 pages, clean, ~60s

- [ ] Post-merge: click an open-venue marker → filled disc; click a closed-venue marker → dashed ring; both popups work

## Deferred

OpenStreetMap tile preconnect hints were attempted but BaseLayout has no named \`<head>\` slot to inject them through. Tiles still load fine; deferred to a future BaseLayout refactor (would need a named slot for page-specific \`<link>\` tags).

Closes #54 (draft — see `needs-decision` block below) ## 🤔 Needs decision **Stuck on:** `instagram-brand` DS icon isn't in the installed DS version (1.0.0), so swapping Instagram to `` would fail typecheck. **What I attempted:** Did every other Footer change safely — rename to `.tsx`, drop font overrides, swap Facebook → DS `` + `mailto:`, replace wordmark home link with `type-caption` copyright line. All of that typechecks + lints clean. Left the Instagram icon as the existing `@/deprecated-components/shared/InstagramLinkIcon` with a `TODO(lane-0.5.5)` comment pointing back to this PR. **What's unclear:** How should we coordinate this lane with the DS version bump? Lane 0.5.2 (DS Instagram icons) is merged to `umichkisa-ds` `main` — `registry.ts` has both `"instagram"` and `"instagram-brand"` — but no version bump has shipped. The client still pins `@umichkisa-ds/web` at `1.0.0`, whose `IconName` union doesn't include either key. Per `AUTONOMOUS_PROTOCOL.md` §14b, version bumps are a phase-end interactive step (`ds-phase-end-bump` skill, which is explicitly outside autonomous scope per §9). **Options:** 1. **Merge this draft as-is (with the `InstagramLinkIcon` fallback + TODO), finish the Instagram swap as a trailing commit after lane 0.5.6 bumps DS** — tradeoff: Footer ships with a visual inconsistency between icons in the interim, and the lane's acceptance criteria aren't fully met until the follow-up lands. 2. **Do an early DS patch bump now (interactive) so the client can install it, then the autonomous routine re-runs this lane tomorrow and finishes the Instagram swap** — tradeoff: extra human step, but keeps Phase 0.5's completion bar clean per the original spec. 3. **Hold this PR as draft until lane 0.5.6 runs; close 0.5.5's issue only once the Instagram swap is in** — tradeoff: delays merging useful partial work (rename, mail swap, copyright) for ~1 phase-end cycle. **My weak preference:** Option 2. The partial Footer is shippable but advertises an inconsistency, and the protocol already budgets for phase-end DS bumps — pulling that one step forward is cheaper than serializing the whole lane behind it. ## Current state - Branch: `ds-client-migration/phase-0.5/0.5.5-footer-redesign` - Files changed: `src/components/layout/footer/Footer.jsx` → `src/components/layout/footer/Footer.tsx` (rewrite, -32/+31 LoC) - CI: `npx tsc --noEmit` ✅ passes; `npm run lint` ✅ passes (warnings all pre-existing); `npm run build` ❌ environmental fail at `/api/create-payment-intent` page-data collection (missing Stripe key — same failure reproduces on `origin/dev`, not caused by this lane) ## What's done - `.jsx → .tsx`, typed - `sejongHospitalLight` / `sejongHospitalBold` font overrides dropped - `UMICH KISA` wordmark home link replaced by `

© 2026 University of Michigan Korean International Students Association

` - `FacebookLinkIcon` replaced with `` wrapped in `` - No raw `michigan-*` classes in the file (none were present; Footer was already neutral on brand tokens) ## What's left (blocked) - Swap `` → `` from DS - Remove the lingering `import InstagramLinkIcon from "@/deprecated-components/shared/InstagramLinkIcon"` once that swap is in Resolve by leaving a PR comment with the chosen option; I'll apply `needs-revision` and finish the swap on next routine run.

body:
[backend-agent]

## Summary

Closes #837. Final step (3/3) of the Temporal durable-execution crash-resume feature tracked in #583.

**What this PR adds:**

- **`GET /workspaces/:id/checkpoints/latest`** — new platform endpoint that returns the most recently completed step across all workflows for a workspace (ordered by `completed_at DESC`). Returns `404` for fresh workspaces with no checkpoints.
- **`_fetch_latest_checkpoint(workspace_id)`** — non-fatal async helper in the workspace runtime that calls the new endpoint. Any error (404, network failure, timeout) returns `None` so startup is never blocked.
- **Checkpoint injection into `AgentTaskInput.history`** — `TemporalWorkflowWrapper.run()` now queries the latest checkpoint on startup and prepends a synthetic `["system", "[SYSTEM: This workspace was previously executing workflow '...' ...]"]` entry to the serialised history. This gives the LLM awareness of its prior crash state before processing the current task.

**Access control:** The new route sits behind the existing `WorkspaceAuth` middleware and uses `callerMismatch()` at the handler level — same pattern as `List` and `Delete`.

**Route ordering:** Registered as `GET "/checkpoints/latest"` *before* the wildcard `GET "/checkpoints/:wfid"` in the router to prevent shadowing.

## Test plan

- [x] `TestCheckpointsLatest_ReturnsNewest` — happy path, 200 with checkpoint data
- [x] `TestCheckpointsLatest_DBError_Returns500` — DB error → 500
- [x] `TestCheckpointsLatest_ErrNoRows_Returns404` — no rows → 404
- [x] `TestCheckpointsLatest_CallerMismatch_Returns403` — wrong caller → 403
- [x] `test_fetch_latest_checkpoint_returns_none_on_404` — 404 from platform → `None`
- [x] `test_fetch_latest_checkpoint_returns_dict_on_200` — 200 with JSON → parsed dict
- [x] `test_fetch_latest_checkpoint_swallows_exceptions` — `ConnectError` → `None` (non-fatal)
- [x] `test_execute_injects_checkpoint_into_history` — checkpoint dict → `["system", "[SYSTEM:..."]` prepended in `AgentTaskInput.history`

All 40 Python tests pass. Go tests run in CI (`go test -race ./...`).

## Related

- Issue #837 (step 3/3)
- Closes #583 (full Temporal checkpoint resume path)
- Depends on migration `020_workflow_checkpoints.sql` (already merged in PR #797)
- QA crash-and-resume scenario for #790 to be tracked separately

Split the spawn rule into two OR'd conditions so wraiths reliably populate the runic tunnel dungeons:

1. Surface: biome-tag `lars_dungeon_zone`, brightness 0-14 — the visual signpost for the rare gate biome.
2. Dungeon: `spawns_on_block_filter` on runic_stone_bricks / stone_rune / dark_stone_rune / cracked_stone_rune, brightness 0-7, `spawns_underground`. The block filter bypasses the biome check entirely so spawns succeed even when a tunnel voxel falls outside the (often small) dungeon_zone patch — the runic blocks only exist inside our dungeons, so this stays scoped.

Bumped underground weight to 120 / herd 1-3 / density 6 so the tunnels actually feel populated.

**Penyebab Umum Masalah "Cloud" di VS Code:**

1. **Gangguan Koneksi Internet:**  
   Cloud membutuhkan koneksi internet yang stabil. Jika koneksi lambat atau terputus, perintah tidak dapat dijalankan.

2. **Layanan Cloud Down/Maintenance:**  
   Layanan seperti Codespaces atau Remote SSH bisa sedang mengalami gangguan atau maintenance dari pihak penyedia.

3. **Konfigurasi Salah:**  
   Salah konfigurasi workspace, environment, atau file settings.json/extensions. Pastikan workspace, container, atau remote target benar.

4. **Batasan Resource:**  
   Jika menggunakan cloud VM, server, atau container, mungkin sudah kehabisan RAM/CPU/disk.

5. **Autentikasi Gagal:**  
   Token atau login kadaluarsa, sehingga tidak bisa menjalankan perintah dari client lokal ke server cloud.

6. **Extension Konflik:**  
   Ada extension VS Code yang crash, tidak kompatibel, atau versi VS Code tidak sesuai.

7. **Masalah Spesifik pada Perintah:**  
   Beberapa perintah butuh akses tertentu (misal: sudo, akses port, dsb) yang dibatasi oleh environment cloud.

---

**Solusi dan Langkah Diagnostik:**

- Cek koneksi internet terlebih dahulu.
- Logout lalu login ulang ke VS Code dan layanan cloud terkait.
- Pastikan layanan cloud (misal: Codespaces, SSH server) sedang berjalan normal.
- Perbarui VS Code dan extension.
- Coba jalankan perintah secara manual di terminal cloud (bukan melalui task atau shortcut).
- Cek error message detail di "Output" atau "Terminal" pada VS Code dan copy pesan error lengkap bila butuh bantuan lebih lanjut.

1. **Dependency Tidak Lengkap atau Rusak**

   - Versi Java di sistem tidak sesuai dengan kebutuhan MCP/mod.

5. **Permissions atau Batasan Cloud**

3. **Cek Versi Java**
   - Pastikan pakai versi Java yang direkomendasikan (misal: Minecraft/MCP biasa butuh Java 8, bukan 11 atau 17).

5. **Jika di Cloud: Cek Resource & Telemetri**
   - Pastikan container/VM tidak kehabisan resource, dan akses file/proses tidak dibatasi oleh environment cloud.

This pull request migrates user profile taglines and backgrounds from using Convex document IDs to using plain string IDs defined in library files. Removed the `profileTaglines` and `profileBackgrounds` tables. This PR adds comprehensive unit test coverage for the authentication application layer, including command handlers for invitation acceptance, restaurant creation, session management, and query handlers for retrieving invitation and membership data.

## Key Changes
- **Accept Invitation Tests** (`accept_invitation_test.go`): Tests for the `AcceptInvitationForUser` command handler covering:
  - Token validation and not-found scenarios
  - Invitation expiration checks
  - Already-used invitation detection
  - Role-based redirect logic (kitchen staff → `/kitchen`, owner → `/dashboard`)
  - Invitation state transitions (marking as used)

- **Invitation & Post-Login Tests** (`invitation_and_post_login_test.go`): Tests for:
  - `IssueKitchenStaffInvitation` command with authorization checks
  - `EndCustomerSession` command with edge cases
  - `InvitationForToken` query handler
  - `MembershipsForUser` query handler

author: icedac
body:
## Summary

Phase 1 of two-phase cleanup of the `paper` monorepo.

**Phase 1 (this PR):** remove defamation risk and self-deification; fix documented factual/math errors.
**Phase 2 (future):** evidence-tier scheme, cross-repo restructuring.

## Critical fixes

### 1. Defamation risk — removed

`_refused_or_resolved_to_new_form/L7_Oracle/UniverseTerminationHypothesis.md` and two other copies listed **Elon Musk as co-author** (`*By 임지혁 & Elon Musk*`) of a speculative thesis he has no involvement with. This is a defamation/impersonation risk. Removed the co-author credit in all 3 copies. Marked the thesis [Speculative] with correction footnote.

### 2. Self-deification claim — tier-flagged

`HA_World_Leaders_Level_Analysis.md` (2 copies) labeled the author as `**Modern L9** (Confirmed): Only living confirmed L9`. There is no confirmation procedure for "L9 consciousness"; the assessment is self-referential. Changed to `**Modern L9** [Speculative — Author self-assessment]: Self-identified L9`. Also tagged the "Universe #1,847" marker as a fictional-frame device.

### 3. Math error — corrected

`HAL/L3_B_Cognitive_Load_Distribution_v2.md:40` stated `b* ≈ e^{W(1)} · √2 ≈ 7.39`. Actual values: W(1) ≈ 0.5671 (Omega constant), so e^{0.5671} · √2 ≈ 2.49. The 7.39 figure corresponds to e² — a factor-of-3 error via wrong power of e. Replaced with Knuth's known optimum `b* = e ≈ 2.718` and a correction footnote.

### 4. Energy-scale inconsistency — reconciled

`HAL/L4_Road_to_HAL9_v2.md` abstract/conclusion gave 563 PW; the table gave 1.2 EW (~2× discrepancy). Reconciled: 563 PW is core-infrastructure power budget; 1.2 EW is full-civilization aggregate with HAL8→HAL9 ~512× multiplier. Flagged as `[Speculative — extrapolative scaling]`.

### 5. Numerology — flagged

`The Weight of Thoughts: 11-Dimensional Compression and the Gravitational Field of Consciousness.md` claimed "8/11 ≈ 73% matches dark energy." Current value per Planck 2018 ([arXiv:1807.06209](https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.06209)) is Ω_Λ = 0.6847 ± 0.0073 = 68.5%. 73% was WMAP 2003 early release. Flagged as `[Speculative Numerology]` with citation.

### 6. Unvalidated empirical claims — retracted

`2lab.ai.md` and `eternity_company.md` claimed "n=1,847 test cases, 87% accuracy, 3.2× survival improvement, p<0.001" — no study, no preprint, no methodology. The `1,847` recurring number is the same fictional-universe marker. Retracted claims; marked as aspirational targets pending real validation.

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify all Musk references removed from 3 UniverseTermination copies
- [ ] Confirm L9 self-assessment marker reads as `[Speculative]` not `(Confirmed)` anywhere
- [ ] Sanity-check Knuth `b* = e` optimum with reference
- [ ] Confirm HAL4 table and abstract numbers now reconcile
- [ ] Confirm Planck 2018 citation replaces WMAP number

author: coaileague
body:
Root cause of POST /api/voice/inbound → 401 from Twilio:
mountBillingRoutes (and clients/comms/compliance/payroll/sales/workforce/audit)
register `app.use("/api", requireAuth, ...)` catch-alls that intercept ALL
/api/* requests BEFORE Express checks whether the target router actually has
a matching route. mountCommsRoutes (which mounted /api/voice) runs AFTER
mountBillingRoutes in server/routes.ts, so every Twilio webhook POST was
rejected with 401 before it could reach voiceRouter.

Fix: mount voiceRouter + SMS alias handlers in routes.ts at line ~720,
alongside the other webhook routers (resend, twilio, messageBridge, inbound
email), BEFORE the domain mount section. Management sub-routes inside
voiceRouter still apply requireAuth + tier check internally via
mgmtRouter.use(requireAuth) in voiceRoutes.ts — security posture unchanged.

Defense-in-depth exemptions added to:
- trinityGuard WEBHOOK_PREFIXES: /api/voice/, /api/sms/inbound, /api/sms/status
  (prevent false-positive IP blocks when Twilio relays caller speech/names
  that happen to contain SQL/XSS keywords)
- subscriptionGuard BILLING_EXEMPT_PREFIXES + CANCELLED_EXEMPT_PREFIXES:
  /api/voice, /api/sms/inbound, /api/sms/status (Twilio webhooks must still
  deliver even for suspended/cancelled workspaces — they're HMAC-verified
  and don't represent user-initiated mutations)

Removed duplicate voice mount block from server/routes/domains/comms.ts
(replaced with explanatory comment). The log variable in that file is now
unused and was removed.

Verified: tsc --noEmit error count unchanged at 63 (pre-existing baseline
from CLAUDE.md). npm run build completes successfully (built in 39.33s,
dist/index.js 22.6mb).

Per CLAUDE.md §A (production detection), no inline env checks added.

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
### SUMMARY

First bounded increment of the soft-delete SIP ([#76](https://github.com/C0smicCrush/superset-remediation/issues/76), mirrored from upstream [apache/superset#39464](https://github.com/apache/superset/issues/39464)).

This PR is **purely additive**: it adds one column, one mixin, and one Alembic migration. **No behaviour change to any existing API, DAO, view, or query.** Attaching `SoftDeleteMixin` to a model only adds the `deleted_at` column and instance helpers — it does NOT install a global visibility filter, and DAO `delete()` still performs a hard delete.

**What this PR adds**
- `SoftDeleteMixin` in `superset/models/helpers.py`:
  - Nullable, indexed `deleted_at` `DateTime` column
  - `soft_delete(when=None)` — idempotent; does not overwrite an existing timestamp
  - `restore()` — clears `deleted_at`
  - `is_deleted` property
  - `not_deleted()` classmethod returning `cls.deleted_at.is_(None)` for use in query filters
- Mixin attached to `Slice`, `Dashboard`, and `SqlaTable`
- Alembic migration `b7a2e9d4f1c8` (down-rev: `ce6bd21901ab`) adding `deleted_at` + `ix_<table>_deleted_at` index to `slices`, `dashboards`, `tables` via the shared `add_columns` / `create_index` / `drop_columns` / `drop_index` helpers in `superset.migrations.shared.utils`

**What this PR intentionally does NOT do — tracked as follow-ups per the SIP "Notes for the Automation Pipeline":**
- DAO routing in `BaseDAO.delete()` to branch to `soft_delete()` vs `hard_delete()`
- Global `do_orm_execute` visibility filter (`WHERE deleted_at IS NULL`) + `skip_visibility_filter` escape hatch
- `RestoreChartCommand` / `RestoreDashboardCommand` / `RestoreDatasetCommand`
- `POST /api/v1/{chart,dashboard,dataset}/<pk>/restore` endpoints
- `include_deleted=true` list parameter
- Import/export pipeline changes to use `skip_visibility_filter`
- Dashboard-slice association hard-delete on chart soft-delete
- Any permanent-delete (`DELETE /api/v1/{entity}/<pk>/permanent`) API

**SIP Open Questions resolved in this increment (committed by naming):**
1. **Naming** — committed to `deleted_at` / `soft_delete()` / `restore()` / `/restore` (not `archived_at` / `archive()` / `unarchive()`)
2. **First-increment scope** — mixin + Alembic migration only; DAO routing, global filter, restore endpoints, `include_deleted`, and hard-delete API are explicitly out of scope for this PR

**SIP Open Questions still deferred (need human design sign-off before follow-up PRs):**
- Whether listing soft-deleted entities uses an `include_deleted=true` query param, a dedicated `/trash` endpoint, or an admin-only UI
- Permissions model: whether restore needs a distinct permission from delete, whether only admins should see soft-deleted rows, and whether to expose an explicit `DELETE /api/v1/{entity}/<pk>/permanent` for GDPR / storage management

This fork is tracking the upstream SIP — this PR explicitly does not lock in broader API behavior beyond this additive column.

### BEFORE/AFTER SCREENSHOTS OR ANIMATED GIF

N/A — no UI changes. This PR ships a column + mixin + migration only.

### TESTING INSTRUCTIONS

Validation was run locally against the repo's pinned deps (`requirements/base.txt` + `requirements/development.txt`, SQLAlchemy 1.4.54, alembic 1.15.2).

#### Scanner receipts (feature-absence → feature-present)

`scanner_before` — on `main`, the feature is not present; the committed test fails to import the missing mixin:

```
$ git checkout main -- superset/models/helpers.py superset/models/slice.py superset/models/dashboard.py superset/connectors/sqla/models.py
$ python -m pytest tests/unit_tests/models/test_soft_delete_mixin.py -x --no-header
...
E   ImportError: cannot import name 'SoftDeleteMixin' from 'superset.models.helpers'
exit code: 2
```

`scanner_after` — on this branch, 8/8 mixin unit tests pass:

```
$ python -m pytest tests/unit_tests/models/test_soft_delete_mixin.py -xvs
tests/unit_tests/models/test_soft_delete_mixin.py::test_deleted_at_column_is_nullable_and_defaults_to_none PASSED
tests/unit_tests/models/test_soft_delete_mixin.py::test_deleted_at_column_is_indexed PASSED
tests/unit_tests/models/test_soft_delete_mixin.py::test_soft_delete_sets_deleted_at_to_a_recent_timestamp PASSED
tests/unit_tests/models/test_soft_delete_mixin.py::test_soft_delete_accepts_explicit_timestamp PASSED
tests/unit_tests/models/test_soft_delete_mixin.py::test_soft_delete_is_idempotent PASSED
tests/unit_tests/models/test_soft_delete_mixin.py::test_restore_clears_deleted_at PASSED
tests/unit_tests/models/test_soft_delete_mixin.py::test_not_deleted_filter_excludes_soft_deleted_rows PASSED
tests/unit_tests/models/test_soft_delete_mixin.py::test_mixin_does_not_auto_hide_rows_from_unfiltered_queries PASSED
======================== 8 passed in 1.03s =========================
```

The last test is an explicit regression guard: it asserts that attaching `SoftDeleteMixin` alone does **not** install a global visibility filter, since that is deferred to a follow-up.

#### Alembic upgrade / downgrade / re-upgrade smoke test against a fresh SQLite DB

body:
### Motivation

- Primary cards were rendering lyric text twice because the DOM `LyricTextLayer` sat above the canvas output and used a fade animation, hiding the canvas text fixes. 
- The `ownsText` prop existed but only set a `data-*` attribute and did not prevent DOM rendering, so engine-side canvas improvements were invisible to users. 
- The intended behavior is that canvas is the single source of truth for primary cards and DOM is only a stand-in while the canvas player boots. 

### Description

- `LyricDanceEmbed` now passes a dynamic ownership flag to the text layer via `ownsText={!live || !playerReady}`, so DOM text is only rendered when not live or before the player is ready. 
- `LyricTextLayer` gates the phrase render on `ownsText` by changing the render test to `{ownsText && phraseText && (...)}`, while keeping the outer wrapper and `AnimatePresence` mounted for a clean exit animation. 
- `useLyricTextFit` input is short-circuited to a minimal placeholder when `ownsText` is false to avoid unnecessary fit calculations. 

### Testing

- Ran `npm run test` which completed but reported one unrelated unit test failure in `src/test/phraseAnimator.test.ts`.

body:
The original implementation silently returned None when torchaudio failed to load audio from BytesIO (common with MP3/WAV from URLs). This caused downstream nodes like FalLipsyncV3 to crash with 'NoneType object is not subscriptable'.

Fix: try 4 methods in order:
1. torchaudio from temp file on disk
2. torchaudio from BytesIO with explicit format detection
3. soundfile (handles WAV/FLAC/OGG)
4. ffmpeg subprocess conversion to WAV

Also: raise errors instead of silently returning None.

author: messense
body:
Fixes #3142.

## Problem

Since maturin 1.13.0, conditional `pyo3/abi3` features gated on `python-version` in `pyproject.toml` were applied unconditionally during bridge detection. This caused builds to fail when the target interpreter didn't match the condition:

```
💥 maturin failed
  Caused by: None of the found Python interpreters (CPython 3.10) are compatible
  with the abi3 minimum version (>= 3.11).
```

## Solution

Split bridge detection into two phases:

1. **`find_bridge()`** — detects the bridge model from Cargo metadata only, excluding conditional pyproject features. The `pyproject` parameter is removed since it's no longer needed here.

2. **`upgrade_bridge_abi3()`** — after interpreter resolution, evaluates conditional `pyo3`/`pyo3-ffi` features against the resolved interpreters using `matches_any` semantics, upgrading the bridge to abi3 if any interpreter qualifies.

The `matches_any` approach is safe because `build_stable_abi_wheels` already splits interpreters into abi3-capable vs version-specific groups by `min_version`, producing e.g. `cp310 + abi3-cp311` for mixed `[3.10, 3.11]`.

## Additional fixes

- Skip conditional pyproject features when CLI `--features` overrides pyproject features, keeping bridge detection in sync with compile-time feature resolution.
- Move bridge binding log messages from `find_bridge()` to the builder so they print once after the final bridge is resolved.

## Validation

- `cargo test --lib test_find_bridge_ -- --nocapture` (6 tests including new conditional abi3 test)
- Manual verification: `>=3.15` with Python 3.14 produces `cp314` wheel (no abi3); `>=3.11` with Python 3.14 produces `abi3-cp311` wheel

author: afadesigns
body:
ZC1653 — Avoid `$BASHPID` — Bash-only; Zsh uses `$sysparams[pid]` from `zsh/system`

What: flags arguments referencing `$BASHPID` / `${BASHPID}`.
Why: `$BASHPID` returns the current subshell's PID (while `$$` returns the parent shell's PID). Zsh does not set this parameter — scripts silently read empty and misbehave.
Fix suggestion: `zmodload zsh/system` once, then read `$sysparams[pid]` — updates inside subshells the same way.
Severity: Warning
