author: kfly8
body:
## Summary

Implements v0 of #887 — browser edits-to-reload, adapter-agnostic.

- `barefoot build --watch` drops `<outDir>/.dev/build-id` after every successful build that changed output on disk. No write on errored or no-op rebuilds.
- `@barefootjs/hono/dev` exports `createDevReloader({ distDir })` (a Hono SSE handler that watches the sentinel and emits `event: reload`) and `BfDevReload` (an inline `<script>` EventSource subscriber that reloads on `reload` and preserves `window.scrollY` via `sessionStorage`).
- `examples/hono` wires both pieces: `app.get('/_bf/reload', createDevReloader({ distDir: './dist' }))` and `<BfDevReload />` inside the shared layout.

Both pieces are gated on `NODE_ENV !== 'production'` by default (override via the `enabled` option) — production builds don't register the route or emit the client snippet.

## Design notes

- **Sentinel file over HTTP IPC**: the builder never touches HTTP (matches the "any backend" design). Dev servers — one per adapter — convert the filesystem event to SSE.
- **5s heartbeat**: Bun.serve's default `idleTimeout` is 10s. Without periodic comment frames the SSE stream is silently closed, the browser EventSource-reconnects, and any `reload` fired in the close↔reconnect gap is lost.
- **`Last-Event-ID` recovery**: on reconnect, the handler compares the client's last-seen build-id against the current sentinel. If the client missed a build while disconnected, it gets `reload` (not `hello`) and refreshes instead of staying stuck on stale HTML.

## Scope

v0 Hono only, per #887. Go-template adapter will follow in a separate PR (`fsnotify` + `net/http` SSE with the same contract).

## Test plan

- [x] `bun test` passes in `packages/cli` (280) and `packages/hono` (69, +8 for new `dev.test.tsx` suite)
- [x] Manual: editing a shared `.tsx` while `bun run dev` runs in `examples/hono` triggers browser reload in <500ms
- [x] Manual: `curl -N http://localhost:3001/_bf/reload` stays open past 10s (heartbeat confirmed)
- [x] Manual: `curl -H "Last-Event-ID: 999"` on the reloader endpoint emits `event: reload` (regression-tested)
- [x] Manual: `NODE_ENV=production bun run server.tsx` → `/_bf/reload` returns 404 and pages no longer include the snippet
- [ ] Verify multi-tab reload on a fresh checkout (each tab opens its own EventSource, so broadcast is automatic by construction)

author: marius-bughiu
body:
## Summary

First slice of issue #10 (milestone 1.1.0): add struct-based, allocation-free enumeration to `IntDictionary<TValue, THasher>`. This is the prerequisite for implementing `IReadOnlyDictionary<int, TValue>` (issue #9).

- `IntDictionary.GetEnumerator()` returns a struct `Enumerator` yielding `KeyValuePair<int, TValue?>`. `foreach` over an `IntDictionary` no longer allocates an `IEnumerator<T>`.
- `IntDictionary.Keys` returns a readonly struct `KeyCollection` with its own struct enumerator.
- `IntDictionary.Values` returns a readonly struct `ValueCollection` with its own struct enumerator.
- The out-of-band zero-key entry is yielded first when present.
- A new `_version` counter is bumped on every structural mutation (indexer set, `Remove`, `TryAdd`, `Clear`). Enumerators snapshot the version on creation and throw `InvalidOperationException` from the next `MoveNext` / `Reset` if the dictionary is mutated mid-enumeration, matching BCL `Dictionary<,>` semantics.

`CelerityDictionary` will get the equivalent surface in a follow-up session; this PR is intentionally kept scoped to one dictionary so it lands cleanly.

## Test plan

New `IntDictionaryEnumerationTests.cs` covers:

- [x] Empty dictionary yields no entries.
- [x] Single-entry, many-entry, zero-key-only, and zero-key-included cases.
- [x] Enumeration reflects `Remove` and `Clear`.
- [x] Enumeration survives multiple resizes (200 inserts from capacity 4).
- [x] `MoveNext` throws `InvalidOperationException` on structural mutation (regular insert, zero-key insert, `Clear`).
- [x] `Reset` throws on mutation.
- [x] `Keys` and `Values` yield every key/value once, including the zero-key entry.
- [x] `Keys.Count` and `Values.Count` track the dictionary's count.
- [x] `IEnumerable<T>` path through `Keys` / `Values` behaves identically to the struct path.
- [x] Enumerator is reusable via `Reset`.

Local `dotnet build` + `dotnet test` — all 334 tests pass (20 new, 314 existing).

## Docs

- `CHANGELOG.md` — `[Unreleased] / Added` entry.
- `ISSUES.md` — #10 updated to `in-progress in 1.1.0`; milestone tag on #9 bumped from 0.3.0 to 1.1.0 to match the current roadmap.
- `docs/api/collections.md` — documented `Keys`, `Values`, `GetEnumerator()` and added a usage snippet.

author: houko
body:
## Summary
Follow-up to #2742. Codex review flagged a P2: `closeCreateModal()` was unconditionally calling `spawnMutation.reset()`, which flips `isPending` back to `false` even when the POST is still in flight. Since `spawnAgent` doesn't abort the fetch, a user who Cancels mid-flight and reopens the modal can re-enable the Create button and submit a second request before the first response lands — producing a duplicate-spawn "already exists" error, i.e. the exact bug #2741 was meant to eliminate.

Fix: gate the reset on `!spawnMutation.isPending`. The in-flight request keeps `isPending` true across reopens, so the Create button stays disabled until the original settles; the subsequent `onSuccess`/`onError` closes + toasts as usual. The stale-error-banner use case `reset()` was protecting is unaffected — by the time there's a banner to clear, the mutation has already settled.

## Test plan
- [x] `pnpm tsc --noEmit` — clean
- [x] `pnpm test` — 244/244 pass
- [ ] Manually: Create → Cancel mid-flight → Reopen → Create button stays disabled until original settles; no duplicate request

author: extratoast
body:
## Summary

Two platform fixes so the cluster bring-up actually completes on a fresh deploy:

- **k3s flannel over Tailscale** — frankfurt (public VPS) and Enschede LAN nodes could not exchange vxlan packets, so cross-site pod networking was silently broken. Pinning \`--flannel-iface=tailscale0\` and ordering k3s after \`tailscaled.service\` puts every node's flannel backend on the shared tailnet.
- **Layered Flux Kustomizations** — the single root Kustomization dry-runs every manifest, so CRs for Helm-installed CRDs (MetalLB IPAddressPool, cert-manager Certificate / ClusterIssuer, prometheus-operator PrometheusRule) blocked the chart releases that would install them. Split into one Kustomization CR per domain with \`dependsOn\` edges; extracted MetalLB/Prometheus CRs into their own dependent Kustomizations.

Also bumps pi-1 and t1000 inventory to \`status: active\` and pins enschede nodes to tailnet IPs (deploy-rs's resolver doesn't consult macOS MagicDNS).

## Test plan

- [x] Deploy applied to pi-1, t1000, and frankfurt — all three k3s services restarted cleanly.
- [x] Flannel on frankfurt now reports \`local 100.108.144.93 dev tailscale0\`.
- [x] Ping from frankfurt to CoreDNS pod IP (10.42.2.7) succeeds over the new vxlan path.
- [x] Flux \`GitRepository\` fetched \`main\` successfully after the flannel fix.
- [x] \`kubectl kustomize platform/cluster/flux/clusters/production\` renders the split Kustomization CRs and the relocated CR manifests.
- [ ] After merge: confirm \`flux get kustomizations -A\` shows apps-core Ready=True first, then downstream Kustomizations reconciling.

author: zhengjf123
body:
## Summary

This PR adds optional `flingSpeedLimit` prop support to `CalendarList`.

When `flingSpeedLimit` is explicitly provided, it is forwarded to the underlying `FlatList`. When it is not provided, `CalendarList` behavior remains unchanged.

## Why

Some React Native platform implementations support a `flingSpeedLimit` prop on `FlatList`. At the moment, `CalendarList` does not expose this prop, so passing it from the app layer has no effect.

This change allows consumers to opt in to that behavior without affecting existing users.

## What changed

- Added optional `flingSpeedLimit?: number` to `CalendarListProps`
- Forward `flingSpeedLimit` to the underlying `FlatList` only when explicitly provided
- Added `PropTypes.number` support for `flingSpeedLimit`
- Updated `calendarList.api.json` to document the prop

## Behavior

- No behavior change by default
- No effect when `flingSpeedLimit` is not passed
- Platforms that support this `FlatList` prop can make use of it
- Existing Android/iOS behavior remains unchanged unless consumers explicitly opt in

## Validation

- Verified the prop is conditionally forwarded only when provided
- Confirmed no lint errors in the modified files
- Type definition is included so TS consumers can use the prop directly

## Summary

**FAZ-C runtime closure 3. track.** Driver parent_env={} sabit'leri iki farklı güvenlik sınırıyla doldurulur. Codex plan consensus: 3 iter → AGREE (thread `019da01e`, plan sha `2b53664`) + post-impl AGREE (`6c06833`).

### Changes

1. **`_compute_adapter_parent_env(policy)`** — UNION `allowlist_secret_ids ∪ env_allowlist.allowed_keys`. Adapter runtime (codex-stub, claude-code-cli, gh-cli-pr) `GH_TOKEN`/`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` gibi secret'lara ihtiyaç duyar.

2. **`_compute_sandbox_parent_env(policy)`** — `env_allowlist.allowed_keys MINUS secret_ids` (structural set-difference guard). CI/patch subprocess'leri least-privilege — operator yanlışlıkla aynı key'i hem `allowlist_secret_ids` hem `env_allowlist.allowed_keys`'e koyarsa bile sandbox'a sızmaz.

3. **`_build_sandbox`** — `resolved_secrets: Mapping[str, str] = {}` **explicit in code**. Security intent data flow'dan okunur (convention değil). `resolve_allowed_secrets` çağrısı kaldırıldı.

4. **`build_driver(root, *, policy_loader=None)`** — `MultiStepDriver(..., policy_config=policy_loader)` forward. Single source of truth: hem Executor hem Driver aynı policy'yi görür (B2 coupling absorb).

## Security invariants

- **CI/patch sandbox** subprocess'leri `sandbox.env_vars`'ında `GH_TOKEN` yok (negatif test pinned).
- **Adapter sandbox** `parent_env`'inde `GH_TOKEN` VAR (positive test — `gh-cli-pr` authentication için gerekli).

Closes Fase E of the macOS / Apple Silicon port (milestones M22–M30).
Brings the Orbiter macOS port to **100% feature parity** with Windows
across UI, plugin support, distribution and CI:

* **M22 — Launchpad** (8 sub-milestones): full ImGui port of the 6
  Win32 tabs (Scenarios / Options / Modules / Video / Extra / About)
  with thumbnail loader, DESC/HYPERDESC parser, splitter,
  per-plugin `.info` sidecars, 12-page Options form, cross-platform
  `LaunchpadItem::clbkRender()` API and 15 built-in Extra items.
* **M22 follow-up** — bridges `Modules/lib<celbody>.dylib` →
  `Modules/Celbody/` so scenarios can dlopen planet plugins.
* **M23 — Dialogs F3-F10**: cross-platform `DlgHelp` URL fallback,
  `DlgOptions` SDL joystick enumeration, case-insensitive vessel
  cfg lookup helper. The 11 ImGui dialogs (DlgInfo, DlgMap,
  DlgCamera, ...) inherit from a shared `ImGuiDialog` base; F-key
  dispatch already wired in `KbdInputBuffered_System`.
* **M24 — gcGUI side bar**: cross-platform `Orbitersdk/include/gcGUI.h`
  with legacy HWND API + new `RegisterApplicationImGui` /
  `RegisterSubsectionImGui`. `OGLWindowMgr` backend, `gcGetGUICore()`
  resolved via `dlsym(RTLD_DEFAULT)` on POSIX. Smoke driver gated
  by `ORBITER_GCGUI_TEST=1`.
* **M25 — Win32 plugins port**: ScnEditor (3108 LOC) → ImGui front-end
  with State / Orientation / AngVel / Propellant / Date tabs;
  AtlantisConfig `clbkRender()` override; Meshdebug ImGui dialog;
  Rcontrol verified ImGui-native. TrackIR excluded macOS.
* **M26 — User paths + Keymap + Joystick calibration**:
  `UserPaths.{h,cpp}` redirects log + cfg to
  `~/Library/Application Support/Orbiter/` and
  `~/Library/Logs/Orbiter/`. New `OGLKeymapEditor` (visual US-ANSI

body:
## Story 76.1: Reproduce and Catalogue All Failing E2E Tests

Closes #1072

### Summary

Complete investigation of all E2E test failures across Chromium and Firefox browsers. This is an **investigation-only** story — no production code was changed.

### Results

| | Chromium | Firefox |
|---|---|---|
| **Passed** | 650 | 654 |
| **Failed** | 6 | 7 |
| **Flaky** | 7 | 2 |
| **Skipped** | 130 | 130 |

body:
## Summary
- remove verbose Fluent bridge diagnostics added for investigation
- keep one compact info log when operations are found
- fix intermittent L2 crash on import:
  - `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE command cannot affect row a second time`

## Root cause of crash
`fluent_bridge_operations` upsert uses conflict target `[:type, :message_hash]`.
Sometimes one insert batch contains duplicate keys, and Postgres rejects `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` when the same target row would be affected multiple times in one statement.

## Fix
In `Explorer.Chain.Import.Runner.Fluent.BridgeOperations.insert/3`:
- pre-deduplicate batch rows by `{type, message_hash}` before `insert_all`
- merge duplicate rows with "last non-nil wins" semantics (compatible with existing COALESCE upsert behavior)
- add warning log when duplicates are merged, with small duplicate-keys sample

## Kept operational log
`Fluent bridge events found. layer=<L1|L2> count=<n> sample=[...]`

Sample includes:
- type
- message_hash
- tx_hash
- block_number

## Validation
- `MIX_ENV=test TEST_DATABASE_URL=ecto://postgres:postgres@127.0.0.1:5432/explorer_test mix test apps/indexer/test/indexer/fetcher/fluent/bridge_test.exs`

body:
### Motivation
- Provide an implementation-ready, Shopify-style (public-event-model inspired) tracking architecture for our Medusa + Next.js stack that supports anonymous visitor tracking, identity stitching, attribution, lifecycle stages, and CRM sync while keeping raw event streams internal.
- Ensure the design is scalable and safe under load by using idempotent ingestion, async queue workers, debouncing, and minimal server overhead.
- Define concrete, ready-to-implement artifacts (Next.js client code, Medusa module/services/subscribers, DB schema, API contracts, and rollout phases) so engineers can implement incrementally without guessing connector behavior.

### Description
- Added a comprehensive guide at `backend/docs/shopify-style-customer-tracking.md` covering system design, Next.js client TypeScript examples for `anonymous_id`/`session_id`/UTM capture/`page_view`/`engaged_visit_5s` and Medusa module patterns (service, subscribers, jobs, idempotent ingest).
- Specified the `customer-journey` module design including entities (`journey_visitor`, `journey_session`, `journey_event`, `journey_customer_rollup`, `journey_identity_link`, `journey_crm_sync_log`), services (`JourneyIngestService`, `JourneyIdentityService`, `JourneyCrmSyncService`), subscribers for `customer.created`, `order.placed`, `payment.captured`, and a `crm-sync-contact` job.
- Included exact field schemas for visitor/session/attribution/rollups, an event taxonomy with dedupe keys, API payload examples (`/store/journey/events`, `/store/journey/identify`), database indexes, and recommended safety/scalability patterns (idempotency keys, batching, TTL/partitioning, DLQ).
- Provided a three-phase rollout plan (foundation, truth & stitching, CRM & optimization) and SQL/reporting guidance for funnel and revenue attribution views.

### Testing

## v1.5.0

### Added

- Introducing the new **Game Mode**! A cross between a classic roleplay and a visual novel, fully driven by the AI GM! Embark on adventures either solo or with a party of characters of your choice. Or perhaps have one of your characters DM the game for you and others? The games span multiple sessions, and *anything* can happen. The sky is the limit. Well, I guess your wallet, too.
  - Follow an easy and quick game setup wizard to customize your game, or ask the model to come up with the ideas for you.
  - The game's UI is a cross between RPGs (think Baldur's Gate) and visual novels. Witness dynamically changing dialogues, backgrounds, sprites, ambiance, music, sounds, and weather; all based on your current scene. The mode supports sprites and will show them with different expressions. You have an item inventory, an automatically updated journal storing information about your adventure, and an option to talk to your party whenever you feel like simply chatting with them instead of progressing.

  - Do dice rolls yourself or let the GM handle those for you.
  - Play with the interactive widgets, travel to different locations via a map, build a reputation with NPCs and factions, and explore a dynamically changing world.

## Summary

author: ratish1
body:
## Motivation

Fixes #293.

This PR removes the hidden omni AR `mem_fraction_static=0.7` product default and lets SGLang choose the hardware-aware value when the user does not pin one. Manual override support remains available for the SGLang AR stages that own weights + KV cache.

## Modifications

- Changed `build_sglang_server_args()` so `mem_fraction_static=None` is omitted from `ServerArgs`, allowing upstream SGLang to run its auto-sizing path. Explicit user-pinned values are still forwarded unchanged.
- Added an omni thinker auto-path reserve for Qwen/Ming encoder-bearing thinker GPUs. SGLang's generic VLM reserve only handles top-level `vision_config`; SGLang-Omni runs vision/audio encoder stages outside the SGLang thinker process, so the thinker builders apply a small AR-only reserve after SGLang computes the raw auto value.
- Kept `mem_fraction_static` scoped to SGLang AR stages: Qwen `thinker`, Qwen `talker_ar`, and Ming `thinker`. Ming `talker`, Qwen `code2wav`, and the vision/audio encoders do not expose a SGLang KV pool; Qwen `code_predictor` uses a lightweight direct executor path and is intentionally left outside the public mem-fraction API.
- Moved mem-fraction role mapping out of instance schema data. `MemFractionOverrideStages` and `PipelineConfig.apply_mem_fraction_static_overrides(...)` were removed; pipeline classes now expose a class-level `mem_fraction_role_to_stage()` capability and call sites use the existing `apply_server_args_overrides(stage_name=..., overrides=...)` primitive.
- Inlined CLI/example range validation and precedence resolution at the call sites. `examples/_mem_fraction_cli.py` and the `apply_thinker_server_args_overrides(...)` method family were deleted.

author: raghavyuva
body:
## Summary

- **Root cause fixed:** `AddCustomDomain` previously required a nixopus-assigned subdomain, causing BYOS (user-owned) machines to fail with "no subdomain configured". BYOS machines have `subdomain = NULL` in `user_provision_details`.
- **BYOS sentinel:** `net.ParseIP(targetSubdomain) != nil` is used consistently across all three service methods to distinguish BYOS (IP stored in `target_subdomain`) from managed (nixopus subdomain) machines — no schema changes needed.
- **Managed path is byte-for-byte unchanged** below each BYOS early-return.

## Changes

### `dns_detection.go`
- Added `GenerateDNSInstructionsBYOS(domain, machineIP, provider)` — returns a single A record instruction pointing the domain to the machine IP (no CNAME, no TXT).

### `dns_verification.go`
- Added `VerifyARecordMatchesMachineIP(domain, machineIP)` — checks DNS resolves to the exact machine IP.
- Added `CheckDNSPropagationBYOS(domain, machineIP)` — returns `verified` / `propagating` / `not_configured`.

### `custom_domains.go`
- `AddCustomDomain`: BYOS branch resolves machine IP via `resolveMachineIP` (prefers `GuestIP`, falls back to `ssh_keys.host`), stores IP in `target_subdomain`, returns A-record instructions.
- `VerifyCustomDomain`: routes to `VerifyARecordMatchesMachineIP` when `target_subdomain` is an IP; managed path unchanged.
- `CheckDNSStatus`: same BYOS sentinel routing.
- Added `resolveMachineIP` helper.

## Test plan

- [ ] Set `guest_ip` for a BYOS org's provision row and call `POST /api/v1/domain/custom` — response must show an A record instruction (not CNAME), pointing to machine IP
- [ ] Point domain A record to machine IP, then call `POST /api/v1/domain/verify` — expect `{"status":"dns_verified"}`
- [ ] Call `GET /api/v1/domain/status` before DNS propagates — expect `propagating`, after — expect `verified`
- [ ] Add a domain for a managed org — instructions must still show CNAME to `abc123.nixopus.ai`

## Notes

- Auth service (`nixopus-auth`) has a companion commit that populates `guest_ip` on `user_provision_details` at BYOS registration time, so the fallback to `ssh_keys.host` is rarely needed.
- No schema changes, no new env vars, no queue handler changes.

author: kaosbr
body:
**🎯 What:** 
Bare `except:` clauses were used in `src/db_manager.py` within `add_message`, `get_messages`, and `clear_session`.

**⚠️ Risk:** 
Using bare `except:` catches all exceptions, including critical system ones like `SystemExit`, `KeyboardInterrupt`, and `MemoryError`. This practice can silently swallow fatal errors, hide bugs, and make the application unresponsive to termination signals, presenting significant operational and security risks.

**🛡️ Solution:** 
Replaced bare `except:` with `except Exception as e:` and added descriptive error logging to `sys.stderr` in English for consistency. This explicitly catches standard runtime errors without masking essential system exceptions.

## Summary
Config-driven derived categories — replaces the two hard-coded `if slug === "mattresses-sale"` branches in the shop PLP with declarative `ShopCategory` config. - `sourceSlug` — Wix collection to source products from when different from the URL slug (derived categories).

body:
Addresses the CodeQL "Statement has no effect" cluster in torment_service/agent_loop.py. One true site in the file:

  `_ = ctx  # silence unused-arg lint until emission logic lands`

inside the `assimilation_outcomes()` stub. The statement existed only to quiet linter warnings while the v0.1 stub deliberately returns `[]`; the function remains the doctrine-documented insertion point for future WRITE_MEMORY / PROPOSE_SHARE / CREATE_ARCHIVE_NOTE emission rules.

Fix:
- Rename the parameter `ctx` -> `_ctx`, using Python's native leading-underscore convention for intentionally-unused parameters. This preserves the TurnContext type contract and the function signature is the permanent interface; the rename makes the "unused by design for now" intent explicit without needing a lint-suppression marker.
- Remove the no-effect `_ = ctx` assignment.

The five `...` literals inside `FabricHandle`, `LLMClient`, and `ToolExecutor` Protocol method bodies are intentionally left untouched. They are the PEP 544 convention for abstract method stubs in `typing.Protocol` classes and are not typically flagged by CodeQL's `py/ineffectual-statement` rule.

Guardrails
----------
- Docstring and all inline comments unchanged.
- Function still returns `[]` — no emission rules introduced.
- No doctrine, no policy, no runner flow changes.
- All callers (`agent_loop.py:517` and `tests/test_assimilation_outcomes_not_deliberative.py:139`) use positional invocation, so parameter rename is safe.

author: cmtalleyrand
body:
### Motivation
- The existing tonal inversion mirrored chromatic offsets across the diatonic degree axis, which could map non-diatonic (chromatic) input notes to diatonic outputs and break the invariant “chromatic pitch in → chromatic pitch out”.
- The intent is to keep diatonic inversion semantics for in-scale notes while ensuring chromatic notes are mirrored against a chromatic lattice centered on the pivot.

### Description
- Implemented a chromatic-lattice inversion path for non-diatonic pitches by adding helper functions: `getChromaticSemitones`, `getChromaticGlobalIndex`, `getPitchFromChromaticGlobalIndex`, `getChromaticMirrorAxis`, and `floorDiv`, and integrating them into `getInvertedPitch` in `components/services/strettoCore.ts`.
- Behavior: if a pitch is non-diatonic relative to the active scale, it is mapped to a chromatic global index (rank within the chromatic semitone class plus octave), mirrored around a pivot-derived chromatic axis (`mirroredIndex = round(2*axis - index)`), and reconstructed back to a MIDI pitch; in-scale pitches still use the original diatonic-degree reflection and preserved chromatic offsets.
- The new chromatic path uses small fixed-size arrays (≤12 semitone classes) and constant-time arithmetic, so runtime cost is negligible and does not change algorithmic complexity of `getInvertedPitch`.
- Added a focused regression test file `components/services/strettoCoreInversion.test.ts` that asserts the C-major chromatic subject inversion around `C4`, closure of chromatic→chromatic mapping, and local symmetry for the G pivot (`#4 ↔ b6`).

### Testing
- Ran the regression assertions with `node --import tsx components/services/strettoCoreInversion.test.ts`, which printed a success message and passed.
- Performed a production build with `npm run build`, which completed successfully (Vite build finished without errors).
- The change keeps the diatonic inversion code path intact and the added test exercises the new chromatic path; no automated test failures were observed.

author: copilot
body:
## Description

Fixes database authentication failure by URL-encoding the PostgreSQL administrator credentials when building the connection string stored in Key Vault.

## Related Issue

The vaultwarden container logs show repeated `FATAL: password authentication failed for user "vaultwardenadmin"` errors after deployment, even though the PostgreSQL server is created successfully with the correct password.

## Changes

- URL-encode the `administratorLogin` and `administratorLoginPassword` using Bicep's `uriComponent()` function in the PostgreSQL connection string (`bicep/modules/postgresql.bicep`)

### Root Cause

The connection string is a URL of the form:
```
postgresql://user:password@host:5432/dbname?sslmode=require
```

If the password (or username) contains characters with special meaning in URLs (e.g., `@`, `#`, `/`, `%`, `?`, `:`), the connection string gets malformed. For example, a `@` in the password would be interpreted as the end of the credentials section, sending a truncated/wrong password to PostgreSQL.

### Fix

Using `uriComponent()` ensures all special characters are percent-encoded before being embedded in the URL, so the full password is correctly transmitted to the database server.

author: revprism-dev-bot
body:
## Summary
- Parser (`parseHookLogLine`) previously split the tail of every hooks.log line on a single whitespace, so a value like `reason="rm -rf at root"` was truncated to `reason="rm`. This surfaced through `hooks audit-guardrails` (PR #44) as broken `sample_reason` output for the false-positive reviewer.
- Fix pairs a quote-aware tokenizer on the reader side with `strconv.Quote` semantics on the writer side. Simple values still emit as literal `k=v` (load-bearing for downstream greps and existing Windows-path negative-case tests); values with whitespace, quotes, or control chars round-trip losslessly via `strconv.Quote` / `strconv.Unquote`.
- Malformed lines (unterminated quote) degrade gracefully: the parser logs a warning, keeps every field parsed before the malformed token, and never panics.

## Quoting protocol
- Writer emits `k=v` unchanged when `v` has no whitespace, quote, or control byte.
- Writer emits `k="..."` via `strconv.Quote` otherwise. Backslash-only values (e.g. `foo\bar`) remain literal for backwards compatibility with the Windows-path negative-case tests.
- Reader uses `strconv.Unquote` for quoted values; on decode failure it falls back to stripping quote bytes so fields are never dropped.

## Files touched
- `internal/heimdall/hooklog.go` — writer: introduced `needsQuoting`, switched quoting to `strconv.Quote`.
- `internal/heimdall/hooklog_reader.go` — reader: added `splitKVTokens` + `unquoteValue`, rewired `parseHookLogLine`.
- `internal/heimdall/hooklog_test.go` — writer tests (protocol table, simple-value canary, space/quote cases).
- `internal/heimdall/hooklog_reader_test.go` — reader tests (simple-value canary, quoted/escaped/unterminated), seven-case round-trip.
- `internal/cli/hooks_audit_test.go` — regression assertion that a multi-word reason survives through to the rendered audit report.

## Test plan
- [x] `go build ./...`
- [x] `go vet ./...`
- [x] `go test ./... -race -count=1` (all packages green)
- [x] New writer tests: `TestRedactLogString_QuotingProtocol`, `TestLogHookEvent_SimpleValueUnquoted`, `TestLogHookEvent_ValueWithSpaceQuoted`, `TestLogHookEvent_ValueWithEmbeddedQuoteEscaped`.
- [x] New reader tests: `TestParseHookLogLine_QuotedValueWithSpaces`, `TestParseHookLogLine_EscapedQuoteInsideValue`, `TestParseHookLogLine_UnterminatedQuoteDegradesCleanly`, `TestParseHookLogLine_SimpleValuesUnchanged`.

author: zvdy
body:
Closes #2. Partially addresses #6.

## Summary

`FileStore.getFilePath` joined `baseDir`, `namespace`, and `name` with no validation, so a namespace like `"../etc"` would write to `/etc` instead of `/data/etc`. The admin token-creation endpoint accepts arbitrary namespace strings, so any token holder could escape the data directory. This PR rejects malformed inputs and verifies the cleaned path stays under `baseDir` as defense in depth.

## Changes

- New helper `validateName` rejects empty strings, `.`, `..`, path separators, and NUL bytes; applied to both namespace and name in `MemoryStore` and `FileStore`.
- New helpers `FileStore.resolvePath` / `resolveNamespaceDir` clean the joined path and assert it stays under `baseDir` via `filepath.Rel`.
- Sentinel errors `storage.ErrNotFound` and `storage.ErrInvalidName` exported and wrapped at all error sites — callers can now use `errors.Is`.
- File permissions tightened from `0644`/`0755` to `0600`/`0700`.

## Tests (TDD)

- `TestFileStorePathTraversalRejected` — drives Store/Get/Delete with payloads `..`, `../etc`, `../../etc`, `ns/sub`, `""`, `.`, `..`, `\x00`. Each must error and a sentinel file outside `baseDir` must be untouched.
- `TestFileStoreListPathTraversalRejected` — same coverage for `List`.
- `TestMemoryStoreRejectsInvalidNames` — keeps the in-memory backend consistent.
- `TestStoreNotFound` / `TestFileStoreNotFoundIsSentinel` — assert `errors.Is(err, ErrNotFound)`.
- `TestStoreConcurrent` — exercises concurrent access under `-race`.

All tests pass under `go test -race ./internal/storage/...`.

## Risk / compatibility

- Existing valid namespace/config names continue to work.
- Stricter file permissions (`0600`) may surface in environments that relied on world-readable config files.

Mirrors tr L-3 (PR #33). fp/fp_param_registry.f90 (new) has a SELECT CASE setter table for ~40 namelist names. fp/fp_api.f90 L-2 stubs are replaced with real wiring: fp_init runs mtx_initialize+pl_init+eq_init+ob_init+Fortran fp_init; fp_set_param dispatches to fp_param_set; fp_run wraps fp_prep+fp_loop with NTMAX=N; fp_get_state populates scalars and profile arrays matching fpregress.f90; fp_finalize clears flags (does NOT call fp_deallocate — fp_allocate guards some arrays with MODEL_DISRUPT but fp_deallocate is unconditional; fpmain never calls fp_deallocate either). > Medium risk because it introduces a new C-callable execution path that drives real initialization, parameter mutation, and simulation stepping against shared FPCOMM globals, which could surface lifecycle/parameter edge cases despite not changing the existing `fp` binary build.

> Adds Phase L-3 functional C ABI support for FP by replacing the previous stubbed `fp_api` entry points with real wiring to the full initialization stack (`mtx_initialize`/`pl_init`/`eq_init`/`ob_init`/`fp_init`), a `fp_run` path that calls `fp_prep`+`fp_loop`, and a `fp_get_state` implementation that exports key scalars plus profile arrays from FPCOMM.

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

Implement the RedScan project in `HanuTyagi/RedScan` as a production-grade, conference-demo-ready Python system following the provided architecture/methodology paper, with a fully functional non-simulated scanning pipeline (except external LLM APIs which must be mocked/pluggable), and robust tests/docs.

## Goal
Build the full core system with these functional layers:
1. Smart Scan Module (adaptive discovery + deep enumeration handoff)
2. Wrapped Commands and Preset Manager (expert presets + conflict resolution)
3. Command Factory Engine (node/graph-based scan command construction)
4. Real-Time Data Parser (non-blocking async scan execution and incremental parsing)
5. LLM Semantic Analysis Layer (fully implemented pipeline with provider abstraction; NO real external API dependency yet)

The final result must be runnable and demonstrable end-to-end locally and suitable for conference showcase.

---

## Mandatory technical stack
- Python 3.11+
- FastAPI for service/API layer
- asyncio for background execution/streaming
- pydantic for typed schemas/config models
- networkx for graph-based command factory
- pytest for tests

If the repository already contains code, preserve and evolve it unless clearly obsolete.

---

## Architecture and module requirements

### A) Smart Scan Module (fully functional; no simulation)
Implement a real scanner pipeline in Python that performs:

1. **Discovery pass with adaptive rate control**
   - Use concurrent TCP connect-based probing (native socket connections / asyncio open_connection with timeout control) for target hosts/ports.
   - Include interleaved calibration probes to a reliable calibration endpoint (host:port expected open), approximately 1 calibration probe per N target probes (N configurable, default 256).
   - Gather calibration RTT samples continuously.
   - Use EWMA smoothing: `rtt_filtered = (1-alpha)*prev + alpha*sample`.
   - Compute target RTT: `rtt_target = rtt_base + delta`, where `rtt_base` is min filtered RTT in initial calibration period.
   - Compute error `e(t) = rtt_target - rtt_filtered(t)`.
   - Implement **incremental/velocity PID** update per control interval Ts:
     - `delta_u = Kp*(e(t)-e(t-1)) + Ki*e(t) + Kd*(e(t)-2e(t-1)+e(t-2))`
   - Rate update with clipping bounds [R_min, R_max].
   - Hybrid AIMD loss-event backoff:
     - Sliding window W seconds and threshold m timeouts define loss event.
     - On loss event: `R <- beta * R` (0<beta<1), and reset PID error history to avoid derivative kick.
   - Add optional pacing mechanism (token bucket or equivalent) to reduce burstiness inside each control window.
   - Track key telemetry: RTT stats, timeout events, current rate, inter-probe-gap CV.

2. **Handoff to deep enumeration**
   - After discovery, compute and persist recommended Nmap rate params (`--min-rate`, `--max-rate`) derived from stabilized controller rate.
   - Build and execute Nmap deep scan command targeting only discovered open ports/hosts (service/version + optional scripts).
   - Capture Nmap XML output path and raw stdout/stderr.

3. **Safety and operational controls**
   - Enforce explicit target allowlist / guardrails where appropriate in config.
   - Respect configurable scan limits/timeouts/concurrency caps.

Implementation note: do not use fake scan data. This must perform real network probing/execution on provided targets in local/demo environments.

### B) Wrapped Commands & Preset Manager
Implement a preset system with serialized data models (YAML/JSON) for categories:
- Evasion and Stealth
- Vulnerability Discovery
- Industrial Control Systems
- Web Application Enumeration

Provide:
- Data schema for preset definition (flags, scripts, args, incompatibilities, required args, safety level).
- API/CLI to list presets, inspect preset, and generate command.
- Conflict resolution subroutine/rule-engine to detect mutually exclusive flags and invalid combinations.
- Include concrete conflict examples such as fragmentation with incompatible scan types; ensure resulting command is syntactically valid.

### C) Command Factory Engine (node-based orchestration backend)
Implement graph-driven command composition backend (UI not required, backend must be production-ready):
- Node types: TargetSpecification, HostDiscovery, PortSpecification, EvasionTechnique, ServiceDetection, ScriptSelection, OutputFormatting, Timing.
- Represent graph in `networkx` DAG (validate acyclic and required node ordering/dependencies).
- Parse node properties and compile deterministic, syntactically valid Nmap command string.
- Provide import/export JSON schema for graph definitions.
- Add validation rules and meaningful error messages for missing required node properties or invalid edge logic.

### D) Real-Time Data Parser + Async Execution Engine
Implement non-blocking execution:
- Run scan subprocess asynchronously (Nmap XML stream or periodic XML file updates, depending on mode).
- Incrementally parse host/port/service info while scan is running.

author: tosha
body:
Field bug: a user's game UI had a ~5px red decorative strip between the nickname and the actual HP bar. HpBarDetector found that strip first (5 rows >= MinBarRows=3) and returned it, so the stored 'HP region' captured the decoration instead of the bar. Runtime analysis then read a nonsense value (~20% HP) while the game showed full HP.

Diagnosed via v0.1.9's rich capture report — the saved PNG obviously wasn't a clean HP bar, and the match map [  .#..##############.  ] showed the fill pattern wrapping around rather than extending solidly across the region width.

Fix: walk every contiguous coloured row-run in the selection and keep the tallest one (ties resolve to the topmost, preserving the HP-on-top convention). The actual HP bar is always the thickest horizontal colour element in a sensible name+bar selection, so tallest-wins is robust to decorative chrome above or below.

Existing tests unchanged:
  - FindTopBar_StandardLayout_ReturnsBarRows (single bar)
  - FindTopBar_NoColouredBand_ReturnsNull
  - FindTopBar_PicksFirstBarWhenMultipleBarsPresent (equal heights -> topmost tie-break, same as before)
  - FindTopBar_ShortSpuriousBand_IsIgnored

New test:

author: copilot
body:
Adds support for connecting to the rotator over a remote RFC 2217 serial server (e.g. MikroTik IP/Serial) in addition to local serial ports, selected via a URL-style `ROTATOR_DEVICE` value.

## Transport layer

- **URL detection**: `rfc2217://host:port` → RFC 2217 over TCP; plain path → local `tokio-serial`
- **`Rfc2217Connection`**: minimal Telnet/COM-PORT-OPTION client — negotiates `IAC WILL/DO COM_PORT_OPTION` on connect, strips/handles inline IAC sequences (`DO`/`WILL`/`WONT`/`DONT`/`SB`) transparently during reads, escapes `0xFF` on writes
- **Auto-reconnect**: exponential back-off (1 s → 30 s cap) on any TCP drop; retries indefinitely on both initial connect and mid-operation failures

```sh
ROTATOR_DEVICE=rfc2217://192.168.1.1:2217 ./target/release/pwn-rotator
```

## Async refactor

- Switched local serial from `serialport` (sync) to `tokio-serial` (`SerialStream: AsyncRead + AsyncWrite`)
- `Connection::Local` wraps `SerialStream` in a persistent `BufReader` to avoid discarding inter-call buffered bytes
- All `Rotator` methods are now `async`; `spawn_blocking` removed from route handlers

author: keyur279
body:
Adding clear signing support for 4 HYSP vault functions on Ethereum mainnet. Each function has a unique 4-byte selector (calculated from keccak256(functionSignature)[0:4]). The firmware reads these selectors from the transaction's data field to identify which function is being called, then parses the arguments and displays human-readable information to the user.
The 4 functions:
1. approve(address,uint256) - Selector: 0x095ea7b3
    * Standard ERC-20 function (not HYSP-specific)
    * Gives a vault permission to spend tokens from user's wallet
    * 2 args: spender address (who can spend), amount (how much they can spend)
    * Used twice: once for USDC→vault, once for mevUSD→vault
2. depositInstant(address,uint256,uint256,bytes32) - Selector: 0xc02dd27a
    * Midas-specific function on Issuance Vault
    * Deposits tokens (USDC/USDT) and receives mevUSD
    * 4 args: tokenIn (which token depositing), amount, minReceive (slippage protection), referrerId (for tracking)
3. redeemInstant(address,uint256,uint256) - Selector: 0x8b53f75e
    * Midas-specific function on Redemption Vault
    * Burns mevUSD and receives tokens back (USDC/USDT) with 0.5% fee
    * 3 args: tokenOut (which token to receive), amount (mevUSD burning), minReceive (slippage protection)
4. redeemRequest(address,uint256) - Selector: 0xbfc2d46a
    * Midas-specific function on Redemption Vault
    * Queued redemption (no fee, ~24-48hr wait)
    * 2 args: tokenOut, amount
Key contract addresses:
* USDC: 0xa0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 (6 decimals)
* USDT: 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 (6 decimals)
* mevUSD: 0x548857309BEfb6Fb6F20a9C5A56c9023D892785B (18 decimals)
* Midas Issuance Vault: 0x5455222CCDd32F85C1998f57DC6CF613B4498C2a
* Midas Redemption Vault: 0x9C3743582e8b2d7cCb5e08caF3c9C33780ac446f

author: sseok-lee
body:
## 증상

Sync Real Estate Data #27 로그에서 다음 에러 반복 발생:

\`\`\`
[REMAINING] 동기화 실패: PrismaClientValidationError:
Invalid `prisma.subscriptionCompetition.upsert()` invocation:
Argument \`modelNo\` is missing.
\`\`\`

## 원인

공공데이터 청약 경쟁률/당첨 가점 API가 \`rank=0\`, \`regionCode=\"00\"\` 같은 **평형 구분 없는 집계 행**을 \`MODEL_NO\` 없이 내려주는 경우가 있음.

Prisma 모델 \`SubscriptionCompetition\`의 composite unique key \`subscriptionId_modelNo_rank_regionCode\`가 \`modelNo\`를 필수로 요구 → \`undefined\` 값이 들어가 validation error.

## 변경

backend/src/scripts/syncSubscription.ts:
- 경쟁률 upsert 루프: \`!item.MODEL_NO\`인 경우 skip
- 당첨 가점 upsert 루프: \`!item.MODEL_NO || !item.RESIDE_SECD\`인 경우 skip (둘 다 composite key)
- 완료 로그에 \`(필드 누락 스킵: N건)\` 표시 추가 → 데이터 소실 추적 가능

## 영향

- 집계 행은 애초에 DB 적재 실패 중이었으므로 **실질 데이터 손실 없음**
- 에러 로그가 사라지고 경쟁률/당첨 가점 동기화가 끝까지 완료됨
- 좀비 이슈(#38)와 무관한 선제 버그

## 검증

author: stefanko-ch
body:
## Summary

Move `SUBDOMAIN_SEPARATOR`, `INFISICAL_URL`, `CONTROL_PLANE_URL` from Terraform `environment_variables` on the Pages project to Pages secrets set via `wrangler pages secret put`. Fixes the Control Plane Secrets page for flat-subdomain deployments.

## Root cause

PR #434 (v0.49.0) added these three values as Terraform `environment_variables` in [`tofu/control-plane/main.tf`](tofu/control-plane/main.tf) on both `production` and `preview` deployment configs. The assumption was they'd survive into the running Pages Functions runtime.

They don't. The existing comment block at [`setup-control-plane.yaml:1003-1007`](.github/workflows/setup-control-plane.yaml) already documents exactly why:

> Pages secrets survive wrangler pages deploy (unlike environment_variables which get wiped). Terraform sets environment_variables on the project, but wrangler pages deploy treats wrangler.toml as source of truth and deletes any env vars not in it. Secrets are NOT affected by this behavior. So we set all values the Functions need as secrets here.

The "Set Control Plane secrets" step (line 990) already runs `wrangler pages secret put` for `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_OWNER`, `GITHUB_REPO`, `DOMAIN`, `ADMIN_EMAIL`, `USER_EMAIL`, `SERVER_TYPE`, `SERVER_LOCATION`, `RESEND_API_KEY` — these are the values the template's own Functions read via `context.env.*`. The three v0.49.0 additions were never added to that list.

On default dot-subdomain deployments (e.g. `nexus-stack.ch`) the failure was invisible because `secrets.js`'s fallback URL `https://infisical.${domain}` happens to match the real host. On flat-subdomain deployments (user forks provisioned by `Nexus-Stack-for-Education`, e.g. `infisical-user.base.example`), the fallback points at a non-existent host and the Secrets page returns "unexpected response".

## Changes

**`tofu/control-plane/main.tf`**
- Drop `SUBDOMAIN_SEPARATOR` / `INFISICAL_URL` / `CONTROL_PLANE_URL` from both `deployment_configs.production.environment_variables` and `deployment_configs.preview.environment_variables`.
- Replace with a comment pointing to setup-control-plane.yaml.
- `locals.infisical_url` / `control_plane_url` / `control_plane_hostname` stay — still referenced by `cloudflare_record`, `cloudflare_pages_domain`, `cloudflare_zero_trust_access_application`, CORS `allowed_origins`.
- `var.subdomain_separator` stays in `variables.tf`.

**`.github/workflows/setup-control-plane.yaml`** (`Set Control Plane secrets` step)
- Add `SUBDOMAIN_SEPARATOR: ${{ secrets.SUBDOMAIN_SEPARATOR || '.' }}` to the step's `env:` block.
- Add three `wrangler pages secret put` calls that compute `INFISICAL_URL` / `CONTROL_PLANE_URL` from `$DOMAIN` + `$SUBDOMAIN_SEPARATOR` and push them as secrets alongside the existing DOMAIN block.

## Backward compatibility

- Default `SUBDOMAIN_SEPARATOR = '.'` when the secret is unset → the template's own deployment resolves to the same URLs as today (`https://infisical.${domain}` / `https://control.${domain}`) and keeps working unchanged.
- Consumers that already set `SUBDOMAIN_SEPARATOR=-` (admin-panel provisioning) now get the right flat-subdomain URLs wired through the whole stack instead of silently falling back.
- Existing deployments: next `setup-control-plane.yaml` run sets the three new secrets. `wrangler pages secret list` will confirm them. No other moving parts.

## Test plan

- [x] `tofu validate` in `tofu/control-plane/` → success (no non-provider errors).
- [x] YAML parse of `setup-control-plane.yaml` → valid.
- [ ] After merge + release: run `setup-control-plane.yaml` on a user fork with `SUBDOMAIN_SEPARATOR=-` in repo secrets. Verify:
  - `wrangler pages secret list` shows `SUBDOMAIN_SEPARATOR`, `INFISICAL_URL`, `CONTROL_PLANE_URL` as Encrypted.
  - `/api/debug` on the Control Plane shows `DOMAIN`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `INFISICAL_TOKEN`, `INFISICAL_PROJECT_ID` all set.
  - `/secrets` page renders Infisical secrets grouped by folder (no "unexpected response").
  - Stack links on `/stacks` use dash form.
- [ ] Template's own deployment (`nexus-stack.ch`, `SUBDOMAIN_SEPARATOR` unset) continues to work — default `.` separator keeps the same URLs.

author: robyt3
body:
In the `CInput::ConsumeEvents` function we iterate over all input events with `for(const CEvent &Event : m_vInputEvents)`, which then call the `OnInput` function of the components. The `CChat::OnInput` function calls the `CChat::EnableMode` function when the chat is activated, which then calls `Input()->Clear()` which clears `m_vInputEvents` and invalidates the iterator of the `for`-loop. This was caught by the additional STL assertions from #11851.

This is fixed by removing the stray call to `Input()->Clear()` entirely. The call does not seem to have any effect (anymore). Opening the chat works. There are no input events being incorrectly handled after opening the chat. Holding binds when opening the chat also works as before.

The call to `Input()->Clear()` was previously `Input()->ClearEvents()`. Before that it was `inp_clear_events()`, which was introduced in dfe499248f1b1236487156b28e4a535d7963fe35.

body:
## Description

This PR implements granular section renaming with language-aware scoping. Users can now rename sections in Settings → Sections via a pencil icon that opens a modal. Renames are scoped to the active dataset by default, with an optional toggle to apply the rename to every dataset sharing the same language.

The implementation introduces a new `section_title_overrides` table keyed by `(section_key, language)` to store language-wide overrides. A new `resolveSectionTitle()` function establishes a clear precedence chain:
1. Per-dataset override (from `sectionOrder[].display_name`)
2. Per-language override (from `section_title_overrides`)
3. Translated section name (from i18n)
4. Built-in default or custom section name
5. Raw section key

The `/api/sections/rename` endpoint handles both per-dataset and language-wide renames, with language-wide renames overwriting all same-language datasets' per-dataset overrides to ensure consistency. Siblings in different languages (same `language_group`) are never touched.

## Test Coverage

Added comprehensive test suite covering:

author: frankbuckley
body:
Stacked on #36 (LRP09/LRP10 baseline + MAE tune).

## Summary

- **LRP09** (`celf_gain`): drop 15 features (34 → 19) — 8 Tier-A at ≤ 0.007 importance plus 7 Tier-B redundant/near-noise (reading-cluster redundancy, parental-education pair, speech-error pair, demographic noise-floor). Less aggressive than LRP07's 34→12 because LRP09's deep-tree many-estimator tune produced a shallower noise floor.
- **Keeps full grammar pair** (`trog`, `aptgram`) and **full DEAP articulation trio** (`deappfi`, `deappin`, `deappvo`) for construct coverage.
- **First Select01 in the programme where carry-forward clearly beats retune** across every CV metric. Primary params are the original 34-predictor tune applied to 19 preds, not the formally retuned 19-predictor params.

## Results

| Step | Preds | CV MAE | CV R² | CV MedAE | insR² |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| MAE-tuned on 34 | 34 | 2.232 | 0.094 | 1.753 | 0.628 |
| **Select01 carry-forward** (primary) | **19** | **2.185** | **0.124** | **1.650** | 0.625 |
| Retuned-19 | 19 | 2.282 | 0.061 | 1.866 | 0.726 |

Carry-forward improves on every CV metric over the 34-pred tune. CV R² rises 0.030; CV MedAE drops 0.10.

## The retune reversal

The 19-pred retune produced a dramatically different regime — **fewer-faster-wide + strong L1** (45 trees, lr 0.099, reg_alpha 1.14) replacing **many-slow-deep + strong L2** (194 trees, lr 0.013, reg_lambda 2.24). Tuner-inner CV MAE was 2.175 but actual refit CV MAE was 2.282 — evaluation gap of 0.11.

**Plausible mechanism**: the many-slow-deep-with-L2 regime generalises well because the regularisation handles correlated-predictor structure in the 34-predictor set. Retuning on cleaner 19 preds finds a narrower high-variance optimum (many wide trees + strong L1) that over-fits inner CV.

Convention broken deliberately: LRP05/LRP07 kept retune despite carry-forward edging on MedAE; here the gap across all metrics is large enough that carry-forward is retained as primary.

## Top importance under carry-forward (primary)

1. `celf` (0.591) — base, slight drop from 0.610
2. `deappfi` (0.057)
3. `trog` (0.043) — grammar (near construct match)
4. `b1exto` (0.038)
5. `erbnw` (0.038) — **doubled** from 0.017 (rank 17 → 5)
6. `attend` (0.037)
7. `ewrswr` (0.035)
8. `deappin` (0.035)
9. `yarclet` (0.032)
10. `mumedupost16` (0.032) — **doubled** from 0.016 (rank 19 → 10)

Every retained feature rose — textbook noise removal. No noise floor; all 19 features at ≥ 0.015.

## Test plan

- [ ] `pytest`
- [ ] `ruff check src/`
- [ ] `npm run spellcheck`
- [ ] `python scripts/fit_model.py lrp09 --config test`
- [ ] Review Select01 rationale in `notes/202604181400-lrp09-feature-selection.md`

author: copilot
body:
The post-migration refactor request included multiple extraction/unification opportunities. This PR now covers the requested scope in `phu-audio-lib`, including shared broadcaster abstractions and audio utility unification.

- ### Shared stateful abstraction
  Added `network/StatefulBroadcaster.h` as a thin base over `MulticastBroadcasterBase` with reusable helpers for:
  - clearing remote state maps
  - snapshotting + pruning remote state maps under lock
  - counting remote instances with API-compatible `int` return

- ### Stateful broadcaster migrations
  Updated these classes to inherit from `StatefulBroadcaster` and use shared helpers instead of duplicating map/mutex traversal logic:
  - `SampleBroadcaster`
  - `SpectrumBroadcaster`
  - `CtrlBroadcaster`

  Refactors are limited to internal state-management paths (`onShutdown`, snapshot/getters, count methods); protocol fields, receiver behavior, and public API contracts remain unchanged.

- ### Command broadcaster base extraction
  Added `network/CommandBroadcasterBase.h` to centralize shared command-channel behavior:
  - sender self-filter helper
  - target-group filtering helper
  - listener add/remove helper logic
  - listener dispatch helper logic

  `CommandBroadcaster` was migrated to use these shared helpers without changing command wire format or public API behavior.

- ### BucketSet refactor
  Added/refined `audio/BucketSet.h` as a generic bucket utility that:
  - represents contiguous index ranges divided into buckets
  - stores only per-bucket dirty state
  - provides generic dirty-range/dirty-index marking and dirty-iterator traversal
  - can mark dirty buckets from generic `Range` and `RingBufferInsertResult` inputs

  `BucketSet` intentionally contains no application-specific timing/configuration modes and no buffer-coupled behavior.

- ### PPQ-addressed ring buffer unification
  Added `audio/PpqAddressedRingBuffer.h` to unify PPQ-addressed single-sample writes and wrap-aware block inserts with dirty-range reporting.

  As part of follow-up refactoring, PPQ-specific write result types were generalized:
  - introduced `audio/RingBufferInsertResult.h` with shared `Range` and `RingBufferInsertResult`
  - `PpqAddressedRingBuffer` now returns `Range` (single write) and `RingBufferInsertResult` (block insert) instead of PPQ-specific result types

- ### Library surface/docs updates
  - Added new headers to `PhuAudioLib` interface sources in `CMakeLists.txt`:
    - `network/StatefulBroadcaster.h`
    - `network/CommandBroadcasterBase.h`
    - `audio/BucketSet.h`
    - `audio/PpqAddressedRingBuffer.h`
    - `audio/RingBufferInsertResult.h`
  - Updated README module descriptions to reflect the added abstractions/utilities
  - Added `.gitignore` entry for `build/` to keep generated artifacts out of source control

Example of the shared stateful snapshot/prune pattern:

```cpp
const int64_t now = getCurrentTimeMs();
getRemoteStates(m_mutex, m_remoteInfos, out,
                [now](const RemoteInstanceInfo& info) {
                    return !info.isOnline || (now - info.lastSeenMs > STALE_TIMEOUT_MS);
                });
```

body:
## Resumen
Se implementó una primera versión funcional del registro de pagos del sistema, integrando el historial de pagos con la actualización del estado actual del cliente.

## Alcance incluido
- Registro de pagos para clientes existentes
- Búsqueda de clientes por DNI o apellido dentro del flujo de pagos
- Selección de membresía activa
- Cálculo automático del monto según el precio de la membresía
- Cálculo automático de fecha fin del pago
- Actualización automática de la vigencia actual del cliente
- Restricción de acceso al flujo de pagos mediante policy

## Cambios realizados
- Se creó `PagoController`
- Se creó `PagoService`
- Se creó `StorePagoRequest`
- Se creó `PagoPolicy`
- Se registró la policy de pagos en `AppServiceProvider`
- Se agregaron las rutas de creación y almacenamiento de pagos
- Se creó la vista `pagos/create.blade.php`

## Reglas de negocio aplicadas
- El monto del pago ya no se ingresa manualmente
- El monto se toma automáticamente desde el precio de la membresía elegida
- `fecha_fin` se calcula en backend según la duración de la membresía
- Si el cliente mantiene vigencia activa, la nueva fecha se extiende desde su vencimiento actual
- Si el cliente está vencido, la nueva fecha se calcula desde la fecha del nuevo pago
- Al registrar el pago se actualiza el estado actual del cliente:
  - `membresia_actual_id`
  - `fecha_ultimo_pago`
  - `fecha_vencimiento`
  - `estado`

## Pruebas realizadas
- Registro correcto de pagos
- Verificación de persistencia en tabla `pagos`
- Verificación de actualización de datos en tabla `clientes`
- Verificación del cálculo automático de:
  - `monto`
  - `fecha_fin`
  - `fecha_vencimiento`
- Verificación del flujo con búsqueda de cliente por DNI y apellido
- Verificación del acceso a pagos solo para usuarios activos con rol permitido

## Pendiente para futuras iteraciones
- Mejora visual del flujo de pagos
- Mostrar más información del cliente antes de confirmar el pago
- Historial de pagos por cliente
- Integración con informes financieros

author: sabbour
body:
## Problem

SWA deploy is still failing even after moving `@kickstart/harness` to devDependencies (#814). Oryx still runs `npm install --production` in `packages/web/api` before our no-op `api_build_command`, and it can't resolve the workspace links in the root `package-lock.json`.

## Fix

Flip `skip_api_build: false` → `skip_api_build: true` in `.github/workflows/deploy-swa.yml`.

The API functions are already pre-bundled by esbuild into `packages/web/api/dist/functions/` during the `npm run build` step earlier in the job. Oryx shouldn't touch them. Setting `skip_api_build: true` bypasses the entire Oryx pipeline for the API; SWA uploads the pre-bundled functions as-is.

`api_location: packages/web/api` is correct — that's where `host.json` lives, and SWA picks up the compiled functions from the `dist/functions/` subdirectory (the default Azure Functions output).

## Scope

YAML-only change. No dependency updates needed.

Working as Bender (Backend Dev).

author: copilot
body:
Reimplements the trolley adventure quiz canvas from a side-view track diagram to a first-person perspective scene, and reorders the game screen so the question sits above the illustration.

## Layout
- **Before:** canvas → question card → buttons
- **After:** question card → canvas → buttons

## Canvas rewrite (perspective view)
Replaced the old flat side-view with a vanishing-point perspective scene driven by a `canvasPhase` state machine:

| Phase | Visual |
|---|---|
| `moving` | Straight tracks scrolling toward camera (parallax); child+trolley sprite at bottom |
| `atFork` | Y-fork; orange sign (left arm) / blue sign (right arm) showing answer words |
| `correct` | Tracks continue + green **○** ring on the track bed |
| `broken` | Rails end at cliff ledge → dark void + red **✕** danger markers |

Crosstie spacing uses a `t²` depth function for natural perspective compression (denser near horizon, sparser near camera).

## Animation system
Replaced `moveTrolley()` / `fallTrolley()` position interpolation with a scroll loop:

```js
const SCROLL_SPEED    = 0.85; // cycles/s
const APPROACH_CYCLES = 1.9;  // total cycles before fork appears (~2.2 s)

function startApproachAnim(onForkReached) {
    canvasPhase = 'moving';
    // rAF loop increments scrollOff; switches to 'atFork' when done
}
```

All quiz logic (data, scoring, shuffle, sound, game-over) is untouched.

**At fork (question + Y-fork + choice signs):**

**Incorrect answer (broken tracks / cliff):**
![broken state](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dad08a3f-1aeb-4f76-b251-496a51a79ca6)

## Summary
ID 컬럼 정의 불일치로 \`ddl-auto=validate\` 프로파일(staging/prod)에서 앱 부팅이 실패하는 버그 수정.

## Bug
\`Long\` 필드에 \`@Column(columnDefinition = \"integer unsigned\")\`가 박혀있음.
- \`ddl-auto: create\` (local/dev): INTEGER UNSIGNED로 컬럼 생성
- \`ddl-auto: validate\` (staging/prod): Java Long → BIGINT 기대 → 검증 실패
\`\`\`
Schema-validation: wrong column type encountered in column [id] in table [playlist];
found [int unsigned (Types#INTEGER)], but expecting [integer unsigned (Types#BIGINT)]
\`\`\`

## Fix
4개 엔티티의 ID 컬럼 정의를 \`bigint unsigned\`로 통일:
- \`PlaylistData.id\`
- \`TrackData.id\`
- \`ActivityData.id\`
- \`ProfileData.id\`

다른 \`columnDefinition\` 사용처는 일관됨 (수정 없음):
- \`*.orderNumber\` (Integer ↔ integer unsigned) ✓
- \`ActivityData.score\` (Score → Integer 컨버터 ↔ integer unsigned) ✓
- \`BaseEntity\` datetime 컬럼 ✓

## ⚠️ 주의 — 기존 데이터 있는 환경 마이그레이션 필요
prod처럼 INT 컬럼이 이미 있는 DB는 ALTER TABLE 필요:
\`\`\`sql
ALTER TABLE playlist MODIFY COLUMN id BIGINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT;
ALTER TABLE track    MODIFY COLUMN id BIGINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT;
ALTER TABLE user_activity MODIFY COLUMN id BIGINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT;
ALTER TABLE user_profile  MODIFY COLUMN id BIGINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT;
\`\`\`
참조하는 외래키도 함께 BIGINT로 변경 필요할 수 있음.

## Test
- [x] \`./gradlew :app:build\` 성공 (테스트 포함, 17s)
- [ ] 머지 후 staging 프로파일로 컨테이너 재기동, 부팅 성공 확인

## Summary

v1.9.0 is a **5-commit stack** covering macro-regime-snapshot's biggest refresh since v1.3.0:

1. **`634f0cd`** — 5-country routing (US/JP/TW/KR/CN) + LSEG-style 5-block dashboard + new `real-rates` group in us-macro (T5YIE/T10YIE/DFII5/DFII10)
2. **`be73756`** — Real-rate four-tier thresholds (Accommodative / Neutral / Moderately Restrictive / Clearly Restrictive) + r\* provenance v1
3. **`13a76d1`** — **Option B hybrid**: per-country threshold files (`thresholds-{us,japan,taiwan,korea,china}.md`) instead of flattening country nuances into SKILL.md
4. **`59fe397`** — **Option C grounding**: primary-source audit (19 🔴 + 16 ⚠️ corrections) via 5 parallel native-language research agents, following `domain-teams/skills/*/research/grounding-v*.md` convention
5. **`e2c6e3a`** — BOJ policy-rate 3-tier structure detail (誘導目標 0.75% vs IOER vs 補完貸付 1.00%; STRDCLUCON market-rate 2-3 bp below target mechanism)

## What v1.9.0 actually does

- **Data layer**: adds 4 new FRED series to us-macro (`real-rates` group)
- **Aggregation layer**: rewires macro-regime-snapshot to use all 5 country macro skills (was US+JP only since v1.3.0) with the v1.7.0 monthly GDP proxies
- **Reference layer**: 5 new per-country threshold calibration files + `recalibration-protocol.md` + consolidated `research/grounding-v1.9.0.md` audit trail

## Critical grounding corrections (selected)

**US**
- FAIT framework **RETIRED 2025-08** Jackson Hole → replaced by FIT. Prior draft said \"FAIT still active\"
- HLW r\* = **~0.75% real** (2025-Q4), NOT 1.42% (web-search confused LW-closure with HLW)
- Lubik-Matthes r\* = **1.68%** (2026-03-10 update), NOT 2.15%

**JP**
- BOJ policy rate **0.75% 程度** (2025-12-19 30 年ぶり水準), NOT 0.5%
- JILPT 均衡失業率 **2.80%** (2026-02), NOT 3.5-3.6% — current unemp 2.6% = 軽度タイト only
- BOJ 展望 2025-10 數値 全錯 (年度 off by 1 year, FY2025 off by 0.8 pp)
- 野村 森田京平 main scenario: ターミナル **1.50%** via 3 hikes, NOT 2 hikes to 1.0%
- 10Y real yield \"-0.386%\" citation UNVERIFIABLE → removed (fabrication risk)
- **New discovery**: BOJ 日銀レビュー rev26j05 (2026-03) = latest official r\* view

**TW**
- 景氣對策信號 9 構成指標 2 項錯: 「非農業就業」→ 實際「工業及服務業加班工時」; 「製造業存貨率比率」→ 實際「製造業營業氣候測驗點 TIER」
- TSMC 佔 TAIEX **44.30%** (TWSE 2026-03-31), NOT ~40%; 5 年 +17 pp
- 景氣燈號現行版本 **2024 修訂** (9 次修訂), NOT 2013
- **2014-2023 十年無紅燈** → 2024-02 首度破紅燈 + 創 31 年分數新高 40 分

**KR**
- 2018-12-26 發表 / 2019 以後適用 (3 年週期廢止 + 適用期間無期限化)
- 2004-2006 (core CPI 2.5-3.5%) vs 2007-2009 (headline 3% ± 0.5%) — prior draft 顛倒
- 삼성+SK하이닉스 = **39.88%** (2026-02) → 40.90%; 양 그룹 합계 **61.29%** (超越 S&P Mag-7 33.41%)
- 가계부채/GDP **~90%** (2025-Q3 BIS), NOT 105% (105 은 2021 피크)
- BOK 연구원 Do/Ahn/Jung 2024 multi-model r\* **~0-1% real**
- **New discovery**: KR 2026-01 起 BIS 重分類為 advanced economy

**CN (largest rewrite)**
- **CPI 目標 = 2% 左右** (2025, 2026 連續兩年) — NOT 3%. **2004 以來首次下調**. 整份 \"3% ceiling\" 假設作廢
- 全利率偏高 1 檔: LPR 1Y **3.0%** / LPR 5Y 3.5% / RRR 9.0% / 7D OMO **1.40%**
- **PBOC 2024-07 改以 7D 逆回購為主要政策利率** (MLF 退位為數量工具)
- \"中國無 r\* 估計\" 錯 — BIS WP 949 (Rees & Sun 2021) real **2-3%**
- CSI300 \"金融+SOE 主導\" 過時 (2016 金融 35% → 2025 23%; IT 9% → 20%; 四分天下)
- \"適度寬鬆\" 是 2010 以來首次 (與 1998-1999, 2008-2009 同列)

## Architecture decisions

**Option B (per-country threshold files)**: Framework (IC + GIP) 通用，但校準參數不通用。5 個 `thresholds-*.md` 各 500-700 行，共同 8-section 模板：
1. Inflation Target
2. Labor Market Tightness (NAIRU)
3. Policy Rate Neutrality (+ JP 3-tier detail)
4. Real Rate Decomposition (available / not / deferred)
5. Structural Regime Notes
6. Asset-Class Tilt Calibration
7. Primary-Source Verification URLs
8. Sources (citations with native-language references)

**Option C (grounding audit)**: 5 平行 native-language research agent (~407k tokens, ~30 min wallclock vs ~2.5 hrs sequential). Output = `research/grounding-v1.9.0.md` (1230+ 行, modeled on `qa-team/research/grounding-v4.2.0.md` pattern).

## Files changed

**+2639 / −92** across 22 files:
- New: `research/grounding-v1.9.0.md` (consolidated audit trail)
- New: `references/thresholds-{us,japan,taiwan,korea,china}.md`
- New: `references/recalibration-protocol.md`
- Rewrite: `SKILL.md` (Step 1 per-country routing with 'do NOT apply US thresholds to non-US' guardrail)
- Rewrite: `references/investment-clock-cheatsheet.md` (threshold provenance, signal-label glossary)
- Update: `us-macro/SKILL.md` + `us-macro-indicators.md` (real-rates group)
- Update: `commands/invest-macro.md` (9-value region enum)
- Update: `using-investing-toolkit/SKILL.md`, plugin `README.md`, `ROADMAP.md`, `plugin.json` (1.8.1 → 1.9.0)

## Test plan

- [x] `fred_client.py --series T5YIE,T10YIE,DFII5,DFII10` → 4 daily series, latest 2026-04-16/17
- [x] `boj_client.py --db FM01 --code STRDCLUCON` → overnight call rate 0.727% (matches 0.75% target ± 3 bp)
- [x] sync-scripts.sh + sync-check.sh: clean
- [x] Plugin version bumped 1.8.1 → 1.9.0
- [ ] Reviewer: spot-check `grounding-v1.9.0.md` audit table for a country of interest
- [ ] Reviewer: skim 1-2 threshold files to assess per-country template consistency
- [ ] End-to-end `/invest-macro --region all` in fresh Claude session (skills load the new SKILL.md + thresholds)

## Deferred to v1.10.0+

- JP JGBi real-rate via MoF XLS scraper
- KR KTBi (requires BOK ECOS API key at ecos.bok.or.kr/api/#/AuthKeyApply)
- ISM PMI via FRED NAPM
- TW 製造業採購經理人指數 / KR 기업경기실사
- Swap-spread block (extra FRED series + calibration)
- Full BOK ECOS API (lagging CI 후행지수; was prior v1.9.0 candidate, re-deferred)

## External documentation (optional)

Obsidian research note written to maintainer's vault:
\`research/2026-04-18 各國中央銀行政策利率體系與自然利率 r-star — 5 國跨市場研究.md\` — cross-country policy-rate architecture + r\* research + 20-year trajectories. Not in-repo; maintainer's personal knowledge management.

## Summary

- Add an optional `remote_endpoint` field to `ClientConfig` and forward it to `UdpTransport` / `TcpTransport` during `SomeIpClient` construction.
- This enables communication with SOME/IP servers that do not run Service Discovery (e.g. Zephyr-based MCU firmware with multicast TX disabled).
- Both transports already accepted the parameter — it just wasn't wired through the high-level config. The field defaults to `None`, preserving existing SD-based behavior.

Closes #13

## Changes

### `src/opensomeip/client.py`
- Added `remote_endpoint: Endpoint | None = None` field to `ClientConfig`
- Updated `SomeIpClient.__init__` to forward `config.remote_endpoint` to both `TcpTransport` and `UdpTransport` constructors

### `tests/unit/test_client.py`
- Added `TestStaticRemoteEndpoint` test class with 5 tests:
  - `test_remote_endpoint_defaults_to_none` — backward compatibility
  - `test_udp_remote_endpoint_forwarded` — UDP transport picks up the endpoint
  - `test_tcp_remote_endpoint_forwarded` — TCP transport picks up the endpoint
  - `test_no_remote_endpoint_preserves_none` — omitting the field preserves `None`
  - `test_lifecycle_with_remote_endpoint` — full start/stop cycle with static endpoint

author: srdvys
body:
In the components/ directory, I developed a new forgotpass.vue component that provides a complete account recovery cycle within a single window. The entire process is implemented through reactive state switching between three logical stages: email submission for token requests (forgot), verification via a 6-digit numeric code (code), and new password configuration (renew).

Special attention was paid to the UX: an intelligent focusing system for the code input was implemented, which automatically advances the cursor to the next field upon entry (handleInput) and returns it to the previous one when a character is deleted (handleKeydown). On the technical side, the component leverages Nuxt's $fetch utility to ensure stable interaction with the /api/Auth/forgot-password and /api/Auth/reset-password backend endpoints.

author: copilot
body:
Each service was a single flat `.yml` fragment in a category directory. This restructures every service into its own subfolder containing a dedicated `Dockerfile` and updated compose fragment, enabling per-service image customization.

## Changes

- **Per-service subdirectories** — each of the 27 services now lives under `services/<category>/<service>/` (e.g. `services/ai/ollama/`, `services/databases/postgresql/`)
- **Dockerfile per service** — each subfolder contains a `Dockerfile` with `FROM <original-image>`, ready to be extended
- **Updated compose fragments** — `image:` replaced with `build: .` in every `.yml` so Docker Compose builds from the local Dockerfile
- **Removed flat `.yml` files** — original category-level files deleted

## Example

`services/ai/ollama/Dockerfile`:
```dockerfile
FROM ollama/ollama:latest
```

`services/ai/ollama/ollama.yml`:
```yaml
ollama:
  build: .
  container_name: ollama
  restart: unless-stopped
  ports:
    - "11434:11434"
  volumes:
    - ollama_data:/root/.ollama
```

body:
### Motivation
- Introduce a local-first runtime to queue, plan, execute, and persist long-running task runs and step histories so tasks can be executed by worker slots and surfaced in the UI. 
- Provide durable schemas and migration-safe initialization so artifacts, evidence, approvals and runtime state are stored in SQLite and survive restarts. 
- Expose simple intake APIs and realtime events so external callers and the UI can create/list/cancel runs and observe queue/run progress. 
- Keep major-action approval gating and existing UI features intact while wiring real execution state into the Task Board and store.

### Description
- Added a new runtime service `TaskRunRuntime` (`packages/server/src/runtime/TaskRunRuntime.ts`) that manages a configurable worker pool, finds queued runs, produces a simple plan, executes steps, persists step attempts, delegates child runs on `spawn_agent`, and writes artifacts to the workspace.

author: sanity
body:
## Problem

Two user-visible bugs in `freenet uninstall`:

**1. Stale binaries from mixed install methods.** The command detects the install directory by looking at `current_exe().parent()` only. A user who ran the `curl | sh` installer (places binaries in `~/.local/bin`) and later `cargo install freenet` (places a binary in `~/.cargo/bin`) ends up with the uninstall removing whichever was on PATH first, leaving the other behind to shadow future reinstalls. Same failure mode on Windows: the PowerShell installer puts binaries in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Freenet\bin`, which PATH detection misses when a different `freenet.exe` is active.

**2. Empty parent folders left behind on Windows** (reported on Matrix by @Ivvvor, filed as #3904). `purge_data_dirs` removes the leaf `data`, `config`, and `cache` subfolders but never touches their common parent, so `%APPDATA%\The Freenet Project Inc\Freenet\` — and analogously `%LOCALAPPDATA%\freenet\` once its `logs` child is gone — stays on disk long after uninstall claims completion.

## Approach

**Install-dir detection is now multi-site.** `get_install_dir` is replaced with `get_install_dirs` (plural) returning the union of the running-exe parent, `~/.local/bin`, `~/.cargo/bin`, and `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Freenet\bin`. `FREENET_INSTALL_DIR` and the explicit `override_dir` arg still short-circuit to a single location. Missing dirs are skipped silently; present dirs have their binaries removed, and on Windows the enclosing `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Freenet\` collapses once `bin\` is gone.

**Parent-folder cleanup is explicit.** `purge_data_dirs` now builds a `DataLeaves` value and delegates to `purge_leaves_and_collapse`, which removes every leaf, collects their parents, then visits the parents deepest-first to collapse any that became empty. A `remove_dir_if_empty` helper enforces safety: it removes a directory only if it contains nothing, so a non-empty sibling app's data under `The Freenet Project Inc\` is preserved.

The overall behavior on a clean Linux install is unchanged; the extra work only kicks in when multiple install sources coexist or when a formerly-Freenet parent is now empty.

## Testing

25 new unit / integration tests covering:

- **`get_install_dirs`** precedence (override > env var > defaults), empty env-var fallthrough, override beating env var, exe-parent/cargo-bin dedup, missing home dir.
- **`remove_dir_if_empty`** safety: empty-dir removal, single-file preservation, subdirectory-tree preservation, missing path, regular file, full children-then-collapse scenario.
- **`purge_leaves_and_collapse` wiring** (the actual #3904 regression site): full Windows-like layout cleanup, sibling-app-grandparent preservation, log-parent gate, missing optional leaves.
- **`collapse_windows_bin_tree`**: extracted so Linux CI can exercise it; tests for empty tree, non-empty sibling preservation, missing tree.

The wiring-level tests mean reverting any individual `push_parent(...)` call at a future date would fail a test, not silently regress #3904.

Tests explicitly chose the unit level because the behavior is pure filesystem manipulation with no network or timing surface. A Windows matrix integration test seeding the actual `%LOCALAPPDATA%` layout would be the next level of coverage; filed as a follow-up but out of scope for this PR.

Full `cargo test -p freenet --bin freenet` (74 tests) passes; `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

## Fixes

Closes #3904

## Out of scope

- **HKCU `Run` registry key** was called out in #3904 as a potential leftover. Skipped here because `install.ps1` does not write a Run entry — it uses `freenet service install` (Task Scheduler) instead, which `stop_and_remove_service` already handles.
- **Auto-update detection of stale installs.** Separate concern.

## Related

- freenet/web#35 merged documentation for the same user-visible problem.
- A follow-up freenet-core PR will add a standalone `uninstall.sh` companion script and update `install.sh`'s final message to steer users away from `sudo freenet uninstall`.

body:
## Summary

- Adds `test_coverage.py` to the JavaScript language plugin with naming convention mapping, import spec parsing (ESM and CommonJS), and test quality patterns
- Fixes a path resolution bug in `ts_build_dep_graph` where project-root-relative paths from `resolve_js_import` were double-joined with the scan path prefix
- Registers the new hooks via `generic_lang test_coverage_module` parameter

## Problem

JavaScript projects using `.test.js` naming convention showed 0% test health regardless of test coverage. Two root causes:

1. The JavaScript plugin had no `test_coverage.py`, so `naming_based_mapping` (which strips `.test.` from filenames to find production files) returned empty for `lang_name='javascript'`
2. `ts_build_dep_graph` had a path mismatch: `resolve_js_import` returns project-root-relative paths (e.g. `_ui/server.js`) but the graph builder joined them with the already-prefixed scan path (`/path/to/_ui/`), producing invalid absolute paths (`/path/to/_ui/_ui/server.js`) that never matched the file set

## Test plan

- [ ] Run desloppify scan on a JavaScript project with `.test.js` files — should show > 0% test health
- [ ] Verify `naming_based_mapping('javascript')` maps `foo.test.js` → `foo.js`

body:
## Summary
- Refs #8074 (Cluster B, CT).
- Implements the statutory exclusion in `RCSA 17b-749-05(b)(2)(E)`: "the earnings of a family member who is under the age of eighteen who is not the parent of a child for whom assistance is requested" are excluded from countable income under Connecticut's Care 4 Kids program.

## Changes
- Split `income.sources` into:
  - `earned_sources`: `employment_income`, `self_employment_income`, `farm_income` — summed only for members aged 18+ or who are the tax-unit head/spouse (parent/applicant), covering the statute's carve-out for teen parents.
  - `unearned_sources`: `social_security`, `pension_income`, `unemployment_compensation`, `workers_compensation`, `alimony_income`, `rental_income`, `veterans_benefits`, `disability_benefits` — summed across all members, since `17b-749-05(b)(1)(A)` counts "unearned income of all adult and child family members" and the exclusion applies only to earnings.
- Replace `ct_c4k_countable_income`'s simple `add(sources)` with a formula that applies the adult/parent filter to earned income.
- Add 3 YAML regression tests: working teen's wages excluded; minor child entrepreneur's self-employment excluded; minor's SSA survivor benefit still countable.

## Statutory reference
- RCSA 17b-749-05(b): https://eregulations.ct.gov/eRegsPortal/Browse/RCSA/Title_17bSubtitle_17b-749Section_17b-749-05/
- Care 4 Kids Policies and Procedures (former regulations retained as policy by CT OEC after Public Act 24-91): https://www.ctoec.org/care-4-kids-regulations/#17b-749-05 (full text of (b)(2)(E) on this page).

## Test plan

body:
This pull request adds robust error handling and retry logic to the MeteoAM integration, improving reliability when fetching weather data from the external API. The main enhancements are the introduction of a new `TransientAPIError` exception to distinguish retryable errors, implementing retries for transient failures, and comprehensive tests to verify this behavior.

**Error handling and retry logic improvements:**

- Introduced a new `TransientAPIError` exception, subclassing `CannotConnectError`, to represent network and HTTP 5xx errors that are safe to retry. (`custom_components/meteoam/coordinator.py`)
- Updated the `fetch_data` method to raise `TransientAPIError` for network issues and HTTP 5xx responses, while non-retryable errors (such as HTTP 4xx) continue to raise `CannotConnectError`. (`custom_components/meteoam/coordinator.py`)
- Modified the `_async_update_data` method in `MeteoAMDataUpdateCoordinator` to retry up to three times with a delay for `TransientAPIError`, logging each attempt and only failing after the maximum attempts. (`custom_components/meteoam/coordinator.py`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-6fdaa5806a5e3fdc42bd69158521a42fd44cbb594ac779826bd107f33a175662R27-R29) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-6fdaa5806a5e3fdc42bd69158521a42fd44cbb594ac779826bd107f33a175662L60-R88)

**Testing:**

- Added new test cases to verify that transient errors are retried and non-retryable errors are not, including tests for network errors, HTTP 5xx/4xx responses, and the retry mechanism itself. (`tests/test_coordinator.py`)
- Updated imports in the test file to include the new exception and coordinator class. (`tests/test_coordinator.py`)
