We have many optional items in the `reccmp-project.yml`, mostly lists of items that default to empty lists. The file produced by `reccmp-project create` looks like:
```yaml
targets:
  JMAN:
    filename: JMAN.EXE
    source_root: .
    hash:
      sha256: 243f62328af86447376d1d94a2458bc96e64bc9b0e70c27b1470a4c21a40f2a0
    data_sources: []
    encoding:
    ghidra:
      ignore_types: []
      ignore_functions: []
      name_substitutions: []
      allow_hash_mismatch: false
    report:
      ignore_functions: []
```

If we exclude items that are set to their default value, we get only:
```yaml
targets:
  JMAN:
    filename: JMAN.EXE
    source_root: .
    hash:
      sha256: 243f62328af86447376d1d94a2458bc96e64bc9b0e70c27b1470a4c21a40f2a0
```
One argument against doing this is our (admittedly) [minimal documentation](https://github.com/isledecomp/reccmp/blob/master/docs/project_files.md) for the project schema. Displaying all the possible options could be considered helpful to users.

author: odinlabs-ai
body:
## Summary

The Claude 4.7 model family (Opus, Sonnet, Haiku) uses adaptive thinking exclusively and rejects `temperature`, `top_p`, and `top_k` parameters — the API returns a **400 error** even when extended thinking is disabled.

This PR:

- **Adds Sonnet 4.7 and Haiku 4.7** to `supportsAdaptiveThinking()` in both `anthropic` and `amazon-bedrock` providers. Opus 4.7 was already present but Sonnet and Haiku were missing, causing them to fall through to budget-based thinking (which 4.7 models also don't support).

- **Introduces `isClaude47()` helper** in the anthropic provider to detect 4.7 family models using a simple `"4-7"` / `"4.7"` substring match. This is intentionally broad to cover future model IDs (e.g. date-suffixed variants like `claude-sonnet-4-7-20260501`).

- **Guards temperature in `buildParams()`** so it is never sent to 4.7 models, even when `thinkingEnabled` is false. Without this guard, any non-thinking API call with a temperature value fails with a 400 error.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.ts` | Add sonnet/haiku 4.7 to `supportsAdaptiveThinking()`, add `isClaude47()`, guard temperature |
| `packages/ai/src/providers/amazon-bedrock.ts` | Add sonnet/haiku 4.7 to `supportsAdaptiveThinking()` |

## Test plan

- [x] Existing `supports-xhigh.test.ts` continues to pass (Opus 4.7 path unchanged)
- [x] Verified no false positives from `isClaude47()` pattern against `models.generated.ts`
- [x] Verified `top_p`/`top_k` are not sent by the anthropic provider (only temperature needed guarding)
- [ ] Manual verification with Claude 4.7 Sonnet API call with temperature (should no longer 400)

# Description

## Summary

This PR contains only the PDF-preview work and is intentionally stacked on top of `quilt3-local-filesystem`.

It increases PDF preview fidelity in the Catalog UI, adds targeted frontend and lambda coverage, and adds small local benchmarking/demo helpers for validating the change.

## Base Branch

This PR is intentionally opened against `Austin-s-h/quilt:quilt3-local-filesystem` because contributors without write access cannot create an isolated stacked PR directly against `quiltdata/quilt` until the base branch exists upstream.

## What Changed

- increased the requested PDF preview size in the frontend preview loader and renderer
- exported the PDF loader helpers/constants to support direct unit coverage
- added frontend tests for:
  - initial PDF preview request shape
  - PPTX preview request shape
  - later-page PDF navigation requests
- updated the thumbnail lambda PDF path to:
  - render at configurable DPI
  - clamp DPI to a sane upper bound
  - downsample using Lanczos
  - report render metadata in the response info
- added targeted lambda tests for PDF render DPI and metadata reporting
- added local helper scripts for:
  - generating a sample multi-page PDF
  - benchmarking the PDF preview path
- updated preview documentation with local validation guidance and benchmark usage

## Scope

This PR intentionally excludes the LOCAL/filesystem infrastructure work except where it is required as the base branch for local testing.

- `cd catalog && npx vitest run app/components/Preview/loaders/Pdf.spec.js app/components/Preview/renderers/Pdf.spec.js`

After `quilt3-local-filesystem` merges upstream, rebase this branch onto `quiltdata/quilt:master` and open a new upstream PR from `Austin-s-h:pdf-preview`.

## Notes for Reviewers

- this PR is about preview quality and validation, not broader LOCAL-mode behavior

- Remove ambiguity caused by two different "official input" collections by making pipeline inputs and customer summary soil metrics explicit and layered. 
- Ensure anyone reading the contract can immediately see which set is the pipeline whitelist and which set is the customer summary subset. 
- Encode the relationship between the two sets in the contract so the hierarchy cannot be misinterpreted. 

### Description
- Introduced `STAGE1_OFFICIAL_PIPELINE_CANONICAL_INPUT_METRICS` as the single authoritative Stage-1 pipeline input whitelist and `STAGE1_OFFICIAL_SUMMARY_SOIL_METRICS` as the customer-summary soil metrics subset in `apps/server/src/domain/sensing/stage1_sensing_contract_v1.ts`.

- Updated `apps/server/src/projections/field_sensing_summary_stage1_v1.ts` to build `official_soil_metrics_json` from the explicit `STAGE1_OFFICIAL_SUMMARY_SOIL_METRICS` (removed ambiguous use of a single `STAGE1_OFFICIAL_INPUT_METRICS`).

author: abc873693
body:
### **User description**
## 摘要

#384 修好 \`productbuild\` 的 Installer 簽章，暴露出下一層問題：App Store Connect 拒收 pkg，`altool` 回 `Validation failed (409) App sandbox not enabled`。

根因：\`flutter build macos --release\` 產出的 \`.app\` 是**未簽章**的，entitlement 只有在 codesign 時才會嵌進 Mach-O 執行檔。原本流程直接 \`productbuild --sign <installer>\` 包 pkg，installer 簽章只蓋在 pkg 外層，.app 內部仍沒有 \`com.apple.security.app-sandbox\` entitlement，App Store Connect 因此拒收。

`macos/Runner/Release.entitlements` 檔案本身正確（`app-sandbox=true`），只是沒有被套用。

## 變更

1. **再匯入一顆憑證**：`3rd Party Mac Developer Application`，來源用新 secret `MAC_APP_CERT_BASE64` / `MAC_APP_CERT_PASSWORD`，放進獨立 keychain `mac-app-signing`
2. **Pre-flight 一併驗兩顆身分**：Installer + Application 缺一就 fail
3. **Build 後新增 codesign 步驟**：
   - 找到 \`build/macos/Build/Products/Release/*.app\`
   - \`codesign --force --deep --options runtime --timestamp --entitlements macos/Runner/Release.entitlements --sign "$MAC_APP_DISTRIBUTION_CERT_NAME"\`
   - 驗證 \`codesign --verify\` 通過
   - 驗證 \`codesign --display --entitlements :-\` 裡確實有 \`app-sandbox\` 字串，沒有就 fail
4. 之後 Fastlane 的 \`productbuild --sign <installer>\` 照舊跑，因為 .app 已經簽好，installer 簽章只要包外層

## 需要先在 repo 設定的 secrets

Merge 前請新增：

| Secret | 內容 |
|---|---|
| `MAC_APP_CERT_BASE64` | 3rd Party Mac Developer Application `.p12` 的 base64 |
| `MAC_APP_CERT_PASSWORD` | 該 .p12 的匯出密碼 |
| `MAC_APP_DISTRIBUTION_CERT_NAME` | 憑證的 common name，例：`3rd Party Mac Developer Application: Open Culture Foundation (5SP52F6F2C)` |

base64 產生指令：

```bash
base64 -i mac_app_distribution.p12 | pbcopy
```

## Diff

```
 .github/workflows/cd.yml | 42 +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++---
 1 file changed, 39 insertions(+), 3 deletions(-)
```

## Test plan

- [ ] 新增 3 個 secret
- [ ] 觀察下一次 `cd.yml` 跑的 `deploy_macos` job：
  - Codesign 步驟的 `codesign --verify` 過關
  - entitlements 檢查印出 `com.apple.security.app-sandbox`
  - Fastlane 的 `upload_to_testflight` 不再拋 409 validation error
  - TestFlight 頁面收到新 macOS build

## 關聯

- 上一手 #384（Installer 憑證匯入）
- Refs #312


___

### **PR Type**
Bug fix, Enhancement


___

### **Description**
- 解決 macOS App Store Connect 拒收問題。

- 導入第二個憑證用於 App 簽章。

- 在部署前對 `.app` 進行沙盒簽章。

- 統一驗證 macOS 簽章身份。


___

### Diagram Walkthrough


```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A["Build macOS"] --> B["Codesign macOS .app with Entitlements"]
  B --> C["Deploy macOS to TestFlight"]
```

author: jerrettdavis
body:
## Summary

- **Root cause:** `Process.WaitForExitAsync` does not guarantee that redirected stdout/stderr pipe data has been fully delivered to the async reader tasks before it returns. This is a documented .NET behaviour — unlike the synchronous `WaitForExit()` overload, the async version only waits for the process to exit, not for I/O completion on the redirected streams.
- **The race:** On Linux CI runners (which are more resource-constrained and schedule OS pipe flushes later), the sequence was: process exits → `WaitForExitAsync` unblocks → code awaits `outputTask`/`errorTask` → reads empty/partial strings before the OS has delivered all buffered pipe data. The test then saw `Output` not containing `"hello"` or `Error` not containing `"oops"`.
- **The fix:** Add `process.WaitForExit()` (no-arg synchronous overload) immediately after `WaitForExitAsync` returns. Microsoft's documentation explicitly states: *"To ensure that asynchronous event handling has been completed, call the WaitForExit() overload that takes no parameter after receiving a true return value from this overload."* This drains all pending pipe data before the reader tasks are consumed.

## Test plan

- [x] `RunCommandAsync_WhenCommandSucceeds_CapturesExitCodeOutputAndError` — ran 10 consecutive times locally, 10/10 passed
- [x] Full `WelcomeServiceStatusProbeExtendedTests` class — all 31 tests pass, 0 regressions
- [ ] CI green on this PR
- [ ] Dependabot PRs #484, #485, #486 will pick up the fix automatically when they rebase onto main

> **Note:** The flake does not reproduce locally on Windows (Windows pipe flushing semantics differ), but the hazard is real and the fix is correct per the .NET Process documentation. The fix is purely additive — `WaitForExit()` after `WaitForExitAsync` is a no-op when the process has already exited and streams are already drained.

author: vloothuis
body:
## Summary

- New `Encrypted string` field on `PropertyDef`; new `EncryptedBody string` on `EntityDef` — cleartext by default.
- New `internal/metamodel/groups.go` with `Groups` type + `LoadGroups(projectRoot, fs)` — reads `<projectRoot>/groups.yaml` with strict YAML decoding.
- New `*GroupError{Kind, Group, Path, Identity}` typed error + sentinel matchers (`ErrGroupsNotFound`, `ErrUnknownGroup`, `ErrDuplicateIdentity`, `ErrInvalidIdentity`).
- New `Metamodel.ValidateEncryption(g *Groups)` — cross-validates every `encrypted:` declaration resolves to a known group. Iterates in sorted order for deterministic error messages.
- New `LoadWithGroups(path, fs)` helper composing metamodel + groups load + validation for the common callers.
- No `internal/encryption` import from `metamodel` (arch-lint constraint preserved).

## Stacked on slice 1

This PR is stacked on `tkt-16ry1-encryption-primitives` (PR #404). The base is set accordingly. Review diff against that branch. Squash on merge.

## Design review

Reviewed with `go-architect` before implementation. All S1–S5 and M1–M4 addressed in the plan before any code was written — notably: `LoadGroups` takes `storage.FS` (not direct `os.ReadFile`) to match the existing `metamodel.Load` contract, groups are NOT auto-loaded by `Load`, and `ValidateEncryption` is a method (not a free function).

## Code review

## Summary
Updates PingMod to support the latest plugin interface versions (v19-v22) and adds configuration to enable/disable the mod. The plugin interface has been refactored to use a single `IPluginSelf` parameter in `PluginInit` instead of four separate interface pointers.

## Key Changes

### Plugin Interface Updates
- Updated `plugin_interface.h` to reflect new interface versions:
  - v19: Introduced `IPluginSelf` consolidating all subsystem pointers (name, version, logger, config, scanner, hooks)
  - v20: Added world end-play notifications (`OnBeforeWorldEndPlay`, `OnAfterWorldEndPlay`)
  - v21: Added `IPluginNativePointers` for raw hooked function addresses
  - v22: Added `IPluginHttpServer` for static file and HTTP request handling
- Updated `PLUGIN_INTERFACE_VERSION_MIN` from 14 to 19 (ABI break)
- Updated `PLUGIN_INTERFACE_VERSION_MAX` from 16 to 22
- Added new callback typedefs: `PluginWorldEndPlayCallback`, `PluginNetworkMessageCallback`, `PluginNetworkServerMessageCallback`
- Added new interface structs: `IPluginNetworkChannel`, `IPluginNativePointers`, `IPluginHttpServer`
- Added `IPluginSelf` struct to encapsulate plugin identity and subsystem access

### PingMod Implementation
- Updated `PluginInit` signature to accept single `IPluginSelf* self` parameter instead of four separate pointers
- Added "Enabled" boolean config option to allow enabling/disable the mod without code changes
- Increased default `MaxPingDistanceM` from 500 to 1000 metres
- Added `IsEnabled()` helper function to check config setting
- Modified `ApplyPingDistancePatch()` to skip patching if mod is disabled
- Updated config schema entry count from 1 to 2
- Updated plugin version from 1.0.0 to 1.1.0
- Updated plugin description to reflect new enable/disable capability
- Updated initialization logging to display enabled status

### CI/CD
- Modified GitHub Actions workflow to trigger on `dev/*` branches instead of just `main`

## Implementation Details
- The plugin now gracefully handles being disabled via config, logging an info message and skipping the patch application
- All interface pointer access now goes through the `IPluginSelf` structure passed to `PluginInit`
- Config initialization and logging now use the consolidated interface pointers from `self`

author: dannydesert
body:
## Problem
AO container crash-loops (exit code 1) on task def :28/:29. Old :26 still running.

**Root cause:** `GITHUB_TOKEN` secret was added to AO's task def. AO uses GitHub App auth (`token-manager.mjs` → dynamic tokens). The `GITHUB_TOKEN` env var conflicts — `gh auth login` ignores the piped App token and uses the env var instead. With `set -e`, the entrypoint dies silently with zero diagnostic output.

## Evidence
- Task def :26 (no GITHUB_TOKEN secret) = works fine
- Task def :29 (has GITHUB_TOKEN secret) = crash-loops
- CloudWatch shows only 3 log lines before crash — classic `set -e` silent kill

## Fix
Remove `GITHUB_TOKEN` from AO's secrets block. GitHub App auth is the primary and correct method.

## IMPORTANT
This change requires `terraform apply` to take effect. CI only rebuilds Docker images and registers new task defs — it does NOT apply Terraform changes.

author: rockharr
body:
## 🚨 Severity: CRITICAL
  
## 💡 Vulnerability
The application used the cryptographically insecure `Math.random()` to generate sensitive transaction and order identifiers in the payment confirmation and receipt screens. This leads to predictable identifiers that could be subject to enumeration attacks or unintended collisions.

## 🎯 Impact
Predictable IDs can allow malicious actors to infer order velocity, guess transaction IDs to access other users' receipt details (if not strictly isolated by auth), or cause database/logic collisions if identifiers overlap.

## 🔧 Fix
Replaced the `Math.random()` calls with the Web Crypto API (`crypto.randomUUID()`) inside `components/PaymentsScreen.tsx`. Additionally, wrapped the ID generation within a `useState` lazy initializer (e.g., `useState(() => crypto.randomUUID().split('-')[0].toUpperCase())`) so that state updates or component re-renders do not unexpectedly regenerate the identifier currently displayed to the user.

## ✅ Verification
- Analyzed codebase for `Math.random()` usage for identifiers.
- Updated `PaymentsScreen.tsx` and validated syntax via `npm run lint`.
- Ran full test suite to ensure no regressions were introduced.
- Documented findings in `.Jules/sentinel.md` as per Sentinel directives.

body: This PR changes the rendering logic of booking pages. Instead of displaying the rendered version of the booking page on the operator page, we do now render it on demand in the operator page context. With some additional changes in this PR, this will fix many issues: - Irrelevant sections of booking expanders are no longer rendered to the DOM. This fixes an issue where results where displayed in the search, but were not available on the page itself (see issue description below) - Images can be rendered out of context now. If you want to render the an image in another page context (for example to render a booking image on an operator page), just write: ``` ![DB reservation booking](db_reservation.de.webp) {page="booking/db-website"} ``` - Footnotes of booking expanders are *finally* scoped globally and are no longer rendered locally inside the expander - The heading map does now properly handle expanders, can be checked via the HeadingsMap extension - Content of the following expander doesn't count as element from the previous expander in the search (as there was no heading in between, so it counted as element of the last heading of the previous expander) - Train categories and booking platforms title matches are ranked higher in the search - If the result targets a booking or train category expander, the page automatically scrolls to it. - Similar to the already existing behavior with train category expanders, it's now possible to link to booking platforms directly, e. g. https://deploy-preview-856--fipguide.netlify.app/de/operator/oebb/#oebb-website works now. --- ### Issue description So far, we only hide some booking sections using `display: none` in the CSS of booking expanders. The issue is: Even if hidden, the content is still indexed for the search. This PR changes the approach to no longer render the irrelevant sections to the DOM by storing the rendered sections in the page store. Steps to reproduce the search issue: 1. Search for "Website der Deutschen Bahn" on the German page 2. Select "Reservierungen": 3. The section doesn't exist, no scrolling happens --- Resolves #887 Resolves #462

author: kasnder
body:
## Summary

Addresses two reported overlay artifacts: (1) overlays briefly disappearing and reappearing while still in the target app, and (2) overlays staying visible after leaving the app.

### Flicker — `onAccessibilityEvent` is too eager to clear
- Only `TYPE_WINDOW_STATE_CHANGED` from a foreign package now counts as a leave signal. Content changes and scrolls from `systemui` (e.g. status bar updates from an arriving notification) or the launcher no longer trigger a clear while the target app is still the active window underneath.
- Foreign window-state changes are debounced by 150ms; any subsequent event from the target package cancels the pending clear. This absorbs transient focus changes such as a briefly pulled notification shade.

### Race — `OverlayManager` add/remove was partly async, partly sync
- All `OverlayManager` operations are now synchronous on the caller's thread (always main for the accessibility service). A queued `addView` can no longer run after a `clear` and leave an orphan view attached but untracked.
- `clearOverlays` can no longer empty the tracker list before `removeView` has actually detached the views.
- `forceClearAllOverlays` collapses to a `clearAllOverlays` alias since both paths are now equivalent.

### Cleanup
- Pending clear runnable is cancelled in all teardown paths (`reloadRulesFromSource`, `reevaluateBlockingState`, screen off, `onInterrupt`, `onDestroy`).

### Considered and rejected
- Per-element grace period (e.g. keep an overlay alive 500ms past its node's last appearance): would pin overlays at stale positions while a feed scrolls beneath them (Instagram-style), which is a worse artifact than a brief flicker.
- Widening `info.packageNames = null` to receive events for unmonitored apps: would fix the case where a switch never delivers an event to the service, but increases battery cost on every other app.

## Test plan
- [ ] Open WhatsApp with a rule active; pull and release the notification shade quickly. Overlay should not disappear.
- [ ] Open WhatsApp with a rule active; let a notification arrive without pulling the shade. Overlay should not flicker.
- [ ] Scroll the Instagram feed (or similar) with a rule active. Overlays should follow scrolled elements without sticking at stale positions.
- [ ] Switch from a rule app to launcher. Overlays should clear within ~150ms.
- [ ] Switch from a rule app to another rule app. Overlays for the first should clear, the second's should appear.
- [ ] Lock screen, then unlock and return to the rule app. Overlays should re-evaluate correctly.

The previous safety layer auto-cancelled destructive tool calls in the web UI because stdin is not a TTY. This change wires up a proper async confirmation flow:

- tools/registry.py: add skip_confirmation kwarg to dispatch(); when True the caller has already obtained consent so the stdin prompt is skipped (bash blacklist and path allowlist are still enforced)
- agent.py: run_events() accepts an optional confirm_destructive async callback; when provided and the tool is destructive, yields a 'confirmation_required' SSE event, awaits the callback, then either dispatches with skip_confirmation=True or returns the cancellation string
- server.py: stores a per-session asyncio.Future in _pending_confirmations; new POST /confirm endpoint resolves it; the callback passed to run_events awaits that future (5 min timeout, cleaned up in finally)
- static/index.html: handles 'confirmation_required' SSE event by rendering an orange confirmation card with Allow / Cancel buttons; sendConfirm() POSTs to /confirm and updates the card status; finaliseToolCard() removes the buttons and colours cancelled results red

## Summary

Fix filtered search pagination so notes matching tag/type/repo/ext filters are not dropped just because they fall outside the initial buffered FTS/vector candidate window.

## Root cause

`LocalOperations.search()` fetched only `offset + limit + FILTER_BUFFER` candidates before applying filters in memory. Broad searches with selective filters could therefore miss valid matches beyond that small raw candidate set and under-report `total`.

## Changes

- Added a small `hasFilter()` helper for search filter detection.
- Fetch the full matched candidate set when filters are active, while preserving the existing buffered fast path for unfiltered searches.
- Added a regression test where the filtered match appears beyond the previous candidate buffer.

## Summary

Release v0.96.0 — session-restore fix so new windows no longer duplicate the primary window.

author: pirapira
body:
## Summary
Add `@[irreducible]` to both scratch-region predicates, matching the pattern already applied to `divN4MaxSkipStackPost` / `modN4MaxSkipStackPost` (#375) and the `fullDivN4MaxSkipPost` / `denormDivPost` / `loopSetupPost` bundles.

Purpose: once unfolded, each of `divScratchValues` / `divScratchOwn` expands to a 15-atom `**`-chain. Leaving them reducible means every `xperm_hyp` call against a spec post that mentions them decomposes the whole chain, bloating the atom count well past the xperm scaling limit (~25 atoms). Marking them irreducible keeps xperm treating them as a single opaque atom.

Existing call sites continue to work — `divScratchValues_unfold` already goes through the irreducibility via `delta` (this PR adjusts its proof from bare `rfl` to `delta divScratchValues; rfl`). All downstream consumers either use the helper lemmas or `unfold` explicitly.

Stacks on #376 → #378. Continues progress toward #61.

Follow-up to #630, #636, #638, #639. Chips away at the `syntest` failures tracked in #631.

## Root cause

`exec_escape`'s `meta_content_scope` pop-skip is gated on `current_syntax_version >= 2`, but that helper reads the top of the stack — the *embedded* syntax at escape time, not the host. When a v2 host embeds a v1 guest (e.g. Rails embedding Ruby), the gate misfires and emits a spurious `Pop` for a scope the v2 host's `embed_scope_replaces` had already suppressed on push. Downstream pops then strip the host's own scopes, cascading into assertion failures across attribute boundaries.

## Fix

Drop the version gate. `embed_scope_replaces` is only set by v2 hosts in `yaml_load` (gated there on `state.version >= 2`), so the flag alone is sufficient and symmetric with the push path (which reads the embedder's version).

## Impact

Baselines in `testdata/known_syntest_failures*.txt`:

| File | Oniguruma | Fancy |
|---|---:|---:|
| `Rails/tests/syntax_test_rails.css.erb` | 83 → 0 | 83 → 0 |
| `Rails/tests/syntax_test_rails.js.erb`  | 37 → 0 | 37 → 0 |
| `Rails/tests/syntax_test_rails.sql.erb` | 8 → 0  | n/a |
| `Rails/tests/syntax_test_rails.html.erb` | 264 → 23 | 264 → 23 |
| `Rails/tests/syntax_test_rails.haml`    | 86 → 65 | n/a |

Net: 390 assertions closed on Oniguruma, 369 on fancy-regex. No regressions.

## Tests

New synthetic regression `v2_host_embedding_v1_guest_skips_meta_content_pop_on_escape` in `src/parsing/parser.rs`.

Refs: #631

author: slai-eddie
body:
## Summary

Fixes #779.

Conan 2 clients probe `GET /v1/ping` on every remote to read the `x-conan-server-capabilities` header and decide whether the server supports the revisions protocol — even when using the v2 API for every other request. See `conan/internal/rest/rest_client.py::_get_api`. The backend's Conan router only mounted `/v2/ping`, so the probe 404'd and every Conan 2 upload aborted with the opaque `NotFoundException: b''`.

This PR aliases `/v1/ping` to the same handler as `/v2/ping`. The response — 200 with `x-conan-server-capabilities: revisions` and an empty body — is identical across both protocol versions, so one handler serves both routes.

Scope is intentionally narrow: only the capability-probe endpoint is added. No other `/v1/*` routes are introduced. Conan 2 uses `v1/ping` solely for capability discovery and then speaks v2 for the rest of the protocol.

Note: after this fix, `conan upload` succeeds, but `conan install` still fails because the recipe/package files-listing endpoints (`.../revisions/{rev}/files`) are also missing — filed separately as #780.

## Test Checklist
- [x] Unit tests added/updated — added `ping_returns_revisions_capability` asserting the handler always advertises `revisions` in the capability header
- [ ] Integration tests added/updated (if applicable) — N/A, the route wiring is trivial and the existing capability-header test prevents the main regression
- [ ] E2E tests added/updated (if applicable) — N/A, no `scripts/native-tests/test-conan.sh` exists in the repo
- [x] Manually tested locally — reproduced the failure on `:latest`, applied the patch, rebuilt the backend image, reran `conan remote login` + `conan create` + `conan upload` against a local stack; upload now completes with both recipe and package revisions uploaded
- [x] No regressions in existing tests — `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `cargo test --workspace --lib` (7815 passed, 0 failed) all green

## API Changes
- [ ] New endpoints have `#[utoipa::path]` annotations
- [ ] Request/response types have `#[derive(ToSchema)]`
- [ ] OpenAPI spec validates: `cargo test --lib test_openapi_spec_is_valid`
- [ ] Migration is reversible (if applicable)
- [x] N/A - no API changes — the added route is an alias of an existing handler; no new request/response types and no public API surface change beyond unblocking Conan 2 clients that were already expected to work

author: noobygains
body:
## Summary

Implements **F3** of the `initiative:self-teaching-paperclip` initiative — closes #19.

Adds a per-project CEO overlay system: overlay MD files stored in `<repoPath>/.paperclip/ceo/` are merged over server defaults at hire time, giving each managed repo its own CEO personality without forking the server. Also adds `projectId` to the `agents` table so the hire path can resolve `agent → project → repoPath`.

- New column `agents.project_id` (migration `0064`, nullable FK to `projects.id`).
- New service `ceoOverlayService` — `readCeoOverlayFile` + `writeCeoOverlayFiles` (safe, idempotent FS helpers).
- Extended `loadDefaultAgentInstructionsBundle` to accept optional `projectRepoPath`; CEO overlay files take precedence over server defaults when present, fall through to defaults when absent.
- Hire path in `agents.ts` resolves `projectRepoPath` from `agent.projectId → projectWorkspaces.cwd` before calling the bundle loader.
- New Express route `POST /api/projects/:projectId/ceo-overlay` (board-authed) to write overlay files into the managed repo.
- New MCP tool `paperclipWriteCeoOverlay` (`SAFE_WRITE`) + client helper `writeCeoOverlay`.
- `projectId?: string | null` added to the shared `Agent` type.

## Downstream

Unblocks:
- #26 (O2 — onboard portfolio, which needs both F1 and F3 on master)
- #27 (S1 — self-teaching loop, which needs F3 for per-project CEO customization)

## Deviations from plan

1. **Migration number is `0064` not `0063`** — plan assumed F1 (`0063_user_profiles`) was already merged to master at write time, but F1 was in a parallel PR. Correct number `0064` used since `0063` will come from F1's merge.
2. **`project.workspaces?.[0]?.cwd` access** — the `projects` table has no embedded `workspaces` array in Drizzle; `projectWorkspaces` is a separate table. Corrected to a separate `db.select().from(projectWorkspaces).where(...)` query ordered by `desc(isPrimary), asc(createdAt)` — matching the pattern in `services/projects.ts`.
3. **Schema circular reference** — `projects.ts` already imports `agents.ts` (`leadAgentId` FK); adding the reverse import (`agents.ts → projects.ts`) caused TypeScript circular inference. Resolved by adding the `project_id` column WITHOUT a Drizzle `.references()` call (FK is enforced via the SQL migration instead, which is correct). Comment in schema explains the decision.
4. **Test pattern** — The plan suggested a DB test helper (`createTestDb`) that doesn't exist in this repo. Integration tests instead use `os.tmpdir()` / `fs.mkdtemp` for FS-based testing of the overlay service + bundle loader (no DB required for this feature's core logic).

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm --filter @paperclipai/db typecheck` — clean
- [x] `pnpm --filter @paperclipai/shared typecheck` — clean
- [x] `pnpm --filter @paperclipai/server typecheck` — clean

- [x] `pnpm typecheck` (whole repo) — clean
- [x] CEO overlay integration tests — 8/8 pass (`server/src/__tests__/ceo-overlay.test.ts`)
- [x] MCP tools tests — 21/21 pass (`packages/mcp-server/src/tools.test.ts`)
- [x] `pnpm --filter @paperclipai/mcp-server build` — clean
- [x] `pnpm db:migrate` — migration `0064_agent_project` applies cleanly

## Known note

The `agent-hire-authority-routes.test.ts` first test (`grants canCreateAgents=true when hiring a cto`) loads onboarding-asset files from disk and can occasionally run close to the 5000ms default Vitest timeout on a cold module load. This is pre-existing flakiness (also present on master); the test consistently passes with a 12s timeout or on subsequent warm runs.

## Description

JSON-RPC 2.0 forbids servers from replying to notifications (messages with no `id`), and MCP Streamable HTTP requires HTTP 202 Accepted with no body for that case. The /mcp handler previously fell through to the method-dispatch else-branch and returned a JSON-RPC error `-32601 Method not found` for `notifications/initialized`.

Tolerant clients (Claude Code) ignore the response; strict clients (Codex's rmcp) treat the resulting transport behavior as a handshake failure and fail to start the MCP server.

author: aminsaedi
body:
## Summary

Fixes identical meta descriptions across practitioner profile sub-tabs by moving meta dispatch to the parent `ProfileComponent` via Router `NavigationEnd` events.

### Problem
When navigating between profile sub-tabs (`/feed`, `/service`, `/review`, `/promotion`, `/event`), all tabs returned the same meta description as the main about tab. Child component `setMeta()` calls from PRs #84/#85 were not reliably firing on sub-tab navigation due to Angular's component lifecycle behavior when the parent route is reused.

### Solution
- Added a `NavigationEnd` subscription in `ProfileComponent` that calls a new `setMetaForActiveTab()` method
- `setMetaForActiveTab()` inspects the current URL and sets tab-specific meta (title, description, OG image) for each sub-tab
- Falls back to the existing `setMetaForAbout()` for the default about tab
- All existing `setMetaForAbout()` call sites now go through `setMetaForActiveTab()`, ensuring correct meta regardless of which tab is active when profile data loads

### Affected tabs
| Tab | Title pattern | Description |
|-----|--------------|-------------|
| About | `{name} in {city} \| PromptHealth` | `{name} is {type} offering {services}.` |
| Service | `Service by {name} \| PromptHealth` | `{name} offers healthcare services in {city}...` |
| Feed | `Contents from {name} \| PromptHealth` | `Read health articles, tips, and posts...` |
| Review | `{name} review \| PromptHealth` | `Read patient reviews for {name}...` |
| Promotion | `Special offers from {name} \| PromptHealth` | `View special offers and promotions...` |
| Events | `Upcoming events from {name} \| PromptHealth` | `Browse upcoming healthcare events...` |
| Past Events | `Past events from {name} \| PromptHealth` | `View past events and workshops...` |

### Files changed
- `src/app/social/profile/profile.component.ts` — added `setMetaForActiveTab()`, `NavigationEnd` subscription

body:
## Summary
Closes all 8 open Dependabot alerts (6 high, 2 moderate) by bumping/adding \`overrides\` entries. No production source code changed — security-only dependency shimming.

## Alerts addressed

### Mobile (7)
| Package | Action | CVE / GHSA | Severity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| node-forge | override 1.3.3 → ^1.4.0 | CVE-2026-33891 (modInverse DoS) | high |
| node-forge | ↳ | CVE-2026-33894 (RSA-PKCS forgery) | high |
| node-forge | ↳ | CVE-2026-33895 (Ed25519 forgery) | high |
| node-forge | ↳ | CVE-2026-33896 (cert chain bypass) | high |
| tar | override 7.5.7 → ^7.5.8 | CVE-2026-26960 (hardlink escape) | high |
| @xmldom/xmldom | new override ^0.8.12 | CVE-2026-34601 (CDATA injection) | high |
| follow-redirects | new override ^1.16.0 | GHSA-r4q5-vmmm-2653 (auth header leak) | moderate |

### Backend (1)
| Package | Action | CVE | Severity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| @hono/node-server | new override ^1.19.13 | CVE-2026-39406 (serveStatic bypass) | moderate |

## Notes on approach
- **@xmldom/xmldom**: the 0.7.13 transitive path via older \`@expo/plist@0.2.x\` had no 0.7-line patch available. Forcing it to 0.8.12+ is the only path to a patched version; 0.8 is API-compatible for the attribute/CDATA surface @expo/plist uses.
- **follow-redirects**: axios 1.15.x bundles 1.15.11; adding an override upgrades the transitive without changing our axios constraint.
- **@hono/node-server**: only reaches us via \`prisma → @prisma/dev\` dev tooling; still alert-worthy so we close it anyway.

author: jlin53882
body:
## Summary

This PR implements a Redis-based distributed lock to solve the high concurrency lock contention problem identified in Issue #643.

## Problem

When captureAssistant=true and sessionMemory.enabled=true:
- Multiple agents write to memory simultaneously
- File lock cannot handle high concurrency
- 200 concurrent writes -> only 6% success

## Solution

Add src/redis-lock.ts with:
- Token-based lock acquisition (prevents race conditions)
- Lua script for safe release (only releases if token matches)
- Automatic fallback to file lock when Redis unavailable
- 60s TTL with exponential backoff

## Test Results

| Concurrency | File Lock | Redis Lock |
|-------------|-----------|------------|
| 10 | 100% | 100% |
| 20 | 55% | 100% |
| 50 | 22% | 100% |
| 200 | 6% | 97.5% |

**15x improvement!**

## Tests Added

- 	est/lock-extreme-concurrent.test.mjs - 10/20/50/200 concurrent
- 	est/lock-production-simulation.test.mjs - Real-world simulation
- 	est/lock-bottleneck-identification.test.mjs - Find threshold
- 	est/lock-200-concurrent.test.mjs - 200 concurrent test
- 	est/redis-lock-real.test.mjs - Real Redis test
- 	est/redis-lock-edge-cases.test.mjs - 10 edge cases
- 	est/redis-lock-optimized.test.mjs - Parallel optimization
- 	est/redis-lock-simulated.test.mjs - Simulation

## Required

Add to package.json:
\\\
npm install ioredis
\\\

## Related

- Extends #643
- See also #659

author: copilot
body:
`Weekly Model Training` failed after a long run due to a push race with other workflows writing to `main`. While fixing that, this PR also corrects Python heredoc indentation regressions introduced in PR #42 and updates the accuracy dashboard to better communicate low sample-size rolling metrics.

- **Workflow syntax fixes (PR #42 regressions)**
  - Fixed invalid Python indentation in embedded heredocs in:
    - `.github/workflows/accuracy.yml`
    - `.github/workflows/auto-retrain.yml` (all affected heredocs, including model-compare/history-write blocks)
  - Logic is unchanged; whitespace-only reindent for syntactic correctness.

- **Serialized writes to `main` for long-running jobs**
  - Added the same concurrency queue to all primary main-writer workflows:
    - `train-model.yml`, `auto-retrain.yml`, `accuracy.yml`, `generate-predictions.yml`
  - Uses queueing semantics (no cancellation):
    ```yaml
    concurrency:
      group: main-branch-writer
      cancel-in-progress: false
    ```

- **Defense-in-depth before push**
  - Added `git pull --rebase --autostash origin main` immediately before `git push` in workflows that commit to `main`:
    - `train-model.yml`, `auto-retrain.yml`, `accuracy.yml`, `generate-predictions.yml`
    - `fetch-history.yml`, `build-features.yml`, `fetch-tickers.yml`, `weekly-report.yml`
    - `walk-forward.yml`

- **Accuracy dashboard sparse-data UX**
  - Updated rolling 7/30/90-day cards in `js/ui/accuracy-dashboard.js` to show partial-window context:
    - “based on N of X days — needs ~Y more days for a stable estimate”
  - Added a chart note when data is still sparse:
    - “Only N days of accuracy data so far…”
  - Rolling calculations themselves were not changed.

- **Example snippet (new push pattern)**
  ```bash
  git diff --cached --quiet && echo "No changes to commit" && exit 0
  git commit -m "..."
  git pull --rebase --autostash origin main
  git push
  ```

- **screenshot**
  - Updated accuracy dashboard empty-state messaging:
    - https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5d9e6b9a-0904-4485-a47c-7fa2a4c11e8f

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

## Context

The most recent `Weekly Model Training` workflow run (#19) failed at the `git push` step after a successful 3.5-hour BiLSTM training run:

```
! [rejected]        main -> main (fetch first)
hint: Updates were rejected because the remote contains work that you do not have locally.
error: failed to push some refs to 'https://github.com/Gandalf-the-shiz/Nostradamus'
```

Root cause: `accuracy.yml` (daily at 23:55 UTC) and `train-model.yml` (Sunday 03:00 UTC, but also triggered by `workflow_run` after `Build Feature Matrix`) can both be writing to `main` at the same time. The training workflow runs for ~3.5 hours and any commit landing on `main` during that window will reject its push.

While auditing the workflows for this fix, I also noticed that **PR #42 introduced broken Python indentation in two workflow heredocs** that will fail with `IndentationError` on the next scheduled run. These need to be fixed in the same PR.

## Required changes

### 1. Fix broken Python indentation in `.github/workflows/accuracy.yml`

In the `Check rolling accuracy and trigger retraining if needed` step, the heredoc Python block (around lines 58–87) has over-indented lines inside the `try:` block. Specifically lines 77–81 are indented one level too deep relative to the surrounding `if not recent:` branch. The correct indentation is to match the rest of the `try:` body. The block should look like:

```python
flag=$(python - <<'EOF'
import json, sys
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone

log_path  = "data/accuracy/accuracy-log.json"
threshold = 0.53   # below this → trigger auto-retrain
try:
    with open(log_path) as f:
        data = json.load(f)
    entries = data.get("entries", [])
    if not entries:
        print("true"); sys.exit(0)
    cutoff = datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(days=30)
    recent = [
        e for e in entries
        if datetime.fromisoformat(e["date"].replace("Z", "+00:00")) >= cutoff
    ]
    if not recent:
        print("true"); sys.exit(0)
    sample_size = sum(int(e.get("total", 0) or 0) for e in recent if e.get("hitRate") is not None)
    correct = sum(int(e.get("correct", 0) or 0) for e in recent if e.get("hitRate") is not None)
    hit_rate = (correct / sample_size) if sample_size > 0 else 0.0
    import sys as _sys
    print(f"Rolling 30-day accuracy: {hit_rate:.4f} ({correct}/{sample_size})", file=_sys.stderr)
    print("true" if hit_rate < threshold else "false")
except Exception as exc:
    import sys as _sys
    print(f"Error reading accuracy log ({exc}); defaulting to false", file=_sys.stderr)
    print("false")
EOF
)
```

### 2. Fix broken Python indentation in `.github/workflows/auto-retrain.yml`

Two heredocs in this file are even more broken than `accuracy.yml`:

- The `Check rolling accuracy` step (around lines 35–87) — over-indented `sample_size`, `correct`, `hit_rate`, and the second `print` call inside the `try:` block.
- The `Extract retrain flag` step (around lines 89–123) — same pattern of over-indented `sample_size`/`correct`/`hit_rate` lines.
- The `Compare models and promote if better` step (around lines 139–223) — entire branches inside `if prev_meta_path.exists():` are over-indented (lines 177–205) and the entire `history_path` write block at the end (lines 207–222) is over-indented one level too deep.

Re-indent every block inside these heredocs so the Python is syntactically valid. Keep the logic identical — only fix whitespace. After the fix, the YAML must still pass `python -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/auto-retrain.yml'))"` and the embedded Python must compile cleanly.

You can verify each heredoc by extracting the Python with `sed -n '/<<.EOF./,/^EOF$/p'` and running `python -m py_compile` on it.

### 3. Add `concurrency:` blocks to serialize workflows that commit to `main`

Add the same `concurrency` group to all four workflows that push to `main`, so only one runs at a time:

- `.github/workflows/train-model.yml`
- `.github/workflows/auto-retrain.yml`
- `.github/workflows/accuracy.yml`
- `.github/workflows/generate-predictions.yml`

Use this block at the top of each file (right after the `on:` block):

```yaml
concurrency:
  group: main-branch-writer
  cancel-in-progress: false
```

`cancel-in-progress: false` is critical — we want to QUEUE not cancel, otherwise a daily accuracy run could cancel a 3-hour training job.

### 4. Add defense-in-depth `git pull --rebase` before each `git push`

Even with the concurrency block, add `git pull --rebase --autostash origin main` immediately before each `git push` in all four workflows above (and `fetch-history.yml`, `build-features.yml`, `fetch-tickers.yml`, `weekly-report.yml` — any workflow that pushes). This catches edge cases where concurrency keys differ or where a manual commit lands during the window.

The pattern for each commit-and-push step:

```bash
git diff --cached --quiet && echo "No changes to commit" && exit 0
git commit -m "..."
git pull --rebase --au...

</details>

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## Summary

Implements **ARCH-A5** (issue #135) under the ARCH-A parent workstream (#123) and the ARCH-2026 meta (#122): the **Consistency Checker** that fires at every stage boundary, every gate, and every tool call. It compares a stage's **derivation revision** (the Preference Ledger revision the stage was built against) to the **current ledger revision** and, on drift, emits a structured `LedgerDrift` signal into the blackboard for the re-manifestation executor (ARCH-A6, #136) to consume.

Scope is deliberately narrow — **detect + signal only**. Re-manifestation planning / validation / execution (A6), and the per-stage derivation-tag mechanism itself (ARCH-B1, #137), are separate tickets and are explicitly not built here. ARCH-B1's tagging surface is **stubbed** in this PR via `record_stage_derivation(...)` writing to a well-known state key, per issue #135's guidance ("accept the value from state under a well-known key, and if missing, treat as 'untagged' and emit a warning rather than failing").

Reads diagrams 1 and 2a in `docs/ARCHITECTURE_DIAGRAMS.md` (fetched from PR #121 branch, since that file is not yet on `main`): the checker implements the `CHECK → CMP{rev match vs drift} → IMP` edge in diagram 2a, stopping at the edge between the checker and the impact analyzer.

### What landed

- `server/callbacks/consistency_checker.py`
  - `LedgerDrift` — frozen dataclass with `stage_name`, `artifact_ids`, `from_rev`, `to_rev`, `new_records`. JSON round-trips via `to_dict()`; validates that `to_rev > from_rev ≥ 0` and that `stage_name` is a non-empty string at construction time.
  - `STAGE_DERIVATIONS_KEY = "_stage_derivations"` — well-known blackboard key holding `{stage_name: {"revision": int, "artifact_ids": [str, ...]}}`, either as a raw dict (test-friendly) or JSON-encoded (blackboard convention). ARCH-B1 will own this surface; until then, `record_stage_derivation(...)` is a convenience stub so A5 is exercisable end-to-end.
  - `LEDGER_DRIFT_SIGNALS_KEY = "ledger_drift_signals"` — JSON-encoded list of drift signals, appended in insertion order; drained by A6.
  - `check_consistency(state, stage_name)` — core function. Returns `None` for up-to-date / untagged stages; returns (and enqueues) a `LedgerDrift` on drift. Raises `RuntimeError` on missing ledger state or a revision decrease (append-only invariant).
  - `after_agent_consistency_check(callback_context)` — ADK `after_agent_callback` registration surface (Timeline Guardian pattern).
  - `before_tool_consistency_check(tool, args, tool_context)` — ADK `before_tool_callback` registration surface; returns `None` so tool calls proceed (drift is a signal, not an error).
  - `check_consistency_at_gate(state, stage_name)` — plain callable for the gate-polling / human L4 path (ARCH-H5).
  - `pending_drift_signals(state)` — read-only queue drainer for A6 wiring and tests.
  - Stage name resolution mirrors existing callbacks: `context.agent_name` → `state["pipeline_phase"]` → `"pipeline"` fallback.

- `server/tests/test_consistency_checker.py` — **35 unit tests** covering:
  - **Drift detection**: new records strictly after derivation revision, signal appended to blackboard as JSON, multiple signals accumulate in order, carried `artifact_ids` / `from_rev` / `to_rev` match the derivation tag and current revision.
  - **No-drift**: up-to-date stage is a no-op, empty ledger is a no-op, detection never mutates the ledger or the stage-derivation tag.
  - **Untagged stages** (pre-B1): log a single warning, return `None`, no signal enqueued.
  - **Fail-loud invariants**: missing `PREFERENCE_LEDGER_KEY` → `RuntimeError`; derivation revision > current revision → `RuntimeError` ("append-only"); malformed derivation blob (bad JSON, wrong top-level type, non-mapping entry, missing `revision`, non-int `revision`, bare-string `artifact_ids`) → loud `ValueError` / `TypeError`; malformed drift queue → `ValueError`.
  - **`LedgerDrift` record invariants**: frozen, forward-revisions required, non-empty stage name, integer revisions, round-trips through `pending_drift_signals`.
  - **`record_stage_derivation` stub**: defaults to current revision, preserves existing artifact ids on re-tag, rejects bare strings / non-strings / empty names / negative revisions.
  - **Registration surface**: after-agent callback uses `agent_name`, falls back to `pipeline_phase`, never short-circuits; before-tool callback returns `None` in both drift and no-drift paths; gate entry point is equivalent to `check_consistency`; all three surfaces propagate the missing-ledger invariant violation without swallowing it.

### Invariant compliance (per meta #122 DoD)

- **ADK idioms** — no new `Agent` subclass introduced (the checker is a callback surface, not an agent), mirroring the Timeline Guardian pattern. Cross-stage state stays on the blackboard under the dedicated `_stage_derivations` / `ledger_drift_signals` / `preference_ledger` keys — no direct cross-module imports between stages.
- **Stage-boundary checks via `after_agent_callback`** — primary registration surface.
- **Tools as plain callables** — before-tool callback is a plain function matching `server/callbacks/before_tool.py`'s signature.
- **Fail loud, no silent degradation** — every invalid input (missing ledger, malformed derivation, non-int revision, revision decrease, poisoned signal queue) raises. Untagged stages only warn because B1 is not yet built (explicit carve-out per #135).
- **Detection-only** — tested invariant: `check_consistency` never mutates the ledger or the stage-derivation tag. Re-manifestation is ARCH-A6.

### Test evidence

```
server$ poetry run pytest tests/test_consistency_checker.py -q
...................................                                     [100%]
35 passed in 0.09s

server$ poetry run pytest tests/test_preference_ledger.py tests/test_consistency_checker.py -q
..................................................................      [100%]
66 passed in 0.12s
```

### Deviations from spec

- **`docs/ARCHITECTURE_DIAGRAMS.md` still not on `main`.** Fetched diagrams 1 + 2a from the `devin/1776498699-architecture-doc` branch of PR #121 (still open) and used them as the canonical reference. Same deviation noted in PR #161 for A1; flagging here too so it can land separately without blocking A5.
- **Stubbed `record_stage_derivation(...)` helper.** ARCH-B1 (#137) will own the per-stage `ledger_revision_at_derivation` tagging surface. Until B1 lands, this PR provides a tiny helper writing to the well-known `_stage_derivations` state key so A5 can be exercised end-to-end in tests and called by downstream wiring. B1 can either replace or delegate to it; the storage shape (`{stage: {"revision", "artifact_ids"}}`) is stable.
- **No registration on real ADK agents / tools in this PR.** The callback factories are exported and covered by tests; wiring them into the master pipeline's agents and tool lists is a follow-up (part of the B1/B2 workstream) so that the wiring lands together with a real tagging source.

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

Risk: yellow (new invariant surface on the hot path, but detection-only — cannot fail the pipeline except on genuinely malformed state).

- [ ] Confirm the `LedgerDrift` shape (`stage_name`, `artifact_ids`, `from_rev`, `to_rev`, `new_records`) is what ARCH-A6 (#136) expects to consume. It is derived from diagram 2a but A6 has not yet been written — if A6 wants a different carrier, easier to agree now than after wiring.
- [ ] Sanity-check the "untagged stage → warn, no drift" carve-out. Once ARCH-B1 (#137) lands, this branch should become dead code in practice; confirm the explicit carve-out (with the log line identifying it as a pre-B1 pass-through) is acceptable as a temporary bridge.
- [ ] Spot-check the fail-loud matrix: missing ledger state, revision decrease, malformed derivation blob, malformed drift queue — each test asserts a specific exception type and message substring.

### Notes

- The before-tool

author: alphabetc1
body:
## Motivation

The FlashInfer attention backend does not accept a `sinks` kwarg, but hybrid-SWA models like `GptOssForCausalLM` and `MiMoV2FlashForCausalLM` (when `add_{swa,full}_attention_sink_bias=True`) pass per-head sink scalars to the attention call. Two auto-selection paths used to fall back to `flashinfer` without considering this, which could leave sink models on an unsupported backend.

## Modifications

- Add `ModelConfig.has_attention_sinks`, derived in `_derive_hybrid_model` via a new `_detect_attention_sinks()` helper:
  - `GptOssForCausalLM` always has sinks
  - `MiMoV2FlashForCausalLM` / `MiMoV2MTP` have sinks only when `add_swa_attention_sink_bias` or `add_full_attention_sink_bias` is set on `hf_text_config`
- In `ServerArgs._get_default_attn_backend`, the non-MLA fallback branch now picks `triton` instead of `flashinfer` when `model_config.has_attention_sinks` is true
- In `ServerArgs._resolve_io_decode_attention_compatibility`, the hicache kernel-io + FA3 avoidance path applies the same check before setting `decode_attention_backend`

## Scope of Behavior Change

Only the implicit auto-selection paths are affected:

| Scenario | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Sink model, no `--attention-backend`, non-Hopper / non-Blackwell GPU | flashinfer (unsupported) | triton |
| Sink model, hicache `io_backend=kernel` with FA3 effective decode | flashinfer (unsupported) | triton |
| Non-sink models, all configurations | unchanged | unchanged |
| Explicit `--attention-backend ...` | unchanged | unchanged |

## Checklist

- [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

author: dcramer
body:
Keep the bottle classifier boundary focused on match, create, and no_match, and leave clarification or correction workflows to downstream proposal handling.

This tightens a few generalized rules that were still too fuzzy in practice. Hydrated current-bottle matches now have to agree on both bottle and release identity, release promotion preserves release-specific traits and only blocks when an actual conflicting child release exists, and retailer-only evidence no longer authoritatively validates release traits.

On the downstream side, same-bottle producer metadata disagreements now become corrections on the existing bottle instead of unnecessary new-bottle proposals, including brand and distillery repairs.

I considered teaching the prompt about specific bottle families, but that would only rescue individual examples. The concrete regressions are covered in evals and tests instead, including Glengoyne Legacy Series Chapter Two, while the rules remain generalized.

author: expertvagabond
body:
Closes #169.

## Problem

`PgTokenStore.rowToToken` materialized only 11 scalar/JSON columns from `sint_tokens`, silently dropping every optional field added to `SintCapabilityToken` after the initial 002 schema:

- \`modelConstraints\`
- \`attestationRequirements\`
- \`verifiableComputeRequirements\`
- \`executionEnvelope\`
- \`behavioralConstraints\`
- \`passportId\`
- \`delegationDepth\`
- \`revocationEndpoint\`

After a \`store → get\` roundtrip, the reconstructed token no longer matched the canonical signing payload, so Ed25519 verification against the persisted copy would fail — exactly the class of bug #166 / PR #168 fixed at the canonicalization layer, now reappearing at the persistence boundary.

## Fix

Persist the full canonical token as a single \`payload\` JSONB column and keep a small set of denormalized scalars (\`token_id\`, \`subject\`, \`issuer\`, \`resource\`, \`expires_at\`) for indexed lookup only. New optional fields on \`SintCapabilityToken\` now roundtrip without any schema churn.

## Changes

- **\`migrations/003_tokens_payload.sql\`** — forward migration: add \`payload\`, backfill from legacy columns with \`jsonb_build_object\`, drop legacy columns, add issuer/resource indexes.
- **\`src/pg-schema.ts\`** — \`ensurePgSchema\` emits the new layout on fresh installs and self-heals 002-era databases in place (same steps as the migration, wrapped in a guard).
- **\`src/pg-token-store.ts\`** — \`store\`/\`get\`/\`getBySubject\` read and write the \`payload\` column exclusively.
- **\`__tests__/pg-stores.test.ts\`** — replaces hand-loaded migration SQL with \`ensurePgSchema\`, plus two regression tests:
  - roundtrips every optional field populated at once (the #169 repro)
  - roundtrips a fully populated nested \`constraints\` shape

## Test plan
- [x] \`pnpm --filter @pshkv/persistence build\` — clean
- [x] \`pnpm --filter @pshkv/persistence test\` — 27 passed, 29 skipped (PG/Redis require \`DATABASE_URL\`/\`REDIS_URL\`)
- [ ] Maintainer-side: run PG suite against a live database to exercise migration 003 and the regression tests

author: mr3project
body:
### Motivation
- Simplify and correct handling of payload offsets by removing implicit normalization and making offset management explicit. 
- Prevent array size overflow and improve capacity resizing semantics to preserve data and reset offset when necessary. 
- Modernize some utilities (hex string conversion) and ensure safe zero-length array handling.

### Description
- Removed the private `normalize()` method and all implicit normalization calls so the backing array may have a non-zero `offset`, and added `getBytesRaw()` and `getOffset()` accessors for raw access. 
- Reworked constructors and `set`/`setSize`/`setCapacity`/`expandIfNecessary` to correctly initialize and preserve `offset` and `size`, always reset `offset` to zero when data is copied into a new backing array, and prevent expanding when `offset != 0`. 
- Introduced `MAX_ARRAY_SIZE` to avoid integer overflow when growing arrays and replaced `EMPTY_BYTES` initialization with an explicit zero-length array. 
- Ensured `readFields` resets `offset` to zero, kept `setDirect` behavior for zero-copy references, and moved `hashCode()` below `equals()` (no functional change). 
- Replaced manual hex-building `toString()` with an `IntStream`-based implementation that formats bytes as two-digit hex pairs separated by spaces. 

### Testing
- Ran the project's unit test suite (`mvn test` for the module containing `tez-common`) and related Hadoop IO unit tests, and they completed successfully.

author: geoffjay
body:
Implements automated release infrastructure triggered by `v*` git tags.

**What's added:**

- **`.github/workflows/release.yml`** - GitHub Actions workflow that triggers on `v*` tag pushes, builds release binaries in a matrix for macOS arm64 (`aarch64-apple-darwin`), macOS x86_64 (`x86_64-apple-darwin`), and Linux x86_64 (`x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`), generates release notes via git-cliff, and creates a GitHub Release with all binaries attached as assets
- **`cliff.toml`** - git-cliff configuration mapping conventional commit types (`feat`, `fix`, `refactor`, `perf`, `docs`, `chore(deps)`) to changelog sections; includes GitHub PR link enrichment
- **`crates/xtask/src/main.rs`** - New `cargo xtask release [--dry-run]` subcommand that verifies a clean working tree, reads the workspace version from `Cargo.toml`, updates `CHANGELOG.md` via git-cliff (if installed), commits the changelog, and creates an annotated git tag; `--dry-run` previews all steps without making changes

**Release workflow:**
```bash
# After bumping version in Cargo.toml and committing:
cargo xtask release        # creates tag v0.3.0
git push origin v0.3.0    # triggers CI → builds + GitHub Release
```

Closes #137

body:
## Summary
- replace the bogus `DAT_8021d1a8` FILE declaration in `RedGlobals.h` with an alias to `__files[1]`
- keep existing RedSound call sites using `&DAT_8021d1a8` working, but route them to the real MSL stdout object
- restore clean linkage for freshly rebuilt RedSound objects, especially `RedStream.o`

## Evidence
- Before this change, rebuilding `src/RedSound/RedStream.cpp` caused the link to fail with `undefined: 'DAT_8021d1a8'`, referenced from `StreamPlay(int, void*, int, int, int)` in `RedStream.o`
- After this change, `ninja` rebuilds the affected RedSound sources and links `build/GCCP01/main.elf`; the build now stops at the expected final SHA1 mismatch check instead of a linker error
- After the fresh rebuild, `build/tools/objdiff-cli diff -p . -u main/RedSound/RedStream -o - StreamPause__Fii` reports `.text` 100.0% and `StreamPause__Fii` 100.0% for the rebuilt `RedStream.o`
- After the fresh rebuild, `build/tools/objdiff-cli diff -p . -u main/RedSound/RedStream -o - _SearchEmptyStreamData__Fv` reports `_SearchEmptyStreamData__Fv` 100.0%

## Why this is plausible source
- `DAT_8021d1a8` is being used everywhere as `&DAT_8021d1a8` for `fflush`, which matches `__files[1]` rather than an independent FILE object
- expressing it as an alias keeps the original call pattern intact while binding it to the actual MSL runtime symbol the linker provides

author: mithr4ndir
body:
## Summary

Closes the visibility gap surfaced by the 2026-04-18 incident where 1Password's daily account-wide cap (1000 reqs/24h on the Families tier) silently exhausted and we only discovered it post hoc via the undocumented \`op service-account ratelimit\` command.

This PR adds an Ansible role \`op_quota_collector\` that runs on command-center1 every 15 minutes, calls the ratelimit command, parses the table output, and writes Prometheus textfile metrics that the existing node_exporter scrapes. The alerts, Grafana panel, and runbook are tracked separately in k8s-argocd (\`.spec-workflow/specs/1password-quota-monitoring/\`).

## What's included

### Role \`roles/op_quota_collector/\`

| Path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| \`files/parse.py\` | Python 3 stdlib parser, CLI table to Prometheus textfile. 5 passing unit tests under \`tests/\` |
| \`templates/op-quota-collector.sh.j2\` | Shell orchestrator: kill-switch check, op call, parse, atomic write, tagged syslog |
| \`templates/op-quota-collector.service.j2\` | systemd oneshot, runs as ladino |
| \`templates/op-quota-collector.timer.j2\` | \`OnCalendar=*:0/15\`, Persistent=true |
| \`tasks/main.yml\` | Idempotent deploy + prime run so metrics exist on first scrape |
| \`handlers/main.yml\` | reload-systemd, restart-op-quota-collector |
| \`defaults/main.yml\` | paths, cadence, user, token location |

### Parser behavior

- Handles \`N/A\` resets (omits the metric line)
- Parses \`"X hours from now"\`, \`"X minutes from now"\`, \`"X hours and Y minutes from now"\` correctly
- Exits 2 with stderr on malformed input so shell catches and writes \`success=0\`
- Python stdlib only (no pip deps)

### Kill switch integration

- Sources the shared \`scripts/lib/op-killswitch.sh\`
- Checks at top, skips op call if active
- Scans op stderr on failure, trips the switch if "Too many requests" seen
- Zero risk of retry storms since the collector always exits 0

body:
**Stacks on #25.** Base is \`geozarr\` (not \`main\`); review #25 first.

## Summary

Groundwork for the upcoming multi-dataset picker UI (layer 3+ of this stack). No behaviour change for anyone not opting in.

- **`bowser.catalog`** — new module. `CatalogEntry` dataclass + `load_catalog` / `save_catalog` for TOML files. Schema is minimal and STAC-adjacent (`id`, `name`, `uri`, `bbox`, `description`).
  - `uri` accepts any fsspec-compatible target — `s3://bucket/path.zarr`, `/abs/path/cube.zarr`, `file://…`, `http(s)://…` — so local and cloud datasets use the same codepath.
  - `id` is the routing key the server will dispatch on in layer 3; constrained to `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*$` so it's URL-safe.
  - Left open: if/when STAC Collections get a standard view over GeoZarr pyramids, migrating is adding a compatibility loader here. Tracked in `TECH_DEBT.md`.
- **`bowser register`** CLI — appends an entry to a catalog TOML file; auto-sniffs the WGS84 bbox from the store if `--bbox` isn't passed (reprojects from the native CRS when needed).
- **`GET /catalog`** — reads `BOWSER_CATALOG_FILE` and returns `{datasets: [...]}`. Returns `{datasets: []}` when the catalog is absent, so callers treat "no catalog configured" as success-with-empty, not error.
- **`Settings`** gains `BOWSER_CATALOG_FILE: str = ""`.

## Verified

```bash
$ bowser register mexico-city --uri /tmp/cube.zarr --name "Mexico City subsidence" --catalog /tmp/test_catalog.toml
Inferred bbox from store: (-99.06276139881109, 19.330434383664112, -99.01725118871379, 19.373543548303225)
Wrote 1 entries to /tmp/test_catalog.toml

$ BOWSER_CATALOG_FILE=/tmp/test_catalog.toml bowser run --stack-file /tmp/cube.zarr &
$ curl http://localhost:8765/catalog
{"datasets":[{"id":"mexico-city","name":"Mexico City subsidence","uri":"/tmp/cube.zarr","bbox":[-99.0627614,19.33043438,-99.01725119,19.37354355],"description":""}]}
```

Auto-bbox reprojected from EPSG:32614 to WGS84 correctly (matches the original GeoTIFF `latlon_bounds`).

## Next in the stack

1. [#25] GeoZarr conventions + converter + pyramid + state — this is the base.
2. **This PR** — catalog + register + endpoint.
3. [next] Dockerfile + EC2 bootstrap so we can run bowser against an S3 catalog.
4. [after] `DatasetRegistry` + per-request dataset routing for multi-user serving.
5. [finally] Picker frontend.

## What changed

Every answer reveal now shows how long you took + how that compares to your topic median (or your global median when the topic has <3 samples). Instant feedback for exam-condition pacing without adding friction.

```

⏱ 44s · topic median 45s · about topic median              your avg 38s

## Overview

This PR adds comprehensive support for Koden MDS-series RADARpc radars, enabling UDP-based discovery, control commands, and spoke reception at native resolutions (240/480/960 pixels).

## Feature & build integration

- Adds a new Cargo feature flag `koden` and includes it in the default feature set.
- Introduces `Brand::Koden` with string parsing, serialization, display formatting, and the "kod" prefix.
- Registers Koden in the recording subsystem with brand ID 7.

## New modules & protocol

- Adds a Koden implementation under src/lib/brand/koden with modules:
  - protocol.rs — wire-level protocol constants, framing markers, timing, model/range tables, and helpers for angle/range conversions.
  - mod.rs — UDP locator that recognizes Koden control/status and image-frame packets, registers radars, and spawns a report-receiver subsystem.
  - report.rs — KodenReportReceiver that manages UDP I/O, startup/keepalive logic, decodes status packets into shared controls, and decodes image packets into spoke frames.
  - command.rs — Command sender that formats and transmits Koden control commands over UDP.
  - settings.rs — Builds SharedControls for Koden-specific controls and enumerations.

## Discovery, reception & decoding

- Performs UDP discovery/identification via control/status prefixes and an image-frame marker on port 10001 (broadcast).
- Runs a receive loop with restart-on-error behavior, optional startup/keepalive sending, and control-subscription handling.
- Decodes image frames to extract transfer type, range, spoke counts, sample counts, start angle, and per-spoke bearings; converts Koden wire angles (0–1023) to radians; scales pixel intensities and publishes spokes at native sample counts without stretching.
- Optionally derives heading from nav data and includes it in spoke metadata.

## Models & capabilities

- Detects 11 known models via model-code mapping (MDS-50R through MDS-10R) and exposes model, serial, and related metadata.
- Supports controls with proper wire encodings and auto/manual handling:
  - Power (transmit/standby via transfer mode), Gain (with auto), Sea clutter (STC), Rain (FTC)
  - Sea state (manual/auto/harbor), Interference rejection, Target expansion, Scan speed
  - Display timing (trigger delay), Tune (coarse with auto), TuneFine (fine tuning), Pulse width
  - No-transmit blanking sectors and Park position (angle controls)
- Encodes multi-byte angle/sector and park position via 16-bit word packets with appropriate scaling.

## State reporting & controls mapping

- Parses status/control responses to update shared controls: gain/STC/FTC and auto modes, transmission/warmup state, scan/antenna parameters, MAC/model/serial, tuning/presets, and park/blanking sectors.
- Implements CommandSender to translate ControlValue → Koden wire commands and send startup/keepalive packets.

## Documentation & configuration

- Adds docs/koden-setup.md describing network requirements (UDP broadcast on port 10001, same-subnet), supported models, controls, and troubleshooting steps.
- Updates README and internal docs to list Koden as implemented (awaiting live-hardware validation).

## Tests & status

- cargo check passes (compiles clean).
- Live hardware verification remains pending (to be tested with Koden MDS-series units such as MDS-5R or MDS-11R).

## Notable implementation details

- Publishes spokes at native resolutions (240/480/960) without stretching.
- Re-enables TuneFine control and maps it to command destination.
- Encodes blanking sectors and park position using radians → word encoding and includes angle normalization helpers.

body:
The `Commercial Balloon Prospects` path could abort with `TargetClosedError` during long ASP.NET sessions, causing zero-output runs. The failure mode was amplified by unguarded page scroll evaluation and no recovery when the page/context died mid year-scan.

- **Sarasota balloon session recovery**
  - Added `_get_fresh_page(...)` to close stale context and reopen a page (with browser restart fallback).
  - Updated both balloon workflows to catch target-closed failures around yearly search/parse, reopen, retry once for that year, and continue scanning on retry failure:
    - `_fetch_maturing_commercial_debt`
    - `_fetch_sarasota_personal_commercial_balloon_clients`

- **Best-effort scrolling (non-fatal)**
  - Wrapped `BaseScraper.random_scroll` in exception handling so transient page closures during `page.evaluate(...)` do not terminate the run.

- **`networkidle` alignment**
  - Kept Sarasota on `load` + visible-results-table wait (no `networkidle`).
  - Verified no `wait_for_load_state("networkidle")` usage remains in Broward or Miami-Dade scrapers.

- **Focused regression coverage**
  - Added tests for:
    - `random_scroll` swallowing evaluate/target-closed failures.
    - Balloon workflows reopening/retrying when a target-closed error occurs mid-loop.

```python
try:
    self._search_official_records(page, "MORTGAGE", f"01/01/{year}", f"12/31/{year}")
    rows = self._parse_results(page)
except Exception as exc:
    if self._is_target_closed_error(exc):
        page = self._get_fresh_page(page)
        self._search_official_records(page, "MORTGAGE", f"01/01/{year}", f"12/31/{year}")
        rows = self._parse_results(page)

```

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>


## Bug: Balloon Prospects scraper crashes with `TargetClosedError` — fix long-running browser session

### Background
The `Commercial Balloon Prospects` scraper (`_fetch_maturing_commercial_debt` and `_fetch_sarasota_personal_commercial_balloon_clients`) crashes immediately with:
```
TargetClosedError('Page.evaluate: Target page, context or browser has been closed')
```

This happens because:
1. `random_scroll()` calls `page.evaluate()` with **no try/except** — when the ASP.NET clerk portal redirects or reloads mid-session, the page context closes and the entire scraper dies with 0 records
2. `wait_for_load_state("networkidle")` in `_search_official_records` hangs forever on the ASP.NET site (it never reaches networkidle due to continuous background polling)
3. The balloon scrapers keep a single browser page open for 10–30 minutes across 7 full-year searches + up to 600 PDF downloads — far too long without page refresh/recovery logic

### Fixes Required in `scrapers/sarasota_scraper.py`

#### Fix 1: Wrap `random_scroll` in try/except
In `BaseScraper.random_scroll` (in `scrapers/base_scraper.py`):
```python
@staticmethod
def random_scroll(page) -> None:
    """Scroll the page by a random amount to simulate reading."""
    try:
        scroll_y = random.randint(300, 900)
        page.evaluate(f"window.scrollBy(0, {scroll_y})")
        time.sleep(random.uniform(0.3, 1.2))
    except Exception:
        pass  # Page may have navigated or closed; scroll is best-effort only
```

#### Fix 2: Replace `networkidle` with `load` + table wait in `_search_official_records`
```python
try:
    page.click("#ctl00_cphBody_bSearch_input")
    try:
        page.wait_for_load_state("load", timeout=15_000)
    except Exception:
        pass
    try:
        page.wait_for_selector(
            "#ctl00_cphBody_rgCaseList table, table",
            timeout=10_000,
            state="visible",
        )
    except Exception:
        pass
    self.sleep()
except Exception as exc:
    logger.warning("Sarasota: form submit failed: %s", repr(exc))
```

#### Fix 3: Add page recovery logic to `_fetch_maturing_commercial_debt` and `_fetch_sarasota_personal_commercial_balloon_clients`

Both of these methods open a single `page` and loop through 7 years of mortgage records. If the page closes mid-loop, they crash. Add a helper method `_ensure_page` that reopens the page context if it has been closed:

```python
def _get_fresh_page(self):
    """Open a new page context, closing any stale one first."""
    try:
        context = self._browser.new_context(...)
        page = context.new_page()
        page.set_default_timeout(self.timeout_ms)
        return page
    except Exception:
        self.start_browser()
        return self.new_page()
```

In the year-loop inside both `_fetch_maturing_commercial_debt` and `_fetch_sarasota_personal_commercial_balloon_clients`, wrap the `_search_official_records` call and page usage in a try/except that catches `TargetClosedError` and reopens the page:

```python
for year in self.MATURING_SEARCH_YEARS:
    if len(records) >= max_results or scanned >= scan_limit:
        break
    try:
        self._search_official_records(page, "MORTGAGE", f"01/01/{year}", f"12/31/{year}")
        rows = self._parse_results(page)
    except Exception as exc:
        if self._is_target_closed_error(exc):
            logger.warning("Sarasota balloon: page closed mid-search for year %d, reopening", year)
            try:
                page.context.close()
            except Exception:
                pass
            page = self.new_page()
            try:
                self._search_official_records(page, "MORTGAGE", f"01/01/{year}", f"12/31/{year}")
                rows = self._parse_results(page)
            except Exception as retry_exc:
                logger.warning("Sarasota balloon: retry failed for year %d: %s", year, repr(retry_exc))
                continue
        else:
            raise
    # ... rest of the row processing loop
```

#### Fix 4: Apply the same `networkidle` fix to `broward_scraper.py` and `miami_dade_scraper.py`
Search both files for `wait_for_load_state("networkidle")` and replace with the same `load` + table-selector pattern.

### Expected Result
- Balloon scraper no longer crashes immediately on `random_scroll`
- Balloon scraper recovers gracefully if ASP.NET closes the page mid-session
- Balloon scraper actually scans PDFs and returns qualified leads
- Cash-out refi scraper is completely untouched

author: andreashasse
body:
Stacked on #162 — review that first.

## Bugs found & fixed

Adding property tests surfaced several real bugs in the library and test infrastructure. Each fix is in its own commit.

- **`spectra_binary_string` decoded strings as latin1 while encoding as UTF-8.** A UTF-8 binary encoded fine but couldn't round-trip through the decoder. Switched decode to `unicode:characters_to_list/2` and threaded the decode failure (`invalid_utf8` / `incomplete_utf8` + decoded/rest) into the `sp_error` ctx.

- **`spectra_string` treated `binary()` as latin1 in both directions.** Roundtrip "worked" at the byte level but `<<"é"/utf8>>` became `[195, 169]` (garbage) instead of `[233]` (the codepoint). Switched to `unicode:characters_to_list/2` and `unicode:characters_to_binary/2`, with structured error ctx on invalid input. Behaviour change for callers passing non-UTF-8 binaries — they now get an error instead of a latin1 byte list.

- **`spectra_json_schema` emitted `oneOf` for unions.** `oneOf` requires *exactly one* subschema to validate, which JSON-Schema validators (jesse, etc.) reject for overlapping union members like two integer ranges sharing a value or `integer() | integer_range`. Switched to `anyOf`, which is the correct encoding of Erlang union semantics.

- **Removed `check_unicode` config option.** The encoder now always validates Unicode for `string()`/`nonempty_string()` inputs. With the new structured `sp_error` ctx (`invalid_unicode` / `incomplete_unicode` + decoded/rest), there is no longer a performance case for an opt-in path. Callers that previously passed invalid iolists will now get `{error, …}` instead of a silently-corrupt charlist.

- **Test generator: `#sp_rec{}` data generator dropped fields.** The clause pattern-matched `{_Name, Type}` against the field record, silently producing empty records. Fixed to read `F#sp_rec_field.type`.

- **Test generator: `sp_literal` generator produced `binary_value = undefined`.** Caused spurious "undefined" output from the encoder. Added `literal_binary_value/1`.

- **Test generator: `sp_rec` / `sp_map` produced duplicate field names.** The atom pool is small (5 values), so `vector(Len, ...)` frequently generated structurally invalid records/maps with two entries for the same key. Added post-generation dedup.

## New property tests

- `prop_json_roundtrip_from_data` — generated type + data, encode → decode, assert `Data =:= Data2`, plus re-encode Data2 and assert byte-identical JSON (encoder idempotence).
- `prop_binary_string_roundtrip` — same pattern for `binary_string`.
- `prop_string_roundtrip` — same pattern for `string`.
- `prop_json_schema_validates_encoded` — encoded JSON validates against the generated schema via jesse.

Each test reuses existing generators and a shared filter (`test/sp_type_filters.erl`) that captures the currently-roundtrip-safe type subset.

## Known limitation (left as filter, not a bug)

`binary_string` / `string` decode picks the first matching union member. `string() | integer()` can't roundtrip because `0` encodes to `"0"` and decodes back as `"0"`. Treated as a design limitation of untagged wire formats — these codecs only support literal-only unions (enums). Codified in `binary_string_roundtrip_safe/1`.

## Test plan
- [ ] `make format && make build-test` clean
- [ ] `make proper` — 9/9 properties pass stably
- [ ] New UTF-8 tests in `spectra_binary_string_test` and `spectra_string_test` pass
