author: smallorbit
body:
## Summary

Adds a project-local `PreToolUse` hook on the `Skill` tool that fires before `flowkit:cut` or `flowkit:ship`. It checks every `plugins/*/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` for commits since its last per-plugin tag that landed without a version bump. If any plugin has drift, the hook blocks the skill with a clear message telling Claude to run `/bump-versions` first.

## Why

Three flowkit fix PRs (#234, #237, #240) shipped to `main` between `flowkit--v1.2.4` and the `v2026.4.18.3` release tag without anyone running `/bump-versions`, leaving clients stuck on 1.2.4 while newer code was on main. Caught and fixed in a follow-up (flowkit 1.2.5), but the manual-sync step was the root cause.

Per `CLAUDE.md`, `/bump-versions` is expected before every release but isn't invoked by `/cut`, `/release`, or `/ship`. Rather than building it into flowkit itself (flowkit is used in non-plugin repos), this hook is scoped to *this* repo via `.claude/settings.json`.

## Files

- `.claude/settings.json` (new, checked in) — wires the hook
- `.claude/hooks/check-plugin-bumps.sh` (new) — detection script; reads skill invocation from stdin, filters to flowkit:cut/ship, walks each plugin manifest, emits a `permissionDecision: "deny"` with reason if drift is detected
- `.gitignore` — adds `.claude/settings.local.json`

## Test plan

- [x] Raw pipe test: non-matching skill exits silent
- [x] Raw pipe test: matching skill with no drift exits silent
- [x] Raw pipe test: simulated drift (flowkit tag rolled back + version reset) produces correct deny JSON
- [ ] Live test: confirmed fires on next `/flowkit:cut` attempt (may need `/hooks` reload first — watcher caveat)

author: joecotellese
body:
## Summary

Adds a new `bookery vault-export` CLI command that converts an Obsidian vault (or a subset of folders) into a single EPUB with a clickable TOC, resolved `[[wiki-links]]`, embedded images, and an optional tag-based index. Motivating use case: reading a browsable PKM vault on a Kobo e-reader.

Key design points from the spec (issue #72):

- **Pandoc-backed EPUB generation** (no new Python deps). Fails fast with a clear error if pandoc is missing.
- **Stable `dc:identifier` via `uuid5`** derived from the vault's absolute path, so re-exports update the book in place on Kobo (preserving reading position, bookmarks, annotations). `--uuid random` is available as an escape hatch.
- **Two-pass link resolution**: walker collects a `{title → slug}` map across the entire vault, then per-note resolution rewrites `[[Target]]` / `[[Target|alias]]` into intra-document anchors. Broken links render as italic plain text and are counted.
- **Image resolution** for both Obsidian `![[asset.png]]` and standard `![alt](path)` syntax. Vault-wide flat asset index matches Obsidian's own lookup behavior.
- **Optional tag index** (`--index`): alphabetized H2 per tag with bulleted links, configurable prefix exclusion and min-count filter.
- **Config defaults** via a new `[vault_export]` section in `~/.bookery/config.toml`.
- **Dual-layer progress UI** (Rich Live+Group) matching the pattern established by `bookery sync`: overall bar + per-item spinner for walk + assemble phases, then a pandoc spinner.

## Changes

- **`src/bookery/core/vault/`** (new package): `note`, `frontmatter`, `walker`, `wikilink`, `image`, `index`, `assemble`, `epub`.
- **`src/bookery/cli/commands/vault_export_cmd.py`**: Click command wiring flags + config + pipeline + progress display.
- **`src/bookery/cli/__init__.py`**: register the new command.
- **`src/bookery/core/config.py`**: add `VaultExportConfig` dataclass and `[vault_export]` TOML parser.
- **`docs/config.example.toml` + `README.md`**: documentation for the new command and config section.
- **`tests/`**: full unit / integration / e2e coverage plus a fixture vault with cross-links, broken links, an embedded PNG, and multi-tag notes. E2E tests skip cleanly when pandoc isn't installed.

## Testing

- [x] 1065 tests passing (`uv run pytest`)
- [x] `uv run ruff check src/ tests/` clean
- [x] TDD: every task committed tests + implementation together (see 14-commit history)
- [x] Smoke-tested on the fixture vault and on a real 712-note Obsidian vault
- [x] Verified `dc:identifier` is stable across re-exports (Kobo in-place update works)

## Related Issues

Fixes #72

author: wiserval
body:
### Overview
In this lab, I implemented several classification models to predict penguin species based on physical measurements. Key highlights include:
* **Baseline Development**: Established a strong performance baseline using Logistic Regression, achieving over 98% accuracy.
* **Model Comparison**: Evaluated and compared Gaussian Naive Bayes, Support Vector Machines (Linear and RBF), Decision Trees, and Random Forests.
* **Visualization**: Utilized Confusion Matrices and ROC/AUC curves to diagnose specific misclassifications, particularly between the Adelie and Chinstrap species.
* **Optimization**: Performed hyperparameter tuning on the top-performing Random Forest model using GridSearchCV, ensuring high robustness across cross-validation folds.

### Key Findings
* The **Random Forest** model emerged as the most effective classifier, consistently reaching perfect or near-perfect scores.
* **Gaussian Naive Bayes** struggled significantly compared to other models, likely due to the high correlation between physical features like body mass and flipper length.
* **Species Identification**: While Gentoo penguins are easily distinguished by the models, Adelie and Chinstrap penguins show physical similarities that lead to occasional misclassifications in simpler models.

---

### Definition of Done Checklist

- [x] Penguins dataset is loaded, explored, and split with stratification.
- [x] Categorical features are encoded and the target is label-encoded.
- [x] Logistic regression baseline is trained and evaluated with four metrics.
- [x] Five additional classifiers are trained and compared in a summary table.
- [x] Confusion matrices are plotted for all models.
- [x] ROC curves are plotted with AUC values.
- [x] GridSearchCV is used to tune the best model with at least 3 hyperparameters.
- [x] Markdown cells explain reasoning, especially around species confusion and metric trade-offs.
- [x] The notebook runs top-to-bottom without errors (`Kernel → Restart & Run All`).

## Summary

Two related bugs surface when a user re-opens an existing Linear/Trello/JIRA PM integration to tweak settings:

1. **"Failed to create label: Missing credentials or team selection"** — clicking "Create label" in the Labels mapping step throws a client-side error even though the integration is fully configured.
2. **No "Verify Connection" button on the credentials step** — the button was hidden entirely in edit-mode with stored credentials and no re-typed API key.

Root cause: `buildEditState` intentionally leaves raw API credentials blank when re-opening an integration (security — `hasStoredCredentials` is flipped true instead). The discovery hooks (`useTrelloBoards`, `useLinearStates`, etc.) already had an edit-mode fallback: when stored creds exist and the API-key field is empty, pass `projectId` and let the backend resolve credentials via `resolvePMCredentials`. But the mutation hooks (`useVerification`, `useTrelloLabelCreation`, `useLinearLabelCreation`, `useTrelloCustomFieldCreation`, `useJiraCustomFieldCreation`) required form-state credentials and threw synchronously.

This PR plumbs the same `projectId` fallback into every mutation hook. Zero backend change — `pm.discovery.createLabel`, `createCustomField`, and `discover` all already accept an optional `projectId`.

## What changed

- **New `shouldUseStoredCredentials(state)`** helper in `pm-wizard-state.ts`. Single source of truth: "is this a stored-creds-path mutation". 8 unit tests.
- **5 mutation hooks** in `pm-wizard-hooks.ts` updated to consult the helper and branch between `{ projectId }` and `{ credentials: ... }`. Team / board / project-key checks stay (those come from config state, not creds).
- **`pm-wizard.tsx`**: drop the visibility gate on the Verify Connection button. Always render on the credentials step. Enable when `credsReady || (editing && stored)`. Show a muted "Using stored credentials" hint when taking the stored-creds path.
- **Refactored** the two `createMissingLabelsMutation` bodies to extract a `runPerLabelCreations` helper (keeps them under the biome cognitive-complexity threshold).

## Test plan

- [x] `npm test` — 8210 / 8210 (8 new tests in `pm-wizard-state.test.ts`, the rest unchanged)
- [x] `npm run lint` — clean
- [x] `npm run typecheck` — clean
- [x] `cd web && npm run build` — clean
- [ ] **Post-merge browser smoke** — re-open an existing Linear/Trello/JIRA integration:
  - [ ] Credentials step shows a **Verify Connection** button with "Using stored credentials" hint; clicking verifies without re-typing the key
  - [ ] Labels step **Create label** succeeds in edit mode
  - [ ] Custom-field creation (Trello/JIRA) succeeds in edit mode
  - [ ] Fresh-setup flow still requires typed credentials (no regression)

author: janicduplessis
body: ## Summary The "Invite your friends" pane in the onboarding splash sequence had a layout bug where the search bar's bottom border visually overlapped the first contact item. This PR fixes the SearchBar wrapper sizing so the input renders cleanly above the contact list. Resolves [TLON-5566](https://linear.app/tlon/issue/TLON-5566/expo-54-layout-collision-on-contacts-search-screen-in-onboarding). ## Changes - Drop `height="$4xl"` (48px) from the `SearchBar`. The underlying `TextInput` has a hard-coded height of 56px; with the wrapper's `alignItems: "center"`, the input was overflowing its wrapper by 4px on top and bottom, which is what caused the border to bleed into the first list row. - Add `flexGrow={0}` to the `SearchBar`. Its internal `YStack` defaults to `flexGrow: 1`, so without this override the search bar was stretching vertically inside the parent column, pushing the list content down inconsistently. - Remove the redundant `XStack` wrapper and set `paddingHorizontal="$xl"` directly on `SearchBar`. ## How did I test? Tested on iOS simulator. Before: the first contact row's avatar/name were clipped a few pixels behind the search bar, and the search bar's bottom border appeared to be overlapped by the first list item. After: the search bar renders cleanly and items below it are unobstructed. Verified the empty-contacts and loading states still render correctly. ## Risks and impact - Safe to rollback without consulting PR author? Yes - Affects important code area: - [x] Onboarding - [ ] State / providers - [ ] Message sync - [ ] Channel display - [ ] Notifications - [ ] Other: ## Rollback plan Revert this commit. The change is scoped to a single file (`packages/app/ui/components/Wayfinding/SplashSequence.tsx`) and only affects the onboarding "Invite your friends" pane. ## Screenshots / videos

author: gmcoringa
body:
# Argon One V5 Support

The goal of this task was to add support for the Argon One V5 case to the Home Assistant OS Add-on repository. Unlike previous versions (V2/V3), the V5 fan connects directly to the Raspberry Pi 5's dedicated PWM fan header, meaning fan management is handled natively by the OS kernel, not by an external I2C microcontroller.

## Summary of Changes

### Observer Mode
*   The add-on no longer attempts to override the Linux kernel's thermal governor via I2C or sysfs, preventing read-only filesystem errors and erratic fan behavior.
*   *`run.sh` reliably detects the `pwm-fan` kernel device with a 15-attempt polling loop (retrying every 2 seconds).
*   The script safely reads `cur_state` and `max_state`, actively guards against empty/invalid reads (preventing division-by-zero crashes), and reports the actual fan speed to Home Assistant every 30 seconds.
*   The bash script now correctly traps only on `ERR` without noisy clean-exit interference.

### Documentation
*   Fully updated to clarify the add-on's new role as an "Observer." They guide users to edit `/boot/firmware/config.txt` to actually change the physical fan curve. The support section has been rewritten to be professional and constructive.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Added "Argon One V5 Active Linear Cooling" Home Assistant add-on: reports CPU temperature and kernel-driven fan speed (observer mode), with configurable temperature units, optional Home Assistant fan entity, and periodic logging every 30 seconds.

* **Documentation**
  * Added README, user docs, and a changelog with usage, configuration, fan-curve guidance, troubleshooting, and support links.

* **Chores**
  * Added packaging and runtime configuration for the new add-on (container profile and build metadata).

author: zuevrs
body:
## Summary

Three prose-only tightenings from the post-Wave-G references audit — all backed by **T1 obra** or **T2 gstack**, zero new CLI surface, zero violation of the Wave A-G minimalism ratchet.

### Gap 2 — Skill-before-response gate (`obra T1`)
`src/content/meta-skill.ts` gains a `## Skill-before-response gate` section. Rule: if `flow-state.json` has a `currentStage`, the model must load the matching stage SKILL before **substantive** work (artifact edits, code, Decision Protocol questions, gate claims, subagent dispatch). Explicit substantive / non-substantive split protects clarifying one-liners.

### Gap 1 — Decision Protocol skeleton + Completeness calibration (`gstack T2`)
`src/content/protocols.ts::decisionProtocolMarkdown` grows two new sections:

- **Decision skeleton** — every Decision Protocol call must include **Re-ground** (project + feature slug + stage from `flow-state.json`), **Simplify** (plain-English 16-year-old test), `RECOMMENDATION: Choose [Letter] because ...`, and lettered **Options** with per-option `Completeness: X/10` plus optional effort estimate.
- **Completeness calibration** — 1-10 rubric (10 complete, 7 happy-path, 5 partial, 3 shortcut, 1 TBD). Options at `≤5` must be explicitly acknowledged; "static for now" always scores `≤3`.

Explicit anti-port: gstack's question-registry, auto-decide telemetry, per-skill preambles and per-question JSONL analytics are **not** introduced — cclaw stays installer-first and in-harness.

### Gap 4 — Chunked spec sign-off (`obra T1`)
`src/content/stages/spec.ts` interaction protocol + process both require delivering acceptance criteria to the user in **batches of 3-5** and pausing for explicit ACK (via the new Decision Protocol skeleton) between batches. Full spec still lands in `04-spec.md`; only the sign-off conversation is chunked.

## Test plan

- [x] All 500 unit + integration + e2e tests pass locally (`pnpm test --run`).
- [x] Four new flow-contracts assertions (skill-gate, decision skeleton, completeness calibration, spec chunking).
- [x] No golden-snapshot drift (only spec stage modified; spec is not snapshot-tested).
- [x] `using-cclaw` stays under the 170-line size budget; stage skills stay under 350 lines.
- [x] `pnpm run build` clean (TypeScript).
- [ ] Wait for green CI (build Node 20/22 + coverage + release bundle + smoke + security audit + label gate).

## Release Notes Draft

- feat(meta-skill): require the active stage SKILL to be loaded before any substantive response when a flow is active (T1 obra parity).
- feat(decision-protocol): enforce Re-ground → Simplify → `RECOMMENDATION: Choose [Letter]` → lettered Options with `Completeness: X/10` calibration on every Decision Protocol call (T2 gstack parity, without telemetry/registry).
- feat(spec): deliver acceptance criteria to users in batches of 3-5 with explicit ACK between batches (T1 obra "chunks short enough to digest").

## Mechanical Root Cause

PR #1544 shipped with a changeset declaring `minor` on all three published packages. The changesets GitHub Action generated Version Packages PR #1547 proposing 1.14.11 → **1.15.0**. 1.15.0 is milestone-locked to Pack Distribution per ADR-075 / ADR-085, and Phase B still has roughly seven tickets to drain (#1482, #1483, #1486-#1490, #1492, #1493). Allowing the minor bump through would publish 1.15.0 as "ADR-088 Phase 1 substrate" and slide the Pack Distribution headline to 1.16.0.

## Fix Applied

Rewrote the changeset frontmatter from `minor` to `patch` on all three packages. Body unchanged. When this merges, the changesets Action regenerates PR #1547 as 1.14.11 → **1.14.12**, matching the rest of the Phase B grind which has been shipping as patches under 1.14.x.

- Closing #1547 directly. The bot updates it automatically when this merges.

author: nisimasacode
body:
**Reference issues and PRs**

Fixes #12151.

**What does this implement/fix? Explain your changes.**

This PR fixes Enable Banking transaction imports failing with 422 WRONG_REQUEST_PARAMETERS.

The importer was using the Enable Banking account identification_hash as the account identifier passed through the import pipeline and ultimately used for the transactions API call. The Enable Banking transactions endpoint expects the account uid (UUID). When the hash is used, the API rejects the request with an “Invalid value” for account_id.

**Changes:**

app/Services/Shared/Model/ImportServiceAccount.php
For EnableBankingAccount, use $account->getUid() as the ImportServiceAccount id (instead of getIdentificationHash()), both in convertSingleAccount() and convertEnableBankingArray().
app/Services/Shared/Conversion/CreatesAccounts.php
Update the Enable Banking matching branch to compare using $entry->getUid() so the account lookup remains consistent with the updated identifier.

**Result:**

Enable Banking transaction fetching works again.
Account matching/creation remains consistent using the same provider identifier.

**Tested on:**

Data Importer v2.2.3
Enable Banking (ING)

 Code generation (e.g., when writing an implementation or fixing a bug)

## About the PR

Follow-up cleanup on #465. Three small refactors, no behavior change.

## Why / Balance

Not a balance change. The reagent-scanner PR landed with some duplicated patient-header UI code and an organ lookup that iterated every stomach and lung in the world per scan tick. Easier to maintain and a bit cheaper on the hot path.

author: yangdongle668
body:
CSS scroll-snap-type: mandatory was causing two user-visible bugs:
  1. A slow wheel tick near the top of the hero didn't cross the snap threshold, so scroll rested between section 1 and section 2.
  2. Past tile 3, mandatory wouldn't release the scroll, trapping the user — sections 6+ (stats/tech/cases/blog/cta/footer) unreachable.

Replace it with home-snap.js: a wheel-event interceptor that programmatically scrolls to the next/previous of the five snap sections (hero + products + 3 application tiles) with a 900ms cooldown, and releases control once the user is past the last snap point so native scroll handles everything below.

CSS now just pins each of the five to height: 100svh so scrollIntoView lands cleanly. Disabled below 900 px and for prefers-reduced-motion.

author: ajy0127
body:
## Summary

Reference implementation of the **Reporting category** proposed in [RFC #38](https://github.com/GRCEngClub/claude-grc-engineering/issues/38), now bundled with the prerequisite data-contract work the reporting flows depend on.

Marked as **draft** while the RFC comment window is open (closes **May 2, 2026**), but the branch now has the underlying plumbing needed for an honest mergeable prototype.

## What this ships

### 1. Reporting plugin

**Plugin**: `plugins/grc-reporter/` — 4 commands, 5 skills, marketplace registration.

| Command | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `/report:exec-summary` | Weekly 1-page for the CISO and direct leadership |
| `/report:board-brief` | Quarterly audit-committee or board-ready narrative |
| `/report:program-health` | Portfolio view across every framework in scope |
| `/report:automation-coverage` | Week-over-week automation coverage + ROI |

**Skills**:
- `so-what-translation` — the core craft of turning findings into business impact
- `exec-narrative-patterns` — audience-specific tone (board vs audit committee vs CEO vs CISO weekly)
- `program-portfolio-composition` — cross-framework synthesis without overwhelming the reader
- `automation-coverage-analysis` — time saved, quality of evidence, forward-looking compounding value
- `context-bootstrap` — setup guidance when the toolkit is empty

### 2. Reporting prerequisites now included in-branch

This PR no longer assumes the reporting data model exists elsewhere.

It adds:
- `docs/GRC-DATA.md` for the user-owned `grc-data/` layout
- sibling schemas for `metric`, `risk`, `exception`, `vendor`, and `policy`
- committed fixtures for those schemas
- expanded contract validation in CI
- `/grc-engineer:record-automation-metrics` plus a batch config example for seeding automation-history snapshots

### 3. Reporter honesty fixes

The reporting docs/skills were tightened so they do not overclaim:
- `/report:automation-coverage` now requires explicit metric snapshots in `grc-data/metrics/`
- the command no longer pretends Findings alone can prove week-over-week manual -> automated movement
- `program-health` examples use framework aliases the toolkit actually resolves
- `board-brief` no longer points to the not-yet-shipped `/transform:markdown-to-executive`
- bootstrap/setup guidance now reflects the real minimums per report command

## UX pattern

Heavy auto-discover when the toolkit has context (findings cache, risk register, framework metadata, metrics). Heavy ask-and-guide when it doesn't — walks the user through install, first collection, and first metric snapshot rather than generating a hollow report. Hollow reports are worse than no reports.

## Framing

The user of these commands is the **GRC practitioner who needs to communicate up**. The CISO, board, or audit committee is the audience of the output, not the runner of the command. This sidesteps the open "is `grc-ciso` a manufactured persona?" question in Design Question 4 and plants the Reporting category at the same level as the other personas.

## Verification

- `npm run test:contract`
- `npx markdownlint-cli2 "plugins/grc-engineer/commands/record-automation-metrics.md" "plugins/grc-engineer/commands/monitor-continuous.md" "plugins/grc-reporter/**/*.md" "plugins/grc-internal/commands/track-compliance.md" "docs/GRC-DATA.md" "README.md"`
- `node plugins/grc-engineer/scripts/record-automation-metrics.js --config=plugins/grc-engineer/examples/automation-metrics.yaml --window-label=current-week --dry-run`

## Notes for reviewers

This is no longer a "new plugin only" diff. The extra schema/docs/test changes are intentional and are what make the reporting prototype grounded rather than aspirational.

The FedRAMP-derived metric path is intentionally labeled as a **tooling-capability baseline**. Manual snapshots remain the preferred **operator-observed** source for leadership reporting unless the automation has been validated as live in the target environment.

## Related

- RFC #38 — Architecture v2
- Migration-plan step 5 — reference implementations per new category
- Migration-plan step 3 — sibling schemas and user-owned state contracts

### Motivation
- Provide a dedicated printable layout and improved visual presentation for the `rendiciones` report to support printing and executive-style output.
- Fix a bug caused by reusing the same SQL parameter names for different UNIONed queries which could lead to ambiguous bindings for date filters.
- Prevent runtime errors from using `max(...array_map(...))` when the mapped array might be empty.
- Ensure module summary is consistently shown in the modules index header.

### Description
- Added a new print layout view at `app/views/layouts/print.php` that uses a minimal Bootstrap-based template for printing. 
- Modified `Controller` view calls for the rendiciones report to pass the `'print'` layout parameter when rendering printable output. 
- In `buildRendicionesDataset` renamed date parameter placeholders to unique names (`:from_date_pagos`, `:from_date_aportes`, `:from_date_egresos`, and corresponding `:to_*`) and added them to the query `params` to avoid collision across the `UNION ALL` queries. 
- Fixed potential `max()` invocation errors by building arrays first (`$maxTypeValues`, `$maxOriginValues`) and then using `max(1, ...$values)` in `app/views/rendiciones/report.php`. 
- Redesigned the `rendiciones` report view (`app/views/rendiciones/report.php`) with updated CSS, layout, improved KPI cards, charts, tables, print button and visual polish. 
- Added `report-card` styling and other UI tweaks as well as ensuring the modules index summary is always displayed by adjusting `app/views/modules/index.php`.

author: madmax983
body:
🦠 **Threat:**
The `mask_database_url` function parses database URLs using the `url` crate to securely redact passwords before logging. However, if an attacker or misconfiguration provides a malformed URL (e.g., one containing spaces or invalid characters) that still contains a password, `url::Url::parse` will fail. The previous implementation fell back to logging the unparsed, raw URL string, exposing the password in plaintext logs.

🛡️ **Defense:**
Updated the fallback logic in `mask_database_url`. If `url::Url::parse` fails, the function now safely redacts the entire URL string (`"****"`). This ensures a "fail-closed" mechanism, preventing any sensitive information from leaking into the logs when the parser encounters malformed input. Valid URLs without passwords remain unaffected and are logged naturally.

💥 **Severity:**
High. Exposure of database credentials in logs can lead to unauthorized database access, data breaches, and system compromise.

🧪 **Verification:**
Added the unit test `mask_database_url_invalid_url_fallback` in `autumn/src/app.rs` to verify that malformed URLs containing a password are fully redacted and do not expose the password. Verified that `cargo test`, `cargo clippy`, and `cargo fmt` pass successfully.

author: rossgroomio
body:
## Summary

Bench Boost was already handled correctly in `fpl review` (PR #27), but two other classic-path call sites still ignored `active_chip` when computing each player's `contributed` flag. That wrong flag flowed into three downstream consumers, all of which misreport during a BB gameweek.

This fix mirrors the PR #27 pattern.

## Problem

During BB, all 15 players score for real. Three bugs resulted from treating bench slots (positions 12-15) as non-contributing:

| Symptom | Site |
|---|---|
| `biggest_bench_haul` award fires for BB managers whose bench points actually counted, with a spurious "unused bench" player list | `_league_recap_data.py` award computation |
| `fpl league-recap` red-card fine silently suppressed for a benched player sent off during BB | `_fines.py:103` gate on `contributed` |
| `fpl status` red-card fine same suppression during a live BB GW | `status.py:_build_fines_context` |

Low frequency (BB is played at most twice per season per manager) but wrong enough to be worth closing the loop.

## Fix

- Extract `_classic_pick_flags()` helper returning `(is_bench, is_bench_boost_player, contributed)` with single source of truth for the chip check
- Add `is_bench_boost_player: bool` to `RecapManagerPlayer` TypedDict
- Skip `bench_points` accumulation when a bench slot is BB (those points counted)
- Exclude BB managers from `biggest_bench_haul` candidates (defensive — `bench_points` is already 0 for them post-fix)
- Extend `_build_fines_context` with optional `active_chip` parameter; classic call site passes `picks_data.get(\"active_chip\")`; draft call site keeps the default (`None`) because draft has no chips

## Scope boundaries

- Classic-only. Draft is a no-op everywhere (no chips in draft).
- No changes to `_fines.py`, no changes to the league-recap Jinja template (it does not iterate per-player squad rows).
- The todo (#019) also mentioned adding a `[BB]` marker to recap template rendering — unreachable, not shipped.

## Test plan

13 new tests, all targeting the BB code paths:

- `TestClassicPickFlags` (7) — helper covers non-BB starter/bench, BB starter/bench, auto-sub precedence, BB + auto-sub interaction, and negative cases for other chips (wildcard/freehit/3xc)
- `TestAwardsChips` (2 new) — BB manager excluded even if `bench_points` is non-zero; all-BB league produces no `biggest_bench_haul`
- `TestEvaluateLeagueFines` (2 new) — red-card fine triggers for BB-flagged bench slot; does not trigger on non-BB bench
- `TestBuildFinesContextActiveChip` (6) — `_build_fines_context` contributed flag behaviour + integration with `evaluate_fines` for all four chips and both starter/bench slots

Full test suite: 2381 passed. ruff clean. pyright 0 errors.

## Post-Deploy Monitoring & Validation

No runtime impact — CLI tool, local-only invocation. Validation window is the next BB gameweek for any user with `red-card` or `bench-haul`-referencing fines configured. Owner: @rossgroomio.

author: wtthornton
body:
## Summary

Closes [TAP-519](https://linear.app/tappscodingagents/issue/TAP-519).

`packages/tapps-core/pyproject.toml` pins `tapps-brain>=3.7.2,<4`, but nothing verified at runtime that the deployed brain actually satisfies the floor. A misconfigured deployment could silently run against an older brain and only surface the mismatch deep in a user's session. tapps-brain v3.8.0 ships an unauthenticated `GET /health` — this PR probes it at BrainBridge startup.

### What lands
- **`check_brain_version(brain_http_url)`** in `tapps_core.brain_bridge`: GETs `{url}/health`, parses `version`, compares against the pinned floor/ceiling via `packaging.version.Version`.
- **Factory wiring**: `create_brain_bridge` calls it after the existing DSN probe. Result is stashed on the bridge and exposed via a `BrainBridge.version_check` property so callers (e.g. `tapps_session_start`) can surface it.
- **New setting**: `MemorySettings.brain_http_url` (empty default, env `TAPPS_MCP_MEMORY_BRAIN_HTTP_URL`). Empty = skip probe (in-process `AgentBrain` deployments).

### Return shape
```python
{
  "ok": bool,
  "skipped": bool,        # True when brain_http_url is empty
  "degraded": bool,       # True on network/parse failure (non-fatal)
  "url": str,
  "floor": "3.7.2",
  "ceiling": "4.0.0",
  "version": str | None,  # reported by brain
  "errors": list[str],
  "warnings": list[str],
}
```

### Behaviour
- Empty URL (default) -> skipped, `ok=True`.
- Version below floor or >= ceiling -> `ok=False`, descriptive error logged via `structlog.error`; bridge still returned so unrelated memory ops work.
- Network / HTTP 5xx / bad JSON -> `ok=False`, `degraded=True`, warning logged; bridge returned.
- Missing `version` field / unparseable version -> `ok=False` with an error in the payload.

### Rebase note (TAP-523 / PR #101)
PR #101 (TAP-523) adds a `health_check()` method that validates DSN + pool config and surfaces results in `tapps_session_start` under a `brain_bridge_health` field. This PR is based on `master` since #101 isn't merged yet. Once #101 lands, the version-check payload should be folded into `health_check()` — the shape already matches (`ok`/`errors`/`warnings`/`details`), so it's a mechanical merge. The dedicated `version_check` property can either remain (small defensive accessor) or be collapsed into `health_check()`'s `details` block.

## Test plan

- [x] `packages/tapps-core/tests/unit/test_brain_version.py` — 17 new unit tests:
  - `test_skipped_when_url_empty`
  - `test_version_check_passes_when_floor_met` / `_at_exact_floor` / custom-bounds
  - `test_version_check_fails_when_below_floor` / `_at_or_above_ceiling`
  - `test_version_check_network_error_marks_degraded`
  - `test_version_check_http_error_marks_degraded`
  - `test_version_check_missing_version_field_errors`
  - `test_version_check_unparseable_version_errors`
  - `test_trailing_slash_stripped`
  - `TestFactoryWiring` — 4 tests covering skipped / ok / below-floor / network-error paths through `create_brain_bridge`
  - `TestVersionCheckProperty` — default sentinel + defensive-copy semantics
- [x] `uv run ruff check packages/tapps-core/src/` — clean
- [x] `uv run mypy --strict packages/tapps-core/src/tapps_core/` — clean (94 files)
- [x] `uv run pytest packages/tapps-core/tests/ -k "brain_bridge or version" -v` — 72 pass, 1 skipped, 0 fail
- [x] `uv run pytest packages/tapps-core/tests/ -m "not slow"` — 1112 pass, 6 skipped, 0 regressions

Mocking uses `unittest.mock.patch` against `tapps_core.brain_bridge.httpx.get`, matching the patch-at-source style already used in `test_brain_cridge.py`'s factory tests.

### Motivation
- Avoid failing startup for scenes that are arm-only or that use non-3-finger end-effectors by enforcing Robotiq 3F joint/TF and URDF-frame checks only when a Robotiq 3F EE is actually configured.
- Use the workcell context loaded from YAML (`Demo::init_from_yaml(workcell_context)`) to decide required readiness checks dynamically based on declared end-effectors (`end_effector.name`, `end_effector.brand`, and declared `links`).

- Added a `GraspReadinessProfile` type and helper functions (`to_lower_copy`, `is_robotiq_3f_end_effector`, `detect_grasp_readiness_profile`) that inspect `WorkcellContext::groups.*.end_effectors` to detect Robotiq 3F end-effectors and produce a profile describing whether 3F checks are required.

author: piny4man
body:
## Summary

- Delete `TerminalCapability` + `detect_from_env` from `src/icon.rs` and the `capability` plumbing in `src/launcher.rs`.
- Replace `KEYWORD_GLYPHS` (and the generic fallback) with Nerd Font codepoints in the private-use area, keyed by the same browser/terminal/editor/file-manager/chat/media/games/settings/office/graphics/dev-tools categories as before.
- Keep `resolve_icon` + `icon_search_paths` (and their helpers) behind `#[allow(dead_code)]` for the upcoming bitmap-icon path.
- Update existing `src/icon.rs` unit tests to the new mapping and add a guard test asserting every glyph lives in U+E000..=U+F8FF.
- Document the Nerd Font requirement in the README (new **Requirements** section, icon feature bullet, project tree, bench description).

Closes #23.

## Window config (#24)

- Extend the TOML config schema in `src/config.rs` with a `[window]` section accepting optional `width: u32`, `height: u32`, and `fullscreen: bool`.
- Default behavior: `fullscreen = true`, no explicit size.
- Validation mirrors `[colors]`: unknown keys rejected, type mismatches rejected via `deny_unknown_fields`.
- Added 5 unit tests covering: default, explicit size, `fullscreen = false`, unknown-key rejection, and type-mismatch rejection.
- Updated `config.example.toml` and README `Fields` table + Validation section to document the new section.

Closes #24.

## Font config + resolver (#25)

- Extend `src/config.rs` with a `[font]` section: `path: Option<PathBuf>`, `size: Option<f32>`. Validates positive size and rejects unknown keys / type mismatches via `deny_unknown_fields`.
- New `src/font.rs` module exposing `LoadedFont`, `trait FontDatabase`, and `resolve(&Config, &dyn FontDatabase) -> Option<LoadedFont>` implementing the PRD lookup matrix:
  - Configured path exists → use it.
  - Configured path missing → stderr warning + fall back to system lookup (does NOT hard-fail).
  - No path configured → try `JetBrainsMono Nerd Font → FiraCode Nerd Font → Symbols Nerd Font`.
  - No Nerd Font present → first available monospace.
- Default size `14.0pt` when `[font] size` is absent.
- Production `SystemFontDatabase` wraps `fontdb::Database`; tests inject a `FakeDb` (mirrors the `icon_search_paths` / `resolve_icon_in` injection pattern in `src/icon.rs`).
- Added `fontdb = "0.23.0"` as a regular dependency for now — the `window` feature split in #26/#27 will move it behind `dep:`.
- Added 5 config tests + 10 font-resolver tests covering the full matrix (configured-path exists/missing, preference order, JetBrains > others, monospace fallback, nothing-available, default size, size override, configured-size + configured-path).
- Updated `config.example.toml` and README `Fields` table + Validation section to document the new `[font]` section.

Closes #25.

## Cargo feature split: `terminal` / `window` (#26)

- `Cargo.toml`: declare `default = ["terminal"]`, `terminal = ["dep:crossterm"]`, `window = ["dep:ratatui-wgpu", "dep:winit", "dep:fontdb"]`; mark `crossterm`, `fontdb`, `ratatui-wgpu`, `winit` as `optional = true`.
- `src/lib.rs`: gate `input` and `terminal` modules behind `cfg(feature = "terminal")`; add new `window` module gated behind `cfg(feature = "window")`.
- `src/window.rs`: empty stub module — the ratatui-wgpu/winit event loop lands in #27.
- `src/main.rs`: `run()` is `cfg`-selected per feature; a `compile_error!` guards against building with no features.
- `src/app.rs`, `src/launcher.rs`, `tests/launcher_flow.rs`: `handle_event` and crossterm-using tests gated on `terminal` so the crate still compiles cleanly without it.
- `src/font.rs`: `SystemFontDatabase` (the only `fontdb`-using part) gated on `window`; the `FontDatabase` trait, `resolve()`, and the `FakeDb`-backed tests remain unconditional.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: CI now runs `cargo clippy` / `cargo test --no-default-features --features terminal --all-targets`, so the default job needs no display server.

Closes #26.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo build --no-default-features --features terminal`
- [x] `cargo clippy --no-default-features --features terminal --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] `cargo test --no-default-features --features terminal --all-targets` (139 unit + 10 integration tests pass)
- [x] Visual smoke test: launch burst inside a Nerd Font terminal and confirm glyphs render

---

## Change of direction (after testing) — reverts #24/#25/#26/#27

Issue #27 (ratatui-wgpu + winit native window) was implemented, built clean, and ran — but the rendered launcher was noticeably sluggish compared to the terminal path: the redraw loop requested a new frame unconditionally every vsync to keep the fade-in effect ticking, and the wgpu backend pays a real startup cost (shader compile + font atlas) that we don't need for a ~5MB terminal UI with no animation past the first second.

Pivoting to the design the README already described: burst stays a pure terminal UI, and a shell wrapper launches it inside the user's preferred terminal with `class=burst` / `app-id=burst` so the Hyprland `windowrule` set continues to float it fullscreen with blur and dim.

**What this commit reverts**

- **#27 (ratatui-wgpu backend)** — `src/window.rs` deleted, winit/ratatui-wgpu/fontdb/pollster deps removed, `src/input.rs` goes back to a thin crossterm poller.
- **#26 (terminal/window Cargo feature split)** — with only one backend, the features are dead weight. `crossterm` is an unconditional dep again; `cfg` gates removed.
- **#25 (font config + resolver)** — font selection now belongs to the host terminal emulator. `src/font.rs`, the `[font]` TOML section, and the `fontdb` dep are gone.
- **#24 (window config)** — window sizing / fullscreen is the host terminal's + Hyprland's job. The `[window]` TOML section and its tests are gone.

**What's new**

- `packaging/burst-launch` — POSIX shell wrapper. Resolution order: `$TERMINAL` first (if set and on PATH), then `alacritty → wezterm → ghostty → kitty → foot` (first found wins). Emits the correct flag per terminal (`--class=burst` for alacritty/kitty/ghostty/wezterm, `--app-id=burst` for foot).
- `packaging/burst.desktop` — `StartupWMClass=burst` so XDG desktop-entry consumers match the Hyprland rules.
- README gains a **Picking the host terminal** subsection documenting `$TERMINAL` with fish / bash examples, and the Hyprland bind becomes `bind = SUPER, Space, exec, burst-launch`.

**Verification**

- `cargo build` clean
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean
- `cargo fmt --check` clean
- `cargo test` — 106 unit + 10 integration tests pass
- Manual test: `packaging/burst-launch` opens burst inside the host terminal with class `burst`; Hyprland float rules apply.

Closes #27.

author: loganrosen
body:
When re-authenticating via the Web UI (e.g. switching Ring accounts), `ring.js` updates `restClient.refreshToken` but never updates `restClient.authConfig`. Since `getGrantData()` in `rest-client.ts` reads `authConfig.rt` for the OAuth grant, the stale `authConfig` means the client keeps authenticating with the old account's token.

**What this does:**

Adds a `parseRefreshToken()` helper (mirrors the upstream `parseAuthConfig` logic) and calls it at both places where `refreshToken` gets updated outside of the initial client creation:

1. The interval check that detects an invalid/changed refresh token (~line 94)
2. The `init()` re-auth branch when a new token arrives from the web UI (~line 112)

The initial `RingApi` constructor and the `onRefreshTokenUpdated` subscription already handle `authConfig` internally, so those don't need changes.

Fixes #1078

body:
`POST /api/repos/add` only enqueued ingestion on repo creation. Repos already in `pending` or `failed` states silently returned 200 without triggering any work.

## Changes

**`backend/app/github_routes.py`**
- Replaced the `newly_created`-only enqueue guard with a full state-machine dispatch:

```python
if newly_created:
    _enqueue_repo_ingestion(str(repo.id))

elif repo.ingestion_status in ("pending", "failed"):
    _enqueue_repo_ingestion(str(repo.id))   # explicit retry allowed

elif repo.ingestion_status in ("running", "success"):
    raise HTTPException(
        status_code=409,
        detail=f"REPO_INGESTION_{repo.ingestion_status.upper()}",
    )
```

- All enqueue paths now have consistent error handling (try/except + logging).
- The worker-side guard (`if repo.ingestion_status in ("running", "success"): return`) is unchanged — still prevents duplicate execution and race conditions.

## State transition table

| `ingestion_status` | Response | Action |
|--------------------|----------|--------|
| *(new repo)* | 200 | enqueue |
| `pending` | 200 | enqueue |
| `failed` | 200 | enqueue (retry) |
| `running` | 409 | — |
| `success` | 409 | — |

body: ## Summary Resolves **P20** ("high-impact"): when the OIDC callback fails, the user currently lands on the backend domain looking at raw FastAPI JSON (`{"detail": "..."}`), and the raw error message is embedded in server access logs / downstream log aggregators. This PR converts every `HTTPException` raised from `/api/auth/oidc/callback` into a client-side HTML redirect back to the configured frontend origin, carrying a short, stable, URL-safe error code in the URL fragment (`#oidc_error=`). The frontend captures the code from the fragment, strips it from the URL, and renders a user-facing message on the login screen. ### Backend — `backend/app/routers/oidc.py` - `_resolve_frontend_origin()` returns `oidc_post_login_redirect`, falling back to the first non-wildcard entry in `cors_origins`, or `""`. - `_fragment_redirect(origin, fragment)` returns an HTML `window.location.replace(...)` page with `Cache-Control: no-store, no-cache`. A client-side redirect is used (not HTTP 302) because some proxies strip the fragment from `Location` headers. - Six stable error codes now drive the UX: `client_misconfigured`, `provider_unreachable`, `token_exchange_failed`, `userinfo_failed`, `missing_claims`, `subject_mismatch`. - `_oidc_callback_error(code, log_detail=…)` is the single funnel for all failure paths. When no frontend origin is configured at all, it still raises a 500 `HTTPException` so an operator sees the missing configuration instead of a silent dead end. The `log_detail` argument is only passed through to the existing structured logger — it is **never** included in the redirect response body or URL, so sensitive provider errors stay in backend logs. ### Frontend - `AuthContext.tsx`: the existing `oidc_token` fragment handler now also reads `oidc_error`. The error code is captured synchronously via a `useState` initializer (so we don't violate the `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` rule) and the fragment is stripped from the URL in the existing `useEffect`. A new `clearOidcError` callback is exposed via the context. - `LoginScreen.tsx` reads `oidcError` / `clearOidcError` via `useAuth()` and renders a dismissable MUI `` above the sign-in form. A local `OIDC_ERROR_MESSAGES` map translates each stable code to a user-facing sentence, with a generic fallback so unknown codes (e.g. from future backend additions) still render something sensible. ### Tests - `backend/tests/test_router_oidc.py`: every former `HTTPException` assertion is replaced with a `_assert_oidc_error_redirect(resp, expected_code, origin)` helper that checks `HTMLResponse`, body contains the exact target URL, and `Cache-Control: no-store` is set. New unit tests cover `_resolve_frontend_origin` precedence and `_fragment_redirect` HTML/JS escaping. All 35 tests in this file pass. - `frontend/tests/components/LoginScreen.test.tsx`: `useAuth` is mocked so LoginScreen can be rendered without an `AuthProvider` wrapper. Four new tests cover the known-code, unknown-code, dismiss, and null-error paths. All 20 tests pass. ### Verification - `cd backend && poetry run pytest --cov-fail-under=80` → **302 passed**, coverage gate satisfied. - `cd frontend && npm test -- --run` → **122 passed** across 9 files. - `npx eslint` scoped to changed files introduces **zero new lint violations** over baseline. ## Review & Testing Checklist for Human - [ ] **Verify no sensitive information leaks into the redirect URL.** The fragment should only ever contain `oidc_error=` — grep the final response body for the original exception message, PII, tokens, or provider URLs. - [ ] **Test against the real Vault OIDC provider** with a deliberately misconfigured scenario (e.g. wrong `OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET` → `token_exchange_failed`; temporarily block egress to Vault → `provider_unreachable`; strip the `email` scope to get `missing_claims`). Confirm the browser lands on the frontend login screen with the correct alert text and the fragment is stripped from the URL after render. - [ ] **Confirm the fallback path**: unset both `OIDC_POST_LOGIN_REDIRECT` and any non-wildcard `CORS_ORIGINS` entry, trigger any callback error, and verify the backend returns a 500 with a descriptive message (so the misconfiguration is obvious rather than silent). - [ ] **Confirm successful logins are unchanged**: a healthy OIDC flow should still redirect to `/#oidc_token=...` exactly as before, and the login alert should not appear. ### Notes - Error codes are intentionally short and opaque so they can be remapped or localized by the frontend without touching the backend. The backend still logs the full underlying exception via the existing structured logger. - If additional error codes are added in the future, update both the constants block in `backend/app/routers/oidc.py` and the `OIDC_ERROR_MESSAGES` map in `frontend/src/components/LoginScreen.tsx` (the frontend comment calls this out explicitly). Unknown codes fall back to a generic message so this pairing is forgiving. - P16–P19 are handled in #109, #110, and #111. P18 (confirmation dialog for file import) is a separate frontend-only change and will land in its own PR. author: robinmordasiewicz
body:
## Summary

- Register `pd-claude-opus-4-7` as a first-class custom Anthropic model in pi/omp/xcsh `models.json` and inline in `crush.json`, so their resolvers stop stripping the `pd-` prefix and emitting `claude-opus-4-7` (which the F5 liteLLM proxy rejects with `400 Invalid model name`).
- Defeat pi-ai's in-place `defaultModel` fallback rewrite by overwriting `~/.pi/agent/settings.json` on every boot, and stop crush re-fetching its embedded Catwalk catalog via `options.disable_provider_auto_update: true`.
- Fix stale `"Claude Opus 4.6"` display name on the `pd-claude-opus-4-7` entry in `opencode.json`.

Closes #986

## Changes

- `entrypoint.sh` — pi/omp/xcsh `models.json` template now includes `pd-claude-opus-4-7` under the anthropic provider (ModelDefinitionSchema: id/api/reasoning/input/cost/contextWindow/maxTokens). Overwrites `~/.pi/agent/settings.json` every boot. Runs `sed 's|__CRUSH_BASE_URL__|${LITELLM_BASE_URL}/anthropic|'` against the committed crush config. Adds a non-fatal startup curl probe that warns if the proxy returns non-200 for `pd-claude-opus-4-7`.
- `crush-config/crush.json` — rewritten with `options.disable_provider_auto_update: true` and an inline `providers.anthropic.models[]` entry for `pd-claude-opus-4-7`. Uses the `__CRUSH_BASE_URL__` placeholder so no F5 hostname is committed. Both `large` and `small` point at `pd-claude-opus-4-7` as a temporary workaround for crush's embedded short-id alias (follow-up tracked separately).
- `opencode-config/opencode.json` — corrected display name to `Claude Opus 4.7`.

## Test plan

- [x] `bash -n entrypoint.sh` passes
- [x] `jq .` validates `crush.json` and `opencode.json`
- [x] `sed "s|__CRUSH_BASE_URL__|...|" crush.json` renders a correct absolute URL
- [x] `pi --print --provider anthropic --model pd-claude-opus-4-7 --no-session 'hi'` returns a response (no 400)
- [x] `xcsh -p --model pd-claude-opus-4-7 --no-session 'hi'` returns a response (no 400)
- [x] `crush run 'hi'` returns a response; logs show no 400 errors
- [x] `opencode run -m anthropic-proxy/pd-claude-opus-4-7 'hi'` returns a response
- [x] `hermes chat -Q -q 'hi'` returns a response (OpenAI pass-through regression guard)
- [x] `~/.pi/agent/settings.json` `defaultModel` remains `pd-claude-opus-4-7` after pi runs
- [ ] CI checks pass (`Check linked issues`, `Lint Code Base`, any other required)

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- `@oh-my-pi/pi-natives` arm64 native-addon build failure blocks `omp` start; needs a devcontainer issue.
- Charmbracelet/crush: custom `providers.<name>.models[]` entries don't override embedded short-id aliases; needs an upstream issue.

author: alexander-zimmermann
body:
The Gatus image ships without a non-root USER instruction, so the chart's containerSecurityContext.runAsNonRoot: true caused the pod to refuse startup:

  Error: container has runAsNonRoot and image will run as root

Set runAsUser/runAsGroup to 65534 (nobody) — matches the upstream TwiN Helm chart defaults — and add fsGroup: 65534 at pod level so the shared emptyDir + ConfigMap mounts are accessible.

body:
### Motivation
- Fix persistent report content overflow and clipped Download PDF action so the final brief is fully readable and the export action is always accessible. 
- Shift the app visual direction from a dark/industrial developer palette to a softer, premium hospitality palette so reports feel like client-facing concept briefs. 
- Improve button/chip active states and section hierarchy so selections are unmistakable and the report reads like a polished design deck.

author: livinglikekrillin
body:
## Summary
`MethodArgumentNotValidException` (Bean Validation 실패)이 `GlobalExceptionHandler`에서 잡히지 않아 기존 `Exception.class` fallback으로 빠져 **500 Internal Server Error**를 반환하고 있었음.

## Why
- `MethodArgumentTypeMismatchException` 핸들러는 이미 있음 (line 72)
- 그 옆의 `@Valid` 실패 핸들러만 누락 — 정책 변화가 아니라 **명백한 코드 갭**
- 현재 `@Valid @RequestBody`를 쓰는 컨트롤러 10개(admin/demo, admin/user, auth, crew-block, crew-grade, crew-penalty, dj, party-access, partyroom, playback-reaction) 전부 묵시적 500 반환 중

## What
- `GlobalExceptionHandler`에 `@ExceptionHandler(MethodArgumentNotValidException.class)` 추가 → 400 + 필드별 에러 메시지
- 응답 메시지 포맷: `"field: message; field: message"` (여러 필드 오류 시 세미콜론 결합)
- `GlobalExceptionHandlerTest`에 단일/다중 필드 케이스 테스트 2개 추가

## Risk
거의 0. 이전엔 500을 받던 요청이 이제 400을 받음 — 이미 500은 서비스 로직상 올바른 응답이 아니었으므로 클라이언트가 의존할 일 없음.

## Test plan
- [x] `:common:test` pass (handler 유닛 테스트)
- [ ] merge 후 develop 기반 feature 브랜치의 `@Valid` 실패 케이스 통합 테스트에서 400 반환 확인

author: nitu01019
body:
Adds a telemetry hook at the single createOrder fallback branch in
BookingApiRepository (~line 590) so that every time the customer app
downgrades from the primary /bookings/orders endpoint to the legacy
/orders endpoint on a 400/404/405/422/501 response, a structured
event is emitted. The event carries:

  event  = "booking_legacy_fallback_invoked"
  params = {
    endpoint          : "bookings/orders",
    primary_code      : <http status as string>,
    primary_error_code: <backend code or "none" for stable cardinality>
  }

The fallback BEHAVIOR is unchanged — the legacy /orders route is still
invoked when the primary is gated by one of the trigger status codes.
This is pure observability so the fallback hit rate becomes a metric
and the legacy route + fallback can eventually be retired in a
coordinated backend+client release once the rate sits at zero for
~ 4 weeks.

The telemetry sink is a thin abstraction (BookingTelemetry) wrapping
FirebaseCrashlytics.getInstance() — the SAME sink already used by
WeeloApplication.initializeSecurity, CustomBookingActivity.logError,
MapSelectionActivity, WeeloPlacesAdapter, and LoadingStateManager.
No new analytics SDK is introduced and no new gradle dependency is
added (firebase-crashlytics-ktx is pre-existing per app/build.gradle).
The abstraction makes the call site read like an analytics intent
instead of a Crashlytics implementation detail, and it lets JVM unit
tests swap in an in-memory capture without pulling FirebaseCrashlytics
onto the test classpath.

Tests (src/test/.../BookingTelemetryTest.kt) — 8/8 passing:
  - canonical event name
  - 400 response emission with primary_code=400
  - 404 response emission
  - 422 response emission with null error code normalized to "none"
  - 501 response emission
  - blank error code normalized to "none"
  - sink exceptions do NOT propagate (best-effort contract)
  - four consecutive fallbacks yield four entries in order

Local verification used `./gradlew :app:testDebugUnitTest --tests
com.weelo.logistics.data.telemetry.BookingTelemetryTest` with two
pre-existing BROKEN peer tests (DataSafetyTest, LocationInputViewModelTest)
temporarily moved aside — those are stale against the current domain
model and have been broken since the initial commit (b1ac3c1); out of
scope for this ticket. Files restored post-run; no repo change.

Ticket: L1 (Phase 1, T1.3).
Rollback: `git revert <this commit>` restores the original fallback
branch verbatim; zero risk either direction.

See .planning/verification/ISSUES-AND-SOLUTIONS.md#L1

body:
## Summary
- Adds `pod-template-configmap.yaml` — a ConfigMap containing the worker pod spec used by KubernetesExecutor
- Sets `AIRFLOW__KUBERNETES_EXECUTOR__POD_TEMPLATE_FILE` in the scheduler so it knows where to read the template
- Mounts the ConfigMap into the scheduler at `/opt/airflow/pod_template.yaml`
- Moves `AIRFLOW__API__SECRET_KEY` in the scheduler to reference the external Secret (removes last hardcoded key)

## Root cause
Every `mlpipeline_test_training` run failed immediately with:
```
spec.containers[0].image: Required value
```
The KubernetesExecutor needs a pod template to set the worker container image. Without one it submits an empty pod spec, which Kubernetes rejects.

author: bendrucker
body:
Sets `compatibility_date` on `cloudflare_workers_script.things_redirect` to force a re-upload of the worker, which is missing from the Cloudflare account and causing `https://things.bendrucker.me` to return `522`.

## Issue

`workers_list` on the account shows only `strava`, `bendrucker-me`, and `github`. The `things-redirect` worker is absent, so the route `things.bendrucker.me/*` has no handler, and `curl -sSI https://things.bendrucker.me/` returns `HTTP/2 522`.

The resource was introduced in #75 (`8b934f2`). Recent Terraform Cloud applies (#76, #77, #79, #84, #85) report `SUCCESS` on GitHub checks, yet the worker has not been restored. Forcing a visible diff via `compatibility_date` ensures the next apply re-uploads the script.

## Changes

- `things.tf`: add `compatibility_date = "2026-03-06"` to `cloudflare_workers_script.things_redirect`.

## Testing

After merge and apply:

- `workers_list` includes `things-redirect`.
- `curl -sSI https://things.bendrucker.me/` returns `200` with `content-type: text/html;charset=UTF-8`.
- `curl -s https://things.bendrucker.me/foo?bar=1` returns the redirect HTML body.

author: gin0115
body:
CI resolver was failing on 'composer update --no-cache' because the ^8.0 || ^9.0 phpunit range overlapped packagist security advisories (PKSA-5jz8-6tcw-pbk4, PKSA-z3gr-8qht-p93v) and composer refused to load the affected versions. Locally the resolver found 9.6.34 anyway, but the CI resolver path differed and errored out.

Narrow to ^9.6 — we dropped PHP 7.x when we required PHP 8.0+, so phpunit 8.x is no longer useful, and yoast/phpunit-polyfills already requires ^9.5.27 transitively.

While in composer.json, fix the 'coverage' script to emit clover.xml explicitly. The <logging><log coverage-clover> block in phpunit.xml.dist uses a PHPUnit 9-deprecated schema that emits on our local devilbox but is skipped on the GitHub Actions runner, so the codecov upload step found 0 files to upload.

author: pickleballattrespalapas
body:
### Motivation
- Replace the existing blanket structure lock that prevented all Tournament Setup edits when any registrations existed with a finer-grained publish analysis so admins can safely edit and republish published tournaments.
- Allow safe non-destructive edits (labels, capacity increases, new days/divisions, etc.) while preventing or converting destructive changes that would break existing registrations.
- Preserve row identity and history for published days/divisions so public registration and downstream modules continue to read a stable published contract.

### Description
- Added repository helpers in `jupr_app/domain/tournament_registration_repo.py`: `list_registration_usage_by_event_option`, `list_registration_usage_by_day`, `analyze_registration_publish_impact`, and `publish_registration_configuration` to perform draft-vs-published diff analysis and apply guarded publishes with soft-close semantics instead of destructive replace for populated tournaments.
- Implemented guarded publish rules that preserve stable IDs when logical entities remain the same, warn for risky but allowed edits (e.g. modest capacity reductions, relabels), block destructive edits (e.g. deleting populated divisions/days, moving populated divisions between days, changing participant/gender/type or rules that would invalidate registrants, reducing capacity below occupied), and convert removed populated items into soft-closed/disabled rows rather than hard deletes.
- Reworked Tournament Setup UI in `jupr_app/ui/pages/tournament_manager.py` to remove the blanket `structure_locked` freeze, keep draft-save workflows intact, show a publish impact summary on the `Publish & QA` tab (counts, safe creates/updates, soft-closes, deletes, warnings, blocked items), and call `publish_registration_configuration` instead of the destructive `replace_registration_configuration` for published tournaments (preserving the replace-path when zero registrations exist).
- Files changed: `jupr_app/domain/tournament_registration_repo.py` and `jupr_app/ui/pages/tournament_manager.py`, and code comments summarizing the final publish rules were added near the `publish_registration_configuration` implementation.
- Deferred/notes: deleting an event-family is inferred from removal of its child divisions (there is no separate persisted family entity to gate independently), and identity fallback for draft events without IDs uses a conservative fingerprint so very unusual bulk-renames may be treated as create+close instead of pure updates.

### Testing
- Ran byte-compile verification with `python -m py_compile jupr_app/domain/tournament_registration_repo.py jupr_app/ui/pages/tournament_manager.py`, which succeeded.
- No additional automated unit tests were added in this change; runtime behavior for UI flows should be validated in staging, and edge-case scenarios (bulk renames / unusual identity collisions) were documented and deferred for follow-up tests.

author: aes256afro
body:
## Summary

New **🗣 Auto-captions** button on the Trim tab runs [faster-whisper](https://github.com/guillaumekln/faster-whisper) over the current trim range and imports the result through the existing SRT → text-layers pipeline. One click: captioned clip.

## Why

Roadmap #9. Closes the loop on "captioned clip" workflows — previously users had to go to a separate service, download SRT, drag it in. Now the app does all three steps.

## Design

- **Pure core module** (`videokidnapper/core/whisper_captions.py`):
  - `is_available()` — cheap import probe, called at UI startup so the button can be conditionally enabled without paying model-load cost.
  - `extract_audio_segment()` — ffmpeg at `-ar 16000 -ac 1 -acodec pcm_s16le`. No Python-side resampling, matches exactly what Whisper expects.
  - `segments_to_entries()` — pure function that normalizes faster-whisper Segment objects into the `{start, end, text}` dict shape the existing `srt_to_text_layers` consumes. **This is what makes testing tractable** — synthetic SimpleNamespaces stand in for Segments, no model required.
  - `transcribe()` — wires everything with progress + cancellation hooks.

- **UI hook:** button sits next to Import SRT; a small dialog picks model size (tiny/base/small/medium/large, default base); transcription runs in a worker thread; results feed `text_layers.import_srt_layers` — the same code path SRT import uses, so auto-caption layers get the reorder/duplicate/fade treatment for free.

- **Optional dep:** `faster-whisper` added to `requirements.txt` under the existing commented "Optional" block. Missing → button shows `pip install faster-whisper` hint. Core install unchanged.

## Why faster-whisper, not openai-whisper

| | faster-whisper | openai-whisper |
|---|---|---|
| CPU inference speed | **~4× faster** (CTranslate2) | baseline |
| Requires torch / CUDA | no | yes |
| Model quality | same as upstream | same |
| License | MIT | MIT |

The CPU-only path matters because many target users don't have dedicated GPUs. A 1-minute clip transcribes in ~15–30s on a modern laptop with the `base` model, which is right at the edge of "feels instant enough."

## Test plan

- [x] `python -m pytest tests/ -q` — 145 passed (9 new in `test_whisper_captions.py`)
- [x] `python -m ruff check videokidnapper/ main.py scripts/ tests/` — clean
- [x] Segment → SRT-dict conversion pinned (offset, empty-text filter, zero-duration repair, dict-like object support)
- [x] Unknown-model-size rejection + missing-dep error surface both covered
- [ ] **Manual verification:** with faster-whisper installed, load a clip with speech, click Auto-captions, confirm layers appear at the right times

## License

- [x] Apache-2.0
- [x] SPDX headers on new files
- [x] faster-whisper is MIT-licensed; users install it themselves

## Notes for reviewers

**Scope:**
- Transcription only. Translation (`--task translate`), speaker diarization, and word-level timestamps are post-MVP. Worth separate PRs if/when they get demand.
- Per-clip operation only (uses `range_slider.get_values()`). Captioning *across* queued ranges would need its own UI affordance.
- No preview of the raw transcript before import — layers just appear in the panel and the user can edit / delete from there. Simpler than a "review & accept" step.

**Performance:**
- First run downloads the selected model into `~/.cache/huggingface` (~40 MB tiny, ~75 MB base, ~250 MB small, ~750 MB medium, ~1.5 GB large). Subsequent runs are cache hits.
- CPU inference is fine for clip-length work; GPU paths are available by installing CUDA-enabled CTranslate2, but we don't configure that explicitly — faster-whisper auto-detects.

**No overlap with other open PRs:** new core module, one UI button in trim_tab.py, one new row in requirements.txt, doc additions only elsewhere.

author: anchapin
body:
🚨 Severity: CRITICAL
💡 Vulnerability: The `cli/pdf/converter.py` and `cli/generators/cover_letter_generator.py` modules invoked `pdflatex` and `pandoc` without the `-no-shell-escape` flag, and without any execution timeouts.
🎯 Impact: Remote Code Execution (RCE) via LaTeX shell escapes if an attacker or AI hallucination controls the template content. Denial of Service (DoS) via infinite compilation loops resulting in application hangs.
🔧 Fix: Appended `-no-shell-escape` (and `--pdf-engine-opt=-no-shell-escape`) to the `subprocess.Popen` arguments. Enforced `timeout=30` on all `process.communicate()` calls, along with proper `try...except subprocess.TimeoutExpired` handling to kill hanging processes.
✅ Verification: Ran `pytest tests/` locally to ensure no regressions in PDF generation and timeout exception handling (which was verified against `tests/test_pdf_security.py`).

- `cli_param_set_json_types` — 6 JSON types (int, float, string, bool, array, object)
- `cli_param_set_rejects_unknown_target`
- `cli_param_get_nonexistent`
- `cli_param_delete_rejects_unknown_target`

That row in the matrix was wrong.

What the existing WS tests don't cover is the **`dora param` CLI binary code path** — argument parsing, JSON deserialization inside the clap layer, the stdout formatting each subcommand performs. A regression in `binaries/cli/src/command/param/*.rs` would slip past them.

## New tests

Under a `param_cli` submodule in `ws-cli-e2e.rs`:

### `cli_param_crud_via_subprocess`

Invokes `dora param {set,get,list,delete}` as a subprocess against an in-process coordinator with a seeded dataflow record. Asserts specific stdout markers:

| Command | Asserted stdout |
|---|---|
| `dora param set sensor rate 100` | `Set \`rate\` = 100 on node \`sensor\`` |
| `dora param get sensor rate` | bare `100` (JSON value) |
| `dora param list sensor` | `rate = 100` |
| `dora param list sensor --format json` | parseable JSON with `rate: 100` |
| `dora param delete sensor rate` | `Deleted \`rate\` from node \`sensor\`` |
| `dora param get sensor rate` (after delete) | non-zero exit |

### `cli_param_set_rejects_non_json_value`

Regression guard for the "invalid JSON value" parse path in `param/set.rs` — a bare word like `hello` isn't valid JSON (needs quotes) and must exit non-zero with an `invalid JSON` stderr message.

## Capability matrix update

`docs/testing-capabilities.md`:
- Parameter operations section expanded to **five rows** listing both WS-layer and CLI-layer coverage.
- Removed `Parameter operations — no tests` from the Open coverage gaps index.

## Verification

$ cargo test --test ws-cli-e2e param_cli:: -- --test-threads=1

body:
## Summary

Restructured the codebase from three standalone game scripts into a unified pygame arcade launcher with a plugin-based game discovery system. All games now share common infrastructure for assets, audio, fonts, leaderboards, and UI.

## Key Changes

- **New arcade launcher** (`vaj_games/arcade.py`): Menu-driven game selector with keyboard navigation (Up/Down to choose, Enter to play, Esc to quit)

- **Game modularization**: Converted `specialdaydodger.py`, `main.py`, and `maddiepaddy.py` into structured game packages:
  - `vaj_games/games/special_day_dodger/game.py`
  - `vaj_games/games/maddie_paddy/game.py`
  - Each exports `META` (game metadata) and `run(screen, clock)` function

- **Shared core infrastructure** (`vaj_games/core/`):
  - `assets.py`: Unified image/sound/font loading from `assets/` tree
  - `audio.py`: Mute-aware pygame.mixer wrappers
  - `fonts.py`: Centralized font loading with fallbacks
  - `leaderboard.py`: Persistent JSON-based leaderboards with initials entry UI
  - `text.py`: Text rendering helpers (draw_text, draw_wrapped)
  - `game.py`: GameMeta contract dataclass

- **Centralized configuration** (`vaj_games/config.py`): Single source of truth for arcade name, palette, screen size, FPS, and asset paths. Games inherit these defaults.

- **Auto-discovery system** (`vaj_games/games/__init__.py`): Games are discovered by introspection—no manual registration needed. Drop a new game folder with `game.py` and it appears in the menu.

- **Reorganized assets**: Moved all images, audio, and fonts into `assets/` with subdirectories; leaderboard data into `data/leaderboards/`

- **Entry point**: Added `vaj_games/__main__.py` for `python -m vaj_games` and updated `pyproject.toml` with arcade entry point

## Notable Implementation Details

- Games no longer manage pygame initialization; the arcade owns the lifecycle
- Esc key on title/leaderboard screens returns to arcade menu (not a hard exit)
- Leaderboard UI is shared: games call `leaderboard.get_initials()` and `leaderboard.show()` 
- Mute state is per-game but respects a global audio mute flag
- Asset loading is lazy and path-agnostic (uses `config.IMAGES`, `config.AUDIO`, etc.)
- Game state is encapsulated in local dicts within each game's `run()` function

author: leocolomb
body:
Consumers of another provider resource should cascade from it, not re-declare the attributes they do not own. Two places violated that:

- `anytype_type.properties` required `{ key, name, format }` per linked property — three attributes copied from `anytype_property`.
- `anytype_object.type_key` forced consumers to reach into `anytype_type.foo.key` rather than just point at the type resource.

`anytype_type.properties` now takes `{ id = anytype_property.foo.id }`; the provider resolves the backend `key` / `name` / `format` triplet (now Computed) by calling GetProperty on each referenced id.

`anytype_object` now accepts `type_id` as an alternative to `type_key` (exactly-one-of). When `type_id` is set, the provider resolves the backend `type_key` via GetType. Both attributes are Computed so state stays populated regardless of which one the user supplied.

author: jah-yee
body:
Good day,

This PR fixes issue #17355, a Firefox-specific bug where React incorrectly throws 'Should not already be working' when a component calls alert(), debugger, or confirm during componentDidMount.

## Root Cause

In Firefox, blocking calls like alert(), debugger, and confirm do not prevent MessageChannel events from firing (see Mozilla bugs 758004 and 951805). Other browsers correctly block these events.

When React calls componentDidMount, it sets the executionContext to RenderContext. If an alert/debugger is called, React's scheduler (which uses MessageChannel) posts a message event that triggers performWorkOnRoot. React then checks if we're already rendering and throws 'Should not already be working.' This bug does not occur in Chrome or Safari because they correctly block MessageChannel events while a dialog is shown.

## Fix

Instead of throwing an error, exit early from performWorkOnRoot and completeRoot when we detect a re-entrant render context. Log a warning in DEV mode to inform developers of the issue and suggest wrapping blocking calls in setTimeout. When the blocked event finishes, it will re-schedule a new render.

## Changes

- Modified performWorkOnRoot and completeRoot in ReactFiberWorkLoop.js to gracefully exit (with DEV warning) instead of throwing when executionContext is non-zero.
- Added comments explaining the Firefox-specific behavior and linking to the relevant Mozilla bug reports.

## Testing

The fix has been verified against the reproduction steps from the issue:
1. Open a React app in Firefox
2. Put an alert() or debugger statement in componentDidMount after a setState
3. Previously this would throw 'Should not already be working'
4. With this fix, React logs a warning and gracefully continues

Thank you for your attention. If there are any issues or suggestions, please leave a comment and I will address them promptly.

Warmly,
RoomWithOutRoof

body:
### Motivation

- Prefer human-curated Chinese explanations/translations for UI chips and orphan text when they are high-quality and actually Chinese, while avoiding using noisy Malay-heavy strings.
- Avoid dropping protected entities (historical names/acronyms) when substituting curated content.
- Add the first manual revision rollout payloads for many chapters so the UI can present curated ZH content for those units.

### Description

- Added heuristics in `assets/js/zh-mode.js`: `looksMalayHeavy` to detect Malay-dominated strings and `isUsableCuratedZhText` to decide when a curated Chinese translation is safe to use. 
- Integrated curated-text selection into the UI flow by updating `buildChipBackContent` and `buildPointExplainText` to prefer normalized, usable curated text (`normalizeZhExplain`) when available and to fall back to existing translation logic otherwise. 
- Ensured protected entities are preserved by checking `extractProtectedEntities` and verifying placeholders/placeholder maps before accepting curated text.
- Populated many `data/zh-units/*.json` files (chapters `bab-1`, `bab-2`, `bab-3`, and subfiles) with `meta` (including `rollout: "gelombang-1-manual-revision"`) and dozens/hundreds of unit entries containing `bm_original`, `translate`, `key_points_zh`, and `bm_focus_phrase` so the frontend can surface the new curated content.

### Testing

- Ran code style/lint checks via `npm run lint` (no lint errors) and the existing test suite via `npm test` (all tests passed). 
- Performed a local smoke test of chip flip and orphan-text annotation flows in the dev build to confirm curated text selection and fallback behavior worked as expected.

author: yxsamliu
body:
When compiler-rt is built for a GPU target in the same runtimes build
as LLVM-libc, the profile sources `#include <string.h>`, `<limits.h>`,
... Those headers are generated by LLVM-libc for the GPU triple.

A concrete example is the amdgcn runtimes build:

    -DLLVM_RUNTIME_TARGETS='default;amdgcn-amd-amdhsa'
    -DRUNTIMES_amdgcn-amd-amdhsa_LLVM_ENABLE_RUNTIMES='compiler-rt;libc'
    -DRUNTIMES_amdgcn-amd-amdhsa_RUNTIMES_USE_LIBC=llvm-libc

Even though `libc` is configured before `compiler-rt`, both sets of
targets live in the same ninja graph and race each other. Ninja can
start compiling `compiler-rt/lib/profile/InstrProfiling.c` before
LLVM-libc has finished generating its GPU `string.h`, and even when
hdrgen has finished, the profile compile needs `-isystem` pointing at
the generated header tree.

Use the runtimes-side libc-provider abstraction in
`runtimes/cmake/Modules/HandleLibC.cmake`:

  - at compiler-rt top level, `include(HandleLibC)` when
    `LLVM_RUNTIMES_BUILD` is set, so all compiler-rt subcomponents can
    reuse the `runtimes-libc-*` targets. `libcxx` / `libcxxabi` /
    `libunwind` include it the same way at their top-level CMakeLists.
  - in `compiler-rt/lib/profile/CMakeLists.txt`, when the GPU build
    sees the sibling `runtimes-libc-headers` target, pass it through
    `LINK_LIBS` of `add_compiler_rt_runtime(clang_rt.profile ...)`.

In the `llvm-libc` case this pulls in LLVM-libc's `libc-headers`
(`-isystem <build>/include/<triple>`), waits for
`generate-libc-headers`, and adds `-nostdlibinc` so the profile compile
does not consult host C library paths.

The dependency is added only when `COMPILER_RT_GPU_BUILD` is on and the
sibling `runtimes-libc-headers` target actually exists, so host
compiler-rt builds, standalone compiler-rt builds, and runtimes builds
without LLVM-libc selected are unchanged.

`add_compiler_rt_runtime` passes `LINK_LIBS` to
`target_link_libraries(<libname> PRIVATE ...)`, so the include path is
used when compiling the profile target itself but is not propagated to
downstream consumers of `libclang_rt.profile.a`.

Related: PR #177665.
