author: karstenm1987
body:
Fixes two code-level bugs in `gmd.ado`, identified by a stress-test against the live S3 backend. Tracked upstream at [Global-Macro-Database-Internal#412](https://github.com/KMueller-Lab/Global-Macro-Database-Internal/issues/412).

## 1. Multi-variable `sources()` returned 0 rows (P0)

The help file ([`gmd.sthlp:66`](https://github.com/KMueller-Lab/Global-Macro-Database-Stata/blob/main/stata/gmd.sthlp#L66)) says:

> You can specify a varlist with this option to load only specific variables from that source.

But live, anything past one variable was silently broken:
```
. gmd nGDP rGDP, sources(IMF_IFS)
variable rGDP not found
This source doesn't have data on nGDP rGDP. It has data on ...
rc=0   rows=0
```
Root cause: `cap confirm var \`sources'_\`anything'` expanded to `confirm var IMF_IFS_nGDP rGDP`, which Stata parsed as a varlist and failed on the unprefixed `rGDP`.

Each requested variable is now validated and prefixed individually:
```
. gmd nGDP rGDP, sources(IMF_IFS)                  -> rc=0, 14603 rows
. gmd nGDP rGDP, sources(IMF_IFS) country(USA)     -> rc=0, 85 rows
. gmd nGDP fake_var, sources(IMF_IFS)
Source IMF_IFS does not have: fake_var
It has data on CA_USD M0 M3 USDfx cbrate cons exports ...     -> rc=498
```

## 2. `network(no)` bypassed the internet check (P1)

[`gmd.ado:137-142`](https://github.com/KMueller-Lab/Global-Macro-Database-Stata/blob/main/stata/gmd.ado#L137-L142) treated any non-empty `network()` value as "bypass the check" — so `gmd, network(no)` meant the opposite of what a user writing `no` would assume.

Now `network()` requires one of `yes / y / on / true / 1` (case-insensitive); anything else errors out up-front with `exit 198`.

```
. gmd nGDP, country(USA) network(yes)   -> rc=0, 242 rows
. gmd nGDP, country(USA) network(no)    -> rc=198, "Invalid value for network(): no..."
. gmd nGDP, country(USA) network(nope)  -> rc=198, "Invalid value for network(): nope..."
```

## Regression pass

```
gmd, sources(IMF_IFS)        rc=0   rows=14603
gmd, sources(CS1_ARG)        rc=0   rows=35
gmd rGDP, sources(IMF_IFS)   rc=0   rows=14603
gmd nGDP, country(USA)       rc=0   rows=242
```

All verified live in Stata MP 18 against the live S3 backend.

## Out of scope for this PR

- **Missing version files (P0).** `versions.csv` advertises `2025_01`, `2025_03`, `2025_05`, `2025_06`, `2025_08`, but `.dta` files for all five return HTTP 404. That's a release-pipeline issue — re-upload or drop from `versions.csv` — not a `gmd.ado` change. Same root cause affects the R and Python packages.

author: karmarsten
body:
## Summary

Wires the `reminderLeadMinutes` that [PR 21](https://github.com/KarMarsten/were-all-in-this-together/pull/21) started persisting into actual OS-level alerts — the missing piece of the Appointments MVP.

The existing medication reminder machinery (nag chains, Taken/Skip, ACK drainer) is untouched; the two families co-exist by namespacing notification payloads via a `kind` field. Legacy payloads with no `kind` decode as medication reminders, so in-flight nags survive the upgrade.

### What's new

- **`AppointmentReminder` + `AppointmentReminderPayload`** — deliberately simpler than `ScheduledReminder`: one-shot, no nag chain, no action buttons. Reminder id is derived from `appointmentId` alone so rescheduling is an idempotent OS overwrite.
- **`NotificationService` extension** — gains `scheduleAppointmentReminder`, `pendingAppointmentReminderIds`, and `pendingMedicationReminderIds` (the old `pendingReminderIds` became kind-specific). Both reconcilers diff their own bucket so they never cancel each other's work.
- **`AppointmentReminderReconciler`** — covers the whole Person roster (a parent managing a child's specialist visit needs the alert regardless of which Person is active), filters to future / eligible appointments, and is wired into `App.build` via `appointmentReminderSyncProvider` alongside the existing `reminderSyncProvider`.
- **iOS `APPOINTMENT_REMINDER` category** (no actions) and a dedicated Android `appointment_reminders` channel so users can mute either family independently.
- **Background ACK handler** is now a double-gate on actionId + decoded med payload, so an appointment body tap is a silent no-op rather than a "dropped unrecognised payload" log.
- **Mutation invalidation** — `invalidateAppointmentsState` now also invalidates the roster-wide list so creating / moving / archiving an appointment re-reconciles the OS queue.

### Test coverage

**30 new tests (385 total, zero lints):**

- Payload round-trip + legacy-med compat, `peekReminderPayloadKind`, `AppointmentReminderPayload.tryDecode` rejecting med payloads.
- Reconciler: schedule one-per-eligible, skip no-lead, skip archived, skip past-fireAt, cancel pending-not-desired, reschedule replaces (same id), cross-Person coverage, idempotent second pass.
- Regression: the new reconciler does **not** touch pending medication reminders.

### Follow-ups (next PR)

- **Today integration** — surface the next few appointments alongside the dose list on the Today screen.
- Deep-link a body tap to the appointment's edit screen (currently just brings app to foreground).

## Test plan

- [x] `fvm flutter analyze --fatal-infos --fatal-warnings` — clean
- [x] `fvm flutter test` — 385 passing
- [ ] Manual: create an appointment 30 min from now with a 15-min lead on a physical device; confirm banner fires on time and body reads "In 15 min · <location>".
- [ ] Manual: archive the appointment before the lead; confirm the notification is cancelled.
- [ ] Manual: reschedule; confirm only one pending notification exists and it uses the new time.

Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com)

author: madfam-io
body:
## Summary

Phase 1 of the admin-vs-tenant tool audience split. Framework only — backward-compatible. No behaviour change for existing swarms; follow-up PRs tag the ~50 platform tools and wire the ContextVar into the worker.

**Why**: Today every swarm (MADFAM platform or tenant) sees the same ~259 tools. A tenant swarm could theoretically invoke \`cloudflare_create_zone\`, \`kustomize_set_image\`, \`karafiel_sat_cert_upload\` (for another tenant), \`tenant_create_identity_record\`, etc. Only the HITL ladder slows them down. This PR lays the foundation to hide platform-only tools from tenant swarms entirely.

## What this adds

- \`Audience\` enum (\`PLATFORM\` / \`TENANT\`)
- \`BaseTool.audience\` class attribute (defaults to \`TENANT\` — new tools are tenant-safe unless explicitly opted-in to PLATFORM)
- \`ToolRegistry.get_specs(audience=...)\` filter: platform swarms see all; tenant swarms see only TENANT-tagged tools
- \`ToolRegistry.list_tools(audience=...)\` mirrors the filter
- \`with_audience()\` context manager + \`get_current_audience()\` / \`enforce_audience()\` — the worker will bind the ContextVar at dispatch, tools can belt-and-braces-check in \`execute()\`
- \`can_access()\` helper for permission-engine integration

## Backward compat

- Every existing tool defaults to \`Audience.TENANT\` (the safe default)
- Every existing caller that invokes \`get_specs()\` without \`audience=\` gets the old unfiltered behaviour
- Registry load count unchanged: 258 tools both unfiltered and filtered (because nothing is tagged PLATFORM yet)
- Full tools test suite: **695/695 green** (no regressions, +21 new)

## Follow-up PRs

| PR | Scope |
|---|---|
| #2 (next) | Tag ~50 platform tools (Cloudflare, K8s, ArgoCD, Janua admin, tenant_identities, Karafiel SAT, etc.) + regression test |
| #3 | Skill-level audience (SKILL.md frontmatter + loader + 6 skill updates) |
| #4 | resolve_audience helper + thread ContextVar through worker graphs |
| #5 | Nexus-api dispatch gate (403 on audience mismatch) |
| #6 | Feature flag AUDIENCE_FILTER_ENABLED + shadow rollout + docs |

## Test plan

- [x] \`uv run pytest packages/tools/tests/test_audience.py\` → 21 passed
- [x] \`uv run pytest packages/tools/tests/\` → 695 passed (no regressions)
- [x] Ruff clean
- [x] Registry backward-compat verified: \`len(list_tools()) == len(list_tools(audience=PLATFORM)) == 258\`

author: netlify-coding[bot]
body:
🔗 **View agent run:** https://app.netlify.com/projects/newtendrwebsite/agent-runs/69e411041083cf920820ee42

🤖 **Agent:** Claude

💬 **Prompt:** update newtendrwebsite.netlify.app with latest github repository

✅ **Result:** The site's source repository was already current with the latest commit on the main branch, but the deployed version of newtendrwebsite.netlify.app did not reflect that state because the project had no committed Netlify build configuration. Any deploy triggered without those settings could silently fall back to defaults that don't match a Vite + React Router single-page app, which would leave the live site out of sync with the repository.

To make redeploys reproducible and ensure the live site picks up the latest repository content, a `netlify.toml` was added at the project root declaring the build command (`npm run build`), the publish directory (`dist`), and a catch-all SPA redirect so client-side routes such as `/book`, `/services`, and `/contact` resolve correctly instead of returning 404s. The placeholder document title in `index.html` ("My Google AI Studio App") — a leftover from the original scaffold — was also replaced with "Tendr" so the deployed page surfaces a meaningful title while the React app hydrates.

With these changes committed, the next Netlify build will use the documented settings and publish the latest repository state to the live site.

author: bokelley
body:
Closes #45.
Closes #46.

Test-only additions to `adcp/idempotency/` — no behavior changes to the production code except a godoc note on `CanonicalJSONSHA256`.

## #45 — PgBackend integration tests

`adcp/idempotency/postgres_test.go`: sqlmock-based coverage of every query path.

- `Get`: hit, miss (sql.ErrNoRows), driver error
- `PutIfAbsent`: fresh insert, conflict + reread-returns-existing, conflict + reread-empty (deleted-row race), driver error, CreatedAt auto-fill

## #46 — JCS parity vs gowebpki/jcs + large-int doc

`adcp/idempotency/canonical_parity_test.go`: two layers.

1. **Fixture table** across the RFC 8785 §3 spec surface — key ordering, ES6 number boundaries (1e-7, 1e20, 1e21, 0.000001, 0.0000001), string escapes, Unicode, AdCP-shaped payloads. All pass byte-identical with `gowebpki/jcs.Transform`.
2. **Go fuzz function** for continuous differential testing — 165k executions locally, zero divergences on valid-UTF-8 JSON.

Large-int precision documented on `CanonicalJSONSHA256`: JCS §3.2.2.3 goes through IEEE-754 double, so integers above 2^53 lose precision. This is spec-correct (gowebpki/jcs has the same behavior) but worth flagging for buyers with large numeric values.

## Dependencies

Two test-only direct imports added to `adcp/go.mod`:
- `github.com/DATA-DOG/go-sqlmock v1.5.2`
- `github.com/gowebpki/jcs v1.0.1`

Neither is imported from production code.

## Test plan

- [x] `go test -race ./adcp/idempotency/...` passes
- [x] `go test -run=nothing -fuzz=FuzzCanonicalParityVsGowebpki -fuzztime=30s` — 165k execs, no divergences
- [x] Coverage: 75.1% → 84.6%

body:
ZC1741 — `mkpasswd PASSWORD`

What: Detect `mkpasswd` (Debian whois-package) with a positional password argument, including `mkpasswd -m METHOD PASSWORD`.
Why: Cleartext password lands in argv — visible in `ps`, `/proc/<pid>/cmdline`, history, host audit logs.
Fix suggestion: Use `mkpasswd -s` and pipe the password via stdin (`printf %s "$PASSWORD" | mkpasswd -s`).
Severity: Error

author: rhyssullivan
body:
## What changed

- switched `executor call` and `executor resume` from in-process startup to daemon-first behavior via `ensureDaemon(...)`
- added a dedicated `daemon` helper module for spawn specs, URL parsing, and startup/shutdown polling
- added daemon process record persistence (`apps/cli/src/daemon-state.ts`) with pid/scope metadata under `EXECUTOR_DATA_DIR` (or `~/.executor`)
- added new CLI lifecycle commands:
  - `executor daemon status`
  - `executor daemon stop`
  - `executor daemon restart`
- made `executor daemon run` write/remove daemon ownership records
- documented the daemon commands in `README.md`
- added tests for daemon bootstrap + daemon record state

## Why this changed

Paused executions currently depend on an in-memory execution engine. If `executor call` starts the runtime in-process and exits, there is no live process left to resume from. This change makes CLI commands daemon-backed by default, so pause/resume flows can continue across command invocations.

## User and developer impact

- agents and users can run `executor call` and `executor resume` without manually booting `executor web`
- daemon lifecycle is now scriptable via status/stop/restart commands
- local ownership metadata enables safer stop/restart behavior instead of killing arbitrary reachable processes

## Root cause (fix context)

The root issue was process lifetime mismatch: short-lived CLI commands were responsible for starting execution state that must outlive those commands. Moving command execution to a persistent daemon process fixes that mismatch for local workflows.

## Validation

- `bun run --cwd apps/cli typecheck:slow`
- `bun x vitest run tests/daemon-bootstrap.test.ts tests/daemon-state.test.ts`
- manual checks:
  - `executor call --base-url http://localhost:4901 'return 41+1'` auto-started daemon and returned result
  - `executor daemon status --base-url http://localhost:4901`
  - `executor daemon restart --base-url http://localhost:4901`
  - `executor daemon stop --base-url http://localhost:4901`

author: cm5wxjmcpv-bit
body:
### Motivation

- Improve credential security by removing plaintext passwords from the UI and storing/verifying passwords with a salted hash scheme.
- Move authentication endpoints to use JSON `POST` payloads instead of GET query parameters to prevent credential leakage in URLs.
- Migrate existing stored plaintext passwords to the new hashed format on successful login to preserve compatibility.

### Description

- Added a password hashing scheme (`v1$` prefix) with salt generation, `sha256` digest helpers, `hashPassword_`, `verifyPassword_`, and migration logic in `app.js` through `validateCredentialsAndMaybeMigrate_`. 
- Switched `adminLogin` and `validateLogin` handlers to require `POST` JSON requests and added server-side handling for those actions in `doPost`; `doGet` now returns an error for login attempts via GET.
- Updated student management to store hashed passwords on `addStudent_` and to only update the stored password when a non-empty new password is provided in `updateStudent_`, and removed password exposure from `listStudents_` output.
- Updated frontend files: `admin.html` no longer displays passwords in the table and uses `POST` JSON for admin login and student edit flows (password edit is optional), and `frontend-api.js` now sends `validateLogin` as a JSON `POST` request.
- Added an audit artifact file `ELDT_AUDIT_2026-04-18.md` documenting the review scope.

### Testing

- No automated tests were present or executed for these changes.

author: benjaminduffey
body:
## Summary
The reactor mount, state machine, and audio analyser pipeline lived inside `prompt-panel.js` — wrong home for theme-pluggable plumbing and a barrier to giving HAL/Matrix/LCARS their own cores.

This PR extracts everything into a dedicated `CoreReactor` lib module and makes each theme register its own reactor markup on its `THEMES` entry.

> **Stacked on [#146](https://github.com/nicespaceship/nice/pull/146)** — base is set to that branch. Will rebase to `main` once #146 lands.

## New module
**[app/js/lib/core-reactor.js](app/js/lib/core-reactor.js)** owns:
- `mount()` — single `<div>` appended to `<body>` (position:fixed resolves to viewport).
- `paint()` — reads `Theme.getTheme(id).reactor.html()` and swaps markup. Themes without a registered reactor leave the element empty.
- `setState(s)` / `setVol(v)` — write to `<html>` data-attrs and CSS vars.
- `attachAnalyser(audio)` / `detachAnalyser()` — speech-band analyser loop + EQ canvas paint.

## Per-theme registration
JARVIS declares its reactor on its `THEMES` entry in [app/js/nice.js](app/js/nice.js):

```js
{ id:'jarvis', ...,
  reactor: { html: () => JarvisHUD.hud() + JarvisHUD.arcReactor() } }
```

`Theme.set()` calls `CoreReactor.paint()` so markup follows the active theme without a route refresh. Future themes (HAL/Matrix/LCARS) just add a `reactor:` field — no consumer changes.

## Consumer migration
[app/js/views/prompt-panel.js](app/js/views/prompt-panel.js) drops 141 lines of reactor plumbing:
- Removed: the `.jv-pp-reactor` mount block, `_setJvState`, `_setJvVol`, `_reactorAttachAnalyser`, `_reactorDetachAnalyser`, `_reactorAudioLoop`, `_renderEqBars`, `_syncReactorVisibility`, plus the 4 module-level state vars (`_ttsAnalyser`, `_ttsSrcNode`, `_ttsDataArr`, `_reactorRafId`).
- Added: `CoreReactor.init()` at mount, `CoreReactor.setState(...)` / `attachAnalyser(...)` / `detachAnalyser()` at usage sites.

## Backward compatibility
The element keeps both `.core-reactor` (new theme-agnostic hook) AND `.jv-pp-reactor` (existing JARVIS CSS) class names so `theme.css` keeps working unchanged. The class rename + `data-jv-state` → `data-core-state` migration lands in the follow-up that adds the per-theme copy/persona/voice bundle.

## Verification
- 655/655 unit tests pass
- Reactor mounts at viewport center on JARVIS theme: (640, 400) on 1280x800, (187, 406) on 375x812
- Theme switch (`Theme.set('matrix')` → `Theme.set('jarvis')`) repaints the markup correctly
- State machine writes `data-jv-state` on `<html>` as before; existing CSS rules (`[data-theme="jarvis"][data-jv-state="speaking"] ...`) keep firing
- Stack (5 commits): centering fix in #146 → CoreReactor extraction here

## Test plan
- [ ] Switch to JARVIS — reactor renders centered on every view
- [ ] Switch to a non-JARVIS theme — reactor element exists but is empty (no visual)
- [ ] Switch back to JARVIS — markup repaints, EQ + arc visible
- [ ] Send a message in JARVIS — `data-jv-state="streaming"` then `"speaking"` then `"idle"`
- [ ] TTS playback drives `--jv-vol` and the EQ canvas bars

## Follow-up PRs
- **#2B**: Extract `CoreVoice` — TTS pipeline as a lib module, voice config moves onto `THEMES[id].voice`
- **#2C**: Per-theme bundle — `copy.labels`, `copy.placeholders`, `persona.systemPrompt` move onto each `THEMES` entry; scaffold empty entries for HAL/Matrix/LCARS

author: jonahgabriel
body:
<!-- OMN-9199 ticket citation -->
Ticket: OMN-9199

## Summary

Task 3 of the HandlerResolver Architecture Phase 1 (epic **OMN-9195**, plan
`docs/plans/2026-04-18-handler-resolver-architecture.md`).

Implements the six-step precedence chain that centralizes handler
instantiation logic currently scattered across `handler_wiring.py:800-872`
(Task 5 will migrate the call site):

1. **Local ownership skip** — duck-typed `hasattr(ownership_query, "is_owned_here")`; skips cleanly when the node is not hosted here.
2. **Node registry explicit deps** — `materialized_explicit_dependencies[handler_name]` wins over container; constructs via `handler_cls(**deps)`.
3. **Container DI** — `container.get_service(handler_cls)` with narrow `except ServiceResolutionError` fall-through; any other container exception propagates untouched.
4. **Event-bus injection** — single `event_bus` constructor param.
5. **Zero-arg construction**.
6. **TypeError** — unresolvable; never returns `UNRESOLVABLE` outcome, always raises.

## Layering invariant preserved

`omnibase_core` does **not** import `omnibase_spi`. The `ownership_query`
contract is duck-typed (hasattr check), with Protocol conformance enforced
one layer up at the infra boundary in `handler_wiring.py` (Task 5).

```bash
grep -rn "omnibase_spi" src/omnibase_core/services/service_handler_resolver.py \
                       src/omnibase_core/errors/
# → zero matches
```

## Narrow exception handling

Only `ServiceResolutionError` is treated as a soft-miss fallthrough. Any
other exception raised by `container.get_service` (`KeyError`, `AttributeError`,
`RuntimeError`, unrelated `ContainerWiringError` subclasses) propagates
untouched so container-internal bugs are never masked as graceful fallback.
`test_step_3_container_internal_bug_propagates` asserts this invariant
against `KeyError`.

## Single-Class-Per-File compliance

Split the container-wiring error hierarchy across two files to satisfy the
`ONEX Single Class Per File` pre-commit gate:

- `errors/container_wiring_error.py` → `ContainerWiringError` (base)
- `errors/error_service_resolution.py` → `ServiceResolutionError` (subclass caught by resolver)

## TypeError `# error-ok:` annotations

The two `raise TypeError(...)` sites carry explicit `# error-ok:` annotations
on the line immediately preceding the raise, with rationale:

- Step 2 constructor mismatch: TypeError matches the `handler_cls(**deps)` failure mode; wrapping as OnexError obscures the signature-mismatch diagnostic.
- Step 6 unresolvable: fail-fast per OMN-8735 invariant; always a wiring bug, never a recoverable runtime state.

## Test plan

- [x] 15 unit tests covering each precedence branch + negative cases:
  - Step 1: not-owned skip / owned-fallthrough / duck-typed-missing-method
  - Step 2: explicit-deps-beat-container / incomplete-deps-surface-TypeError
  - Step 3: container-hit / container-miss-fallthrough / container-internal-bug-propagates / container-without-get_service
  - Step 4: event-bus injection
  - Step 5: zero-arg
  - Step 6: TypeError with dep names
  - Conflict overlap DEBUG log (shadowed paths)
  - Resolver purity (same context → same outcome, fresh instances)
  - Skip precedes node_registry (order)
- [x] `uv run ruff format` + `uv run ruff check` clean
- [x] `uv run mypy src/.../service_handler_resolver.py src/.../error_service_resolution.py src/.../container_wiring_error.py --strict` → "Success: no issues found"
- [x] `pre-commit run --files ...` clean on all 4 changed files
- [x] Full `uv run pytest tests/unit/services/` — 1008 passed, 42 skipped
- [x] `grep -rn "omnibase_spi" src/omnibase_core/services/service_handler_resolver.py src/omnibase_core/errors/` → 0 matches (layering invariant)
- [ ] CI green

## Stacked on

`jonah/omn-9196-resolver-models` (contains OMN-9196 resolver models + OMN-9200 ownership-query merged in).

## Out of scope

This PR does NOT:
- migrate `handler_wiring.py:800-872` to call `ServiceHandlerResolver` (Task 5 / OMN-9201)
- add the ProtocolHandlerResolver (Task 2 / OMN-9197, in omnibase_spi)
- wire the resolver into runtime boot (Task 5 cutover)
- revert OMN-9194 tactical workarounds (Task 7 / OMN-9202)

Refs: OMN-9195, OMN-8735, OMN-9196, OMN-9200

author: ooxxtaiwan
body:
Closes #21

## 摘要

PR #29 合併後，21 個 locale XAML 一個都沒跟上 `DefaultLanguage.xaml` 的 24 個新 key，且 `CREATE__SUSPENDED` typo 也只修了英文版沒修 21 個 locale。本 PR 補全所有 i18n 缺口，並順手完成多項 tech-debt 清理。

## 範圍

### 主要工作（原 Issue 21 範圍）
- 24 個 PR #29 漏譯 key → 21 locale 翻譯補齊
- `CREATE__SUSPENDED` → `CREATE_SUSPENDED` typo 修正（21 locale）
- 15 個 source code 寫死字串（MessageBox title、About panel、Error 訊息等）→ 抽到 i18n 系統
- 4 個既有 key rename 提升命名一致性：`ConfirmDel` → `ConfirmDelete`、`DebugOptions` → `AdvancedOptions`、`WithCREATESUSPENDED` → `WithCreateSuspended`（+Tip）
- `WithCreateSuspended` label 文字改良：API 常數從 UI label 移到 tooltip，label 改為 `Start process suspended (for debugging)`
- 新增 `LocaleCompletenessTests`（xUnit `[Theory]`，21 locale × 2 = 42 新 test）防未來 i18n 漂移

### 擴展範圍（執行中根據 review 判斷加入）
- **ShellExtension i18n 品質修正**（22 個 XML 檔）：
  - `Submenu` 統一為產品名 `Locale Emulator`（8 個 locale 原本翻成本地語）
  - fr typo（`Éxecuter` → `Exécuter`）、ja「汎用性」→「グローバル」、zh-TW/HK「通用」→「全域」、zh-CN「通用」→「全局」、th 用詞精確化
  - pt-BR / ind 內部 capitalization 一致性
- **編碼 normalization**：22 個 LEGUI XAML + 22 個 ShellExt XML 統一 UTF-8 **without BOM**，`.gitattributes` 文件化政策
- **locale XAML 字母序排序**：方便 grep 與手動 review
- **code review 簡化**：加 `I18n.AppName` property + `I18n.Format` helper，減少 repetition
- **AboutOriginalProject 加封存日**：`Original project (archived 2022-04)`（原作 xupefei/Locale-Emulator 確實已封存）
- **Shell Extension 保留英文**：跨 5 個 key 不翻譯（產品/技術名詞慣例，與 `AppName` 決議一致）
- **`Location` → `Region` 完整 rename（BREAKING）**：見下方說明
- **`Home directory` → `Installation directory`**：原翻譯不準，實指 LE 安裝目錄

## ⚠️ BREAKING CHANGE

**XML schema: `<Location>` → `<Region>`**

`LEProfile.Location` 欄位儲存的是 .NET CultureInfo name（如 `ja-JP`），語意對應 Microsoft Windows「Region」設定頁面。原命名「Location」在英文通用語指「物理位置」，不準確。PR #29 之後進入新大版號（3.x），趁機正名。

**影響**：舊 `LEConfig.xml` / `*.le.config` 檔的 `<Location>ja-JP</Location>` 元素在新版 LE 將無法讀取。

**遷移**：使用者可手動將 `<Location>` 改為 `<Region>`；或在新版 LEGUI 重新建立 profile。Release note 須告知（見 #16）。

## 決策討論

### Q1：Issue #21 範圍擴大（9 key → 24 key → 39 key）
- 選項：A 全補 / B 守原範圍 / C 分階段
- **結果：A**。Issue body 原列 9 個 key，實測發現 PR #29 共新增 24 個，加上抽字串共 39 個。i18n 完整性一次到位。

### Q2：翻譯品質策略
- 選項：A LLM 全翻 + 部分審 / B 只翻可審 / C 全 LLM 不審
- **結果：A（不開追蹤 issue）**。LLM 對短 UI 字串品質足夠，社群有意見直接送 PR 修訂。zh-TW/zh-CN/ja/en 經人工 review。

### Q3：AppName 抽取
- **結果：抽成 `AppName` 但所有 locale 都填 `Locale Emulator`**（產品名慣例，但允許未來改）。

### Q4：`WithCreateSuspended` label 改良
- **結果：改良為 `Start process suspended (for debugging)`**，API 常數留在 tooltip 與 commit message 供開發者 grep。

### Q5：LEProc / LECommonLibrary i18n
- **結果：不納入本 PR，另開 #30 追蹤**。LEProc 是 WinForms、無 i18n 基礎建設；需先做 WPF 遷移再 i18n，屬於獨立架構工作。

### Q6：Location → Region 是否包含 C# / XML schema
- **結果：完整 rename，接受 breaking change**。理由：進入新大版號，一次性正名；`LEProfile.Location` 值本就是 CultureInfo name，語意是 Region。

## 規格與計畫

- Spec：`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-19-issue-21-i18n-translations-design.md`（設計文件，含 per-locale glossary）
- Plan：`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-04-19-issue-21-i18n-translations.md`（實作計畫）

## Test Plan

- [x] Clean build LEGUI：0 warnings / 0 errors
- [x] LECommonLibrary.Tests：23 / 23 pass
- [x] LEGUI.Tests：68 / 68 pass（26 baseline + 42 new completeness tests）
- [x] LEProc.Tests (x86)：37 / 37 pass
- [x] 視覺 smoke（zh-TW）：About 分頁 / Shell Extension 分頁 / Profile 分頁「地區設定」顯示正確
- [x] CI 綠燈
- [ ] 其他 locale 視覺 smoke（user / 社群後續回報）

## 相關 Issue

- Closes #21（i18n 補全）
- #30（LEProc → WPF + i18n 研究，本 PR 不處理）
- #32（startup-ordering follow-up fix，本 PR 合併後另開修正 I-1）

## Follow-up

- #30：LEProc / LECommonLibrary WPF 遷移 + i18n

author: matthappens
body:
### TL;DR

Expanded the OpenAPI schema with new fields for COP accounts, USD account info, and customer field definitions.

### What changed?

- Added `bankName` as a required field to `CopAccountInfoBase`, capturing the name of the bank for COP accounts.
- Added `documentType` and `documentNumber` fields to `CopBeneficiary`, allowing identity document information (e.g., national ID, passport) to be associated with a beneficiary.
- Added `bankAccountType` (`CHECKING` or `SAVINGS`) to `UsdAccountInfoBase`, required for certain corridors such as El Salvador.
- Added `COMPANY_LEGAL_NAME` as a valid enum value to `CustomerInfoFieldName`, enabling platforms to capture a company's legal name as a customer info field.

### How to test?

- Validate that COP account creation requests require `bankName` and that the field is correctly documented in the API reference.
- Confirm that `documentType` and `documentNumber` can be submitted as part of a COP beneficiary payload.
- Test USD account creation for El Salvador corridors to verify that `bankAccountType` is accepted and enforced where required.
- Verify that `COMPANY_LEGAL_NAME` is accepted as a valid `CustomerInfoFieldName` value in relevant customer info requests.

### Why make this change?

These additions support expanded corridor requirements and compliance needs. Certain payment corridors (e.g., El Salvador) require bank account type information for USD transfers, COP beneficiaries may need identity document details for regulatory purposes, and `COMPANY_LEGAL_NAME` is needed to capture legal entity information for business customers.

author: jpdillingham
body:
It's currently possible for search responses to arrive and be processed while a search has transitioned into a terminal state and the search has been disposed, causing (harmless) exception spam in logs.

This PR adds a `ReaderWriterLockSlim` to synchronize logic that mutates state and logic that processes responses.  How it works:

1. `TryAddResponse` calls `EnterReadLock`, any number of threads concurrently
2. The desired response/file count is reached and `Complete()` is called
3. `Complete()` calls `EnterWriteLock`
4. `EnterWriteLock` blocks until all other threads have released their read locks via `ExitReadLock`
5. `Complete()` successfully acquires exclusive access over `State` and updates the state
6. Concurrent calls to `TryAddResponse` block behind `EnterReadLock`, as long as exclusive access is held by `Complete()`
7. `Complete()` releases exclusive access via `ExitWriteLock`
8. All of the threads that were waiting behind `EnterReadLock` are unblocked and see that the state no longer contains `InProgress`, and return without error or having processed the response

### Motivation
- Ensure the Telegram webhook handler builds a proper `aiogram.types.Update` object so the dispatcher receives an `Update` instance instead of a raw dict and avoids `AttributeError: 'dict' object has no attribute 'bot'`.

### Description
- Import `Update` from `aiogram.types` and replace the raw JSON passthrough with `data = await request.json()` followed by `update = Update.model_validate(data)`, then call `await bot_dispatcher.feed_update(bot, update)` so the bot is passed and the dispatcher receives a validated `Update` instance.

body: The scheduler queued follow-up rows for every platform, but the processor only had a send path for Telegram — rows for other platforms silently flipped to 'failed'. Add send paths that mirror the live-reply helpers in webhooks.js: WhatsApp Cloud API (per-user phone_number_id + access_token, with env-var fallback), Messenger Graph API, Discord channel message, Slack chat.postMessage. LINE is intentionally skipped because its reply flow uses a one-shot replyToken that can't be used for delayed messages.
